title: Two concurrent Accepts race on the one delivery clone; the loser fails with GitWrongBranch
description:
`github.deliver` drives a single shared `delivery.clone_dir` through
checkout -> apply -> commit -> push -> restore. The Accept endpoint is a
sync FastAPI route, so uvicorn runs each request in its own threadpool
thread. Nothing serialises them. Two Accepts a few seconds apart overlap
in the clone.

Observed 2026-09-02. Clone reflog:

    18:45:47  checkout: master -> agentic/irc-ircd-ratbox-2026Q3-...
    18:45:48  commit: irc/ircd-ratbox: fix build failure on DragonFly
              <- 18:45:50.93 math_arpack-ng@openmpi Accept refuses here
    18:45:53  reset: moving to HEAD          } restore_to_base
    18:45:54  checkout: ...ratbox -> master  }

bundle_review_requests rows bracket it: id=19 arpack-ng create_failed at
18:45:50.937 with

    GitWrongBranch: clone is on branch 'agentic/irc-ircd-ratbox-2026Q3-...',
    expected base_branch 'master'

and id=20 ircd-ratbox created at 18:45:54.294. The push is the slow leg
(~5s) and is the window.

The refusal is the guard working, not the bug. `prepare_clean_branch`
asserting clean+on-base is the only thing that stopped arpack-ng's diff
being committed onto ircd-ratbox's branch and force-with-lease pushed
there, silently corrupting an already-accepted PR. The bug is that a
shared mutable resource has no mutex.

Recovery today is a plain retry once the clone is idle: the finally-block
restore does run, so the clone returns to base on its own.
design:
Serialise deliveries on the clone. Candidate shapes, simplest first:

(a) module-level threading.Lock keyed by clone_dir in the git driver.
    Correct for today's deployment: one uvicorn process, no --workers.
    Smallest diff. Does not cover a second process (a CLI-driven
    delivery, or a future worker count > 1).

(b) fcntl.flock on a lockfile inside the clone, wrapping github.py's
    whole prepare -> push -> restore span, bounded wait so a hung
    delivery reports "another delivery holds the clone, retry" rather
    than blocking the request thread. Covers any process. clone_dir is
    already documented as dedicated to delivery, so it is the natural
    mutex key.

(c) queue accepts and deliver from one worker. Largest change; only
    worth it if delivery grows other shared state.

Not yet chosen -- pick the simplest that actually holds. Whichever wins,
the lock must span the restore, not just the prepare: the window that
bit us was between commit and restore.
notes:
Implemented: one module-level threading.Lock in orchestrator, held
across the whole provider.create_review_request call.

Chosen over the file lock originally sketched, on facts: deliver() has
exactly one caller (the Accept route) and uvicorn.run() is invoked
without `workers`, so every delivery is a thread in one process. A
cross-process lock would defend against a process that cannot exist
today.

Bounded wait, not blocking: anyio's default thread limiter is 40
(verified in the installed anyio), so an unbounded wait behind one hung
delivery would park request threads until the tracker stops answering.
Waits delivery.git_timeout -- an existing setting, no new knob and no
env var -- which is 60s against a measured 7s healthy delivery.

The timeout raises DeliveryError from inside deliver()'s existing try,
so a busy clone records the same create_failed row as any other
provider failure, with a message saying to retry.

Lock spans the HTTP calls too, necessarily: restore_to_base runs in
create_review_request's finally, i.e. after the PR is created, so the
clone is still on the feature branch during those calls.

Tests: tests/test_delivery_clone_lock.py (6). The last one reproduces
the incident against real git -- two deliveries started on a barrier
against one real clone -- and fails 5/5 runs with the lock removed.

Residuals, deliberately not coded for:
- If the tracker process dies mid-delivery the lock dies with it and
  the clone can be left on the feature branch. That is a crash, not a
  race; the next Accept refuses, which is the safe direction.
- If anyone adds uvicorn `workers` or a second delivering process, the
  in-process lock stops being sufficient. The assumption is stated in
  the comment above the lock.

title: the bootstrapped overlay is written to the shared checkout, then the patch job composes in a fresh worktree that does not have it
description:
Two worklist ports have failed identically in every run: the patch job
refuses before the agent is invoked, so the port cannot be fixed by the loop at
all.

  patch refused: could not compose <origin> before starting. The compose tree
  is shared across jobs, so proceeding would work against whatever the previous
  job left there. Underlying error:
  extra: {"rc": 2}

REPRODUCTIONS

Four, across two runs about eight hours apart, on exactly the two worklist
ports that have no overlay.dops in DeltaPorts:

  databases/libvalkey   run 1 and run 2
  sysutils/ucored       run 1 and run 2

Every other worklist port with an existing overlay passed this preflight. The
correlation is with "no overlay", not with load: run 2 happened with the queue
otherwise idle, after concurrent build activity had been stopped.

SEQUENCE

  1. triage runs normally and classifies the failure
  2. triage bootstraps a `type=port` header overlay (new_port) because none
     exists -- "proceeding to patch"
  3. the patch job's preflight calls materialize_dports (steps.py, "Compose
     this one origin BEFORE the agent touches anything")
  4. that returns rc=2 and the job refuses by design: "a compose that did not
     work means we do not know what is on disk"

The refusal is correct behaviour given a failed compose. The bug is that the
compose fails at all, deterministically, for a port whose overlay the harness
itself just created.

WHAT THE COMPOSE ACTUALLY SAYS

Reproduced by hand, and the two ports do not fail the same way:

  sysutils/ucored      rc=2   [fail] preflight_validate: changed=0 skipped=0
                              warnings=0 errors=1
  databases/libvalkey  rc=1   Traceback ... io.open(self, mode, buffering,
                              encoding, errors, newline)

So there is at least a validation failure and an unhandled exception behind the
same refusal, and neither reaches the operator: the message interpolates
`stderr_tail or error`, both empty, so "Underlying error:" prints nothing and
only rc survives into extra.

The bootstrapped overlay is a bare header with no ops:

  port databases/libvalkey
  type port
  reason "Step 48 bootstrap: deterministic header; patch authors the body"
  target @any

NOT THE MISLABELLING BEAD

poly-e75 / poly-jg9 cover the verdict: any harness refusal is recorded as
agent_gave_up, with no patch.md and no patch_audit.json, which reads as "the
agent tried and could not fix it". That is a separate defect from this one and
they are independently fixable:

  fix only the label  -> these ports stay permanently unfixable, honestly named
  fix only this       -> they get a real patch attempt, while provider outages
                         keep being blamed on the agent

RELATED

poly-3sq -- bootstrap overlay stubs left behind in the shared DeltaPorts
checkout when a job does not land. Same bootstrap path; these refusals are one
way a job fails to land. 38 such untracked stubs were counted in the checkout
today, and they block `dev-env update` from fast-forwarding it.
notes:
DIAGNOSIS CORRECTED 2026-09-03 by validating the description against the
code. The description's central claim -- "the compose fails at all,
deterministically, for a port whose overlay the harness itself just
created" -- is WRONG, and the two different rc values it reports were a
red herring.

Compose does not fail on these ports. Run right now, through the exact
code path the preflight uses (worker.materialize_dports, which is just
`reapply <origin>`):

    sysutils/ucored      ok=True rc=0
    databases/libvalkey  ok=True rc=0

Both succeed. Nothing about the bootstrapped header is unacceptable to
compose.

THE ACTUAL MECHANISM: the overlay is not there when the patch job looks.

  PORTS_DIR      = /work/DeltaPorts   (a SYMLINK)
  PORTS_MAIN_DIR = /work/ports-main   (the shared checkout)

  1. Triage has NO worktree. _checkout_bundle_branch_for_job has exactly
     one call site, runner.py, and it passes job_type="patch". So triage
     runs with /work/DeltaPorts -> ports-main.
  2. _ensure_overlay_or_abort writes the header with
     worker.put_file(env, "/work/DeltaPorts/ports/<origin>/overlay.dops")
     -- landing in ports-main, UNTRACKED and uncommitted.
  3. The patch job calls create_job_worktree, which does
     `git worktree add` a fresh tree from the base branch and then
     _point_ports_link repoints /work/DeltaPorts at that worktree.
  4. `git worktree add` does not carry untracked files. The overlay the
     harness just wrote is not in the new tree.
  5. materialize_dports composes a port with no overlay -> fails ->
     preflight refuses.

Verified, not inferred:
  - the ports link currently resolves to ports-main (which is exactly
    why a manual reapply succeeds and the real job does not)
  - git status in ports-main shows the bootstrapped overlays untracked:
        ?? ports/databases/libvalkey/
        ?? ports/misc/libuuid/
        ?? ports/sysutils/ucored/
  - 42 untracked stubs in that checkout now

SO poly-3sq IS THE SAME BUG, seen from the other end. The stubs are not
"left behind when a job does not land"; they are orphaned by design at
step 3 of every single bootstrap, because the writer and the consumer
look at different trees. Fixing this fixes the accumulation too.

Also corrected: the description says this reproduces on "exactly the two
worklist ports that have no overlay.dops". The population is wider --
misc/libuuid hit it tonight as a third. It is every port with no
overlay, i.e. every port the bootstrap path exists to serve.

WHY THE ORIGINAL HAND-REPRODUCTION SHOWED rc=2 AND rc=1: not
reinvestigated, and no longer load-bearing. Those runs were made before
the poly-cpd compose fix landed. The rc values in the description should
not be treated as evidence of anything.
IMPLEMENTED. The patch job now establishes its own overlay state, which
is the same principle the compose preflight already states: "each
attempt responsible for its own starting state instead of trusting an
ordering that spans two modules".

  worker.ensure_bootstrap_overlay(env, origin) -- writes the
  deterministic header if the tree PORTS_DIR points at right now has no
  overlay. Idempotent, so a no-op for every port that never needed a
  bootstrap. Called from the patch preflight between assert_port_clean
  and materialize_dports.

  worker.BOOTSTRAP_REASON / worker.read_status_type -- moved out of
  runner so triage and the preflight emit a byte-identical header from
  one source. Read through runner's existing function-level `worker`
  import; a module-level one would have been the only such import in
  that file.

DELIBERATELY BEST-EFFORT. The first cut refused the job when the
bootstrap failed, and four runner-parity tests caught it: that adds a
SECOND refusal path for a condition the compose already gates, so an
unreachable env would start failing with a different message than the
one operators know. It now records what happened
(patch_overlay_bootstrapped / patch_overlay_bootstrap_failed) and lets
the compose arbitrate. Those four tests then passed unmodified, which is
the signal the design was wrong rather than the tests.

Tests: tests/test_patch_bootstrap_overlay.py (6) plus 4 ordering tests
in test_patch_preflight_compose.py. Mutation-verified both ways --
removing the preflight call fails 3, and removing the overlay_dops guard
(so it clobbers real overlays) fails 1. Suite 2972 passed.

STILL OPEN, and unchanged by this: triage keeps writing its bootstrap
into the shared checkout, where it stays untracked and orphaned. That is
poly-3sq's accumulation (42 stubs counted now, up from 38). This fix
makes the orphan harmless rather than fatal; whether triage should stop
writing entirely is the poly-3sq decision, not this one.

NOT YET VERIFIED ON HARDWARE. The three ports that hit this tonight
(databases/libvalkey, sysutils/ucored, misc/libuuid) are the real test
and need a deploy first.
VERIFIED ON HARDWARE 2026-09-03, after deploying a41d8bb and re-raising
the three ports that hit this.

All three success criteria met:

  patch_preflight_compose_failed   0   (was 3 of 3)
  patch_overlay_bootstrapped       3   ("re-established type=port
                                        bootstrap overlay in this job's
                                        worktree")
  llm_turns on the patch job       21 / 30 / 49   (was 0 / 0 / 0)

The model had never once been invoked for any of these ports across
three prior runs. It now is.

  databases/libvalkey   agent_gave_up (never invoked) -> agent_fixed, 21 turns
  misc/libuuid          agent_gave_up (never invoked) -> agent_fixed, 30 turns
  sysutils/ucored       agent_gave_up (never invoked) -> agent_budget_exhausted, 49 turns

Both fixes carry the full artifact set -- analysis/changes.diff,
analysis/patch.md, analysis/rebuild_proof.json -- so they are real
attempts, not empty terminal states. Both are unverified and sit in
"Needs verify" for an operator.

ucored is not a regression: it got a genuine attempt and ran out of
runway at 49 turns, which is the tier budget problem measured on
devel/nspr the same night (120k funds ~1.4 attempts against a nominal
max_iterations of 4), not a failure of this fix.

Worklist moved: Needs verify 6 -> 8, Needs a decision 19 -> 17.

Two of the ports the worklist had been reporting as three failed agent
attempts each were fixable on the first real attempt.

title: a verify failure records no reason anywhere, and the bundle summary still says 'verified' when it failed
description: Verification is the only failure path in the pipeline that keeps no evidence. An operator can see THAT verify failed and never why. WHAT IS STORED POST /api/bundles//verification writes three columns: verification_status, verification_at, verification_applied_diff_sha256. There is no column for a reason, an exit code, or a log reference. `dsynth_exit` IS accepted in the request body -- documented as "optional, kept for audit" -- and is then forwarded only into the bundle_verified SSE event payload. It is never persisted, so nothing can query or render it. The endpoint docstring names the missing piece itself: "The dsynth log itself is not stored here -- Slice 3 may upload it as a bundle artifact (e.g. analysis/verification.log) via the artifact-store endpoint independently." That slice never landed. WHY THE EVIDENCE IS GONE BY THE TIME ANYONE LOOKS Two perishable copies, no durable one: - dev-env apply-and-build writes work/artifacts/apply-and-build-.log and verify-fix deletes it on success. Sampling every env after two failed verifies found none present. - dsynth's per-port log under work/dsynth/logs/ is overwritten by the next build of that origin. Establishing why devel/libunwind failed verification took an ssh session and a read of a log the next build would have destroyed. It had to be done twice. The answer -- check-sanity rejecting the port over ineffective options helpers, nothing to do with the fix under test -- was worth having: it was poly-cpd, and the loop had been patching the wrong file for five bundles because of it. A CONTRADICTION IN THE SUMMARY _bundle_summary.html renders {% if bundle.verification_at %} verified {{ bundle.verification_at }} {% endif %} verification_at is set on BOTH outcomes -- the endpoint writes it whether ok is true or false. So a failed bundle shows the red "verify failed" pill from fix_status() and, two lines away, "verified 2026-09-02T13:38:13". The wrong one looks authoritative because it carries a timestamp. SHAPE OF THE FIX - Upload the apply-and-build log as analysis/verification.log on failure. The endpoint already names the path; the artifact store already takes uploads. - Persist the exit code and a short reason next to verification_status so the bundle page can say what happened without fetching an artifact. - Gate the summary line on verification_status, not verification_at, so a failed verification stops claiming it was verified. Verification is the gate an operator accepts a fix on. It is the one place where "it failed, work out why yourself" is most expensive.

title: a dsynth_test refusal is lost when the attempt hits the turn cap, so an observed gate failure still reports agent_fixed
description:
poly-8ni gave the agent dsynth_test so it could reach the acceptance
gate. It does. The refusal is then discarded, because reporting it depends on
the model emitting a Patch Log it may never reach.

OBSERVED

devel_libunwind-20260902-124214Z, first run after poly-8ni deployed:

  turn 19  dsynth_build  rebuild_ok=true
  turn 22  dsynth_test   rebuild_ok=false   <- gate refused
  turn 23  dsynth_log
  turns 24-30  get_file / grep / list_dir   <- diagnosing the refusal
  turn 30 = max_tool_turns (patch.py)

The attempt hit the turn cap mid-investigation and never emitted a final
response. analysis/patch.md is 205 characters of mid-reasoning. The
proof-block orphan rescue in attempt_loop then lifted rebuild_ok=true from
the turn-19 dsynth_build result and synthesized

  {"rebuild_ok": true, "source": "tool_result"}

so the bundle resolved agent_fixed with no record anywhere that the gate had
refused it. Verify will refuse it again, for the same defect, with the loop's
own evidence already discarded.

WHY THE PROMPT IS NOT ENOUGH

The patch prompt asks the agent to name a gate refusal in Patch Log and stop.
That instruction can only run if the model gets a turn to write the report.
Here the gate landed at turn 22 of 30 and the refusal was ambiguous enough to
investigate -- reasonable behaviour, since the agent cannot tell immediately
whether the failure is its own. Any instruction whose execution competes with
the turn budget will be dropped exactly when the news is most interesting.

The harness does not have this problem. The dsynth_test result is in the tool
trace; nothing needs to be remembered or re-derived.

FIX DIRECTION

Record the gate outcome harness-side, next to rebuild_ok:

- track dsynth_test results in the tool loop the way rebuild_ok_seen already
  tracks dsynth_build
- carry it into the proof dict on both paths -- the model-authored proof block
  and the synthesized orphan-rescue one -- so analysis/rebuild_proof.json
  gains a gate field that is present regardless of what the model wrote
- surface it in the tool-trace summary so the next attempt's payload shows the
  gate refused, not just that a build passed

Then the prompt instruction becomes a nicety rather than the mechanism.

A prompt guard capping post-gate investigation is worth adding too, but on its
own it only narrows the window; it does not close it.

NOTE ON SCOPE

This does not change what agent_fixed means -- see poly-8ni for why requiring
a green gate is not yet safe. It makes a refusal visible to the operator and
to the next attempt.

title: patch loop proves fixes with dsynth build but acceptance gates on dsynth test, so DEVELOPER/QA defects pass the loop and fail verify
description:
The agent's success oracle and the acceptance gate run different
builds, so a bundle can be resolved agent_fixed and then fail verification for
a defect the loop had no way to observe.

MECHANISM

Patch loop: worker.dsynth_build runs `dsynth build` directly with -S -y (its
docstring says dbuild is intentionally not used). rebuild_ok comes from that
exit status, and rebuild_ok is what marks a bundle agent_fixed.

Verify gate: dev-env cli.py apply_and_build step 3 runs `dtest`, i.e.
`dsynth test`. Per helpers.py that "exercises the extra Q/A phases (stage-qa,
check-plist, the test target) AND force-rebuilds by removing any existing
package first". It also runs with DEVELOPER=1.

DragonFly's Mk/bsd.sanity.mk gates its whole DEV_ERROR block on
`.if defined(DEVELOPER)`. So a class of Makefile defects is fatal under the
gate and invisible to the loop.

FIRST CONFIRMED INSTANCE

devel/libunwind-20260902-103058Z. Patch agent: rebuild_ok=true, one attempt,
resolution agent_fixed. Verify: two runs, both `dsynth stage exit=1`, both
dying at check-sanity:

  The following options helpers are incorrectly set after bsd.port.options.mk
  and are ineffective: TESTS_CONFIGURE_OFF TESTS_CONFIGURE_ON

The underlying Makefile defect is poly-cpd (mk eval appended after the options
include) and is pre-existing -- the agent's diff only adds a static patch file
and one `file materialize` line. The build dies before the patched file is ever
compiled, so the fix was neither proved nor disproved.

WHY THE AGENT CANNOT SEE IT

No agent tool runs `dsynth test`. The 18-tool surface has dsynth_build and
dsynth_log only. The loop cannot reach the gate it is judged by, and the
verify failure is not fed back into the bundle, so a re-attempt starts from the
same blind spot and would produce the same green result.

FIX DIRECTIONS

- Set DEVELOPER=1 in the agent's dsynth_build. Cheapest; surfaces DEV_ERRORs
  during the loop. Does not cover the QA phases or the force-rebuild.
- Add a dsynth_test tool and require it as the final proof for a fix the agent
  wants to call done. Closes the gap properly; every attempt gets more
  expensive, and stage-qa/check-plist failures become the agent's problem.
- At minimum, write the verify failure back onto the bundle so a re-attempt
  sees why acceptance was refused instead of re-deriving a green build.

Worth deciding deliberately: making the loop's build identical to the gate is
not obviously right -- the cheap build is what makes iteration affordable.
Surfacing the delta may be better than closing it.

ALSO

dev-env cli.py apply_and_build's docstring says it runs `dbuild ORIGIN`; the
code runs `dtest`. Stale doc, same function.

title: A provider outage is recorded as agent_gave_up, so the verdict cannot be trusted
description:
`agent_gave_up` is recorded whether the agent gave up or the harness never
reached the model. The two are indistinguishable afterwards, and the second
case is the common one.

MEASURED 2026-09-02 across the full tracker history (136 bundles):

  resolution            with analysis/patch.md   without
  agent_fixed                    18                 0
  agent_gave_up                   3                32
  agent_budget_exhausted          1                 8

Artifact retention is NOT the explanation. agent_fixed bundles have their
patch.md on every day in the window, including the oldest (20260829). The
absence is specific to the give-up verdicts, and spans every day:
20260830 0/14, 20260831 1/9, 20260901 0/8.

A genuine give-up is a real agent output: the patch prompt asks for
`## Rebuild Status: gave-up` plus a next-step recommendation in Patch Log, and
that lands in analysis/patch.md. A bundle marked agent_gave_up with no patch.md
never got that far.

OBSERVED DIRECTLY tonight. archivers_lz4json-20260902-002241Z was marked
agent_gave_up at 03:49. Its entire history is provider rate limiting - four
patch attempts, each ending `Harness patch failed ... Error code: 429`. The
agent did real work (make_patch, get_file, dupe, edit_file, genpatch) and never
once concluded anything. Its patch.md and patch_audit.json return
`{"error": "artifact not found"}`.

WHY IT MATTERS

The resolution is the only durable record of what happened. Anything reasoning
about agent quality reads it:

- An operator triaging the queue sees "the agent gave up on lz4json" and
  concludes the port is hard. It is not; the provider was down.
- Any claim of the form "the agent fails on N% of ports" is unfounded, because
  the denominator mixes model failure with infrastructure failure.
- poly-3aa sampled the agent_fixed side and is unaffected, but the same style of
  analysis applied to the give-up side would be measuring the provider.

This is adjacent to poly-4av (a transient provider error kills the job) but it
is a different defect. poly-4av is about the job dying; this is about the
death being misattributed to the agent in the permanent record.

PROPOSED

Separate "the agent concluded it could not fix this" from "we could not run the
agent". A distinct terminal resolution for infrastructure failure - provider
error, env broken, harness crash - would do it. The evidence to decide is
already present at the point the resolution is written: a give-up that produced
no patch.md is not a give-up.

Do not backfill silently. The 32 existing rows should be treated as unknown
rather than relabelled, since the underlying cause is no longer recoverable for
most of them.
notes:
SECOND LIVE CONFIRMATION 2026-09-02 06:21.

math_xspread-20260902-043007Z resolved agent_gave_up. Its analysis/patch.md and
analysis/patch_audit.json both return {"error": "artifact not found"}. Its
history is the same as lz4json's: triage completed, then patch attempts cut off
by HTTP 429, never reaching a rebuild.

Two different ports, same night, same false verdict. Running count is 33 of 36
agent_gave_up bundles with no patch.md, against 18 of 18 agent_fixed that have
one.
SCOPE REFINEMENT 2026-09-02 06:30. Distinguishing misnamed from merely
evidence-free, so the fix targets the right rows.

  resolution               with report   without   name honest?
  agent_fixed                  18           0      yes
  agent_gave_up                 3          33      NO - asserts the agent decided
  agent_budget_exhausted        1           8      partly - budget is a harness
                                                   condition, and running out
                                                   mid-attempt explains a missing
                                                   report
  triage_failed                 0           4      yes - says triage failed, does
                                                   not claim the agent concluded
                                                   anything

The defect is specifically agent_gave_up. It is the only verdict that attributes
a decision to the model while carrying no evidence the model ever spoke. 33 of 36.

triage_failed and agent_budget_exhausted are evidence-free too, but they name a
harness condition rather than an agent judgement, so they mislead far less. They
do not need renaming; agent_gave_up does.

New data point: net-mgmt_ipv6mon-20260902-043028Z resolved triage_failed at 06:29
straight after `Harness triage failed ... Error code: 429`. Its analysis/triage.md
returns {"error": "artifact not found"}. Correctly named, and the honest contrast
with lz4json and xspread on the same night is what makes the agent_gave_up naming
indefensible.
THIRD CONFIRMATION 2026-09-02 08:27. security_libfido2-20260902-043053Z
resolved agent_gave_up after `Harness patch failed ... Error code: 429`.
analysis/patch.md returns {"error": "artifact not found"}.

Three ports in one night - archivers/lz4json, math/xspread, security/libfido2 -
all marked as the agent giving up, none of which reached the model's conclusion.
Running count 34 of 37, against 18 of 18 agent_fixed with a report.

title: Triage carries the recipe in prose, so closing the diff channel did not break the loop
description:
poly-9u2 closed the diff channel: the patch payload no longer carries a prior
attempt's changes.diff, its ops JSON, or any fenced block. Verified against the
three real prior libunwind bundles - no ```diff, no ```json, no
"mk target set", no ${REINPLACE_CMD}, no MK heredoc.

The recipe still arrives. It travels as prose, and triage is what carries it.

MEASURED on devel_libunwind-20260901-234836Z, the first run after poly-9u2
deployed. Triage's Suggested Fix reconstructs the whole fix without ever seeing
a diff:

  "two REINPLACE_CMD substitutions against ${WRKSRC}/tests/test-ptrace.c that
   insert #elif defined(__DragonFly__) branches ahead of both #error sites
   (SYSCALL case: a comment noting DragonFly uses INSTRUCTION mode and this
   branch is unreachable; Singlestep case: a ptrace(PT_STEP, ...) call
   mirroring FreeBSD's behavior), and add a post-patch target that invokes
   dfly-patch. The exact expression text is already validated in the three
   prior bundles' diffs - the patch agent should reproduce that change, not
   invent a new form."

That names the defect exactly: the comment-only SYSCALL branch is what makes
the binary hang, and post-patch invoking dfly-patch is what double-runs a
non-idempotent sed. The final sentence is reproduced verbatim from the
224859Z triage.

TWO MECHANISMS, both in dportsv3/agent/context.py.

1. PriorTriagesSection renders prior analysis/triage.md WHOLE. A prior
   triage.md contains that round's own Suggested Fix, so the recipe
   propagates triage -> triage -> patch and never touches a diff. This was a
   deliberate choice in poly-9u2 - prior triage reasoning looked like the
   record worth keeping, and fence-stripping was scoped to patch.md. The
   choice was wrong for one subsection.

2. rebuild_proof.json defeats its own relabelling. poly-9u2 retitled it
   "Rebuild Proof (compile-only)", but the JSON body still reads
   "rebuild_ok": true, and triage quoted it three times as proof the fix is
   validated - "all three with \"rebuild_ok\": true". The key name is the
   claim; the title above it does not survive being quoted.

Note what triage asserts: that the expression text "is already validated in
the three prior bundles' diffs". It no longer has those diffs. It is citing
evidence it cannot see, reconstructed from prose, and raising its confidence
on it.

PROPOSED

a. Do not render a prior triage's ## Suggested Fix. It is the one subsection
   addressed to the patch agent rather than a record of what was found. Keep
   Classification, Platform, Root Cause, Evidence, Notes.
b. Stop emitting a raw rebuild_ok key into any prompt. Render the proof as a
   compiled: yes/no line built host-side, or drop the artifact from the
   section - the same fact is already in the audit summary, labelled.
c. Consider whether patch.md's Patch Log should be summarised rather than
   quoted. It says "added two REINPLACE_CMD commands to dfly-patch target for
   test-ptrace.c, added post-patch target to invoke dfly-patch" - shape-level
   but sufficient. Lower confidence on this one: it is also the narrative
   that correctly flagged the fix was never persisting to DeltaPorts, which
   is real diagnostic value. Do a and b first and re-measure.

Related: poly-9u2 (closed the diff channel), poly-3aa (the weak oracle that
makes rebuild_ok worth quoting in the first place).

title: The patch payload offers a prior attempt's diff as a worked example, so the agent copies it
description:
The patch payload hands the agent a prior attempt's full diff under a heading
that says it succeeded. The agent copies it. The copy compiles, gets stamped
success, and becomes the next run's exemplar.

MEASURED. devel/libunwind produced five consecutive agent_fixed bundles on
2026-09-01 whose changes.diff is byte-identical:

  devel_libunwind-20260901-134302Z
  devel_libunwind-20260901-194535Z
  devel_libunwind-20260901-214812Z
  devel_libunwind-20260901-222907Z
  devel_libunwind-20260901-224859Z

Four harness changes landed between them (poly-dq5, poly-et4, poly-j83,
poly-6cj) and the last run used a different model on a different provider.
Output did not change. The tracker returns newest-first, so the three
exemplars offered to the next patch job are now 100% this fix.

The fix is wrong: it writes a comment-only __DragonFly__ branch into
test-ptrace.c's SYSCALL switch. Every case in that switch must resume the
child, so the binary compiles and hangs. It also adds
`post-patch: ${MAKE} dfly-patch`, which double-runs a non-idempotent sed
(bsd.port.mk orders 700:post-patch before 880:dfly-patch).

MECHANISM

1. runner.py:2377-2385 takes the first three bundles from
   port_bundle_history(origin). No filter on resolution, delivery, or whether
   the fix was later found wrong. Recency is the only criterion.
   Triage gets the same, capped at two (runner.py:2289-2297).

2. PriorAttemptsSection (context.py:583) renders each one into the prompt:
   - analysis/changes.diff, verbatim, in a fenced diff block, 6000 chars
     (max_diff_chars)
   - analysis/patch.md, whose required format opens with `## Rebuild Status`
     (context.py:774) and carries a `## Patch Plan (JSON)` block
   - patch_audit.json summarised to `rebuild_ok=` per attempt plus
     `last_rebuild_ok` (context.py:632-636)

3. rebuild_ok is the whole oracle and means only that dsynth compiled the
   port. attempt_loop.py:328-336 synthesises the proof from a bare tool
   result when the model never claimed it. Nothing in the pipeline can
   observe a runtime hang.

So the agent reads, under "Prior Attempts", a complete working diff directly
beneath the words Rebuild Status: success. Copying it is correct reasoning
from the evidence supplied. Kimi-k3 said so explicitly: "the exact expression
text is already validated in the two prior bundles' diffs - the patch agent
should reproduce that change, not invent a new form."

WHY IT COMPOUNDS

Attempt N copies attempt N-1. It compiles, because it compiled last time. It
is stamped success and exported as attempt N+1's exemplar. A stronger
reasoner weights the success label more heavily, not less, so better models
lock in harder.

This is why the four prior interventions missed. Playbooks are advice; the
payload carries the answer. Banning code in the triage prompt (poly-6cj) does
nothing when the diff arrives via PriorAttemptsSection instead.

PROPOSED CHANGE

Prior attempts should carry what was tried and what happened, not a copyable
recipe labelled success.

a. Drop the fenced changes.diff block from PriorAttemptsSection.
b. Close the second channel: patch.md's `## Patch Plan (JSON)` can hold the
   same ops verbatim. Dropping only changes.diff leaves it open.
c. State the inference that is free at render time: this port is being
   patched again, therefore every attempt listed below failed to resolve it,
   whatever its Rebuild Status says. The payload currently asserts the
   opposite.
d. Relabel rebuild_ok in the audit summary and the lifted Rebuild Status
   line: compiled, correctness unverified.

Keep the narrative. History is genuinely useful - it is how the 224859Z
triage spotted that the fix was absent from the tree the build ran against.
The defect is the copyable diff plus the success label, not history itself.

VALIDATION

Rerun devel/libunwind. Five runs across two models produced one output; this
changes exactly one input. Expect a different wrong fix rather than a correct
one - that is still the result we need, because we have never observed what
the agent does when it is not handed an answer.

RELATED

poly-3aa covers the weak oracle itself (rebuild_ok cannot tell a fix from a
silencing). This bead is the separate defect of re-serving that oracle's
output as a validated exemplar. Fixing this one does not need the oracle
fixed first.
notes:
IMPLEMENTED, not yet deployed. dportsv3/agent/context.py.

Both PriorAttemptsSection (patch flow) and PriorTriagesSection (triage
flow) carried the defect; the triage one was missed in the original
write-up and is where the 224859Z triage got the diff it told the patch
agent to reproduce.

- changes.diff renders through _summarize_diff: per-file name and
  +/- tally, never diff content. max_diff_chars (6000 patch / 3000
  triage) deleted - it only existed to bound a body no longer emitted.
- patch.md and the legacy patch.log render through
  _strip_fenced_blocks, which elides the ## Patch Plan (JSON) block
  carrying the ops. The legacy patch_plan.json entry is dropped
  outright - it is nothing but the recipe.
- Section headers now state that the port is failing now so no listed
  attempt left it working, and that a success status means the port
  compiled, not that the change was correct.
- rebuild_ok relabelled compiled / last_attempt_compiled everywhere it
  reaches a prompt. Titles: Files Changed, Rebuild Proof
  (compile-only), Legacy Rebuild Status (compile-only).
- Two fallback paths found in review that reopened the channel:
  _tool_trace_summary dumped 2000 raw chars of tool_trace.jsonl when no
  line parsed (tool args carry put_file/edit_file bodies), and
  rebuild_proof.json rendered uncapped though it is model-authored.
  Both bounded.
- prompts.py: ## Suggested Fix now asks for the state the file must end
  up in rather than the operation, and the clause "because that decides
  the form of the fix" is gone - it invited mechanism-picking.

VALIDATED against the real 224859Z artifacts: diff body, plan JSON and
proof JSON all absent from the rendered section.

KNOWN GAP, measured on the same render. The prose in patch.md's Patch
Log still describes the mechanism closely enough to reconstruct it:
"extended dfly-patch with two REINPLACE_CMD ops inserting #elif
defined(__DragonFly__) branches at both #error sites, and added a
post-patch hook". Stripping that would also remove the narrative this
section exists to carry - the same report is what flagged that the fix
was never persisting to DeltaPorts. Left in deliberately; the rerun
will show whether the weaker form still drives an exact copy.

Tests: tests/test_prior_attempts_are_not_exemplars.py (16 cases),
plus the two payload parity tests updated. 2920 pass.

title: Triage writes the fix and the patch agent transcribes it: nothing says triage can be wrong
description:
The patch agent is told to apply triage's Suggested Fix and not to
re-investigate, and triage is told to produce a "Concrete DeltaPorts-style
fix plan". So triage writes the change and the patch agent transcribes it.
Nothing anywhere tells the patch agent that triage can be wrong.

MEASURED 2026-09-01/02, devel/libunwind, three consecutive runs on
different bundles (134302Z, 194535Z, 214812Z). All three produced a
byte-identical fix. Its content came from triage's Suggested Fix, which
carried the literal REINPLACE_CMD lines including a comment-only branch
and a statement missing its semicolon, and ended:

  "Keep the fix in the existing overlay style (REINPLACE_CMD at
   post-patch) rather than adding a static patch file."

The third run had the corrected toolchain-autoconf playbook loaded and
triage's playbook count raised from 1 to 5, and produced the same fix, so
this is not a playbook-content problem.

THE THREE PLACES

prompts.py PATCH_SYSTEM: "Apply triage's Suggested Fix first. It's a
concrete starting hypothesis. Don't burn turns re-investigating what's
already in the Triage Summary." The one hedging word is cancelled by the
next sentence.

context.py AutomationContextSection: "Apply it first. Only explore further
if the suggested fix has already been tried (check Prior Attempts) or
doesn't work." Those are the only two exits, and neither fires for a
suggestion that builds green and is still wrong - which is exactly this
case. There is no branch for "it builds and is the wrong change".

prompts.py TRIAGE_SYSTEM: "## Suggested Fix / Concrete DeltaPorts-style
fix plan." Asked for something concrete, it emits applicable code.

Reinforcing it: every playbook is flows:[triage, patch], so triage sees
all of them, including five error-* entries carrying 14 paste-ready
REINPLACE_CMD and dops blocks. It is shown recipes and asked for a
concrete plan.

Searched for any counterweight: nothing in prompts.py, context.py or the
playbooks tells the patch agent triage may be wrong. The only
"you may disagree" line is in TRIAGE_SYSTEM, about disagreeing with an
operator - the other direction.
design:
1. PATCH_SYSTEM reframes triage as an initial investigation, not an
   instruction: it read the log and the port metadata, never opened the
   source, never touched the tree, never ran a build, and the patch agent
   can do all three. Usually right about what failed, can be wrong about
   what to do. Neither wave it away nor transcribe it - confirm its
   reading against the source, then choose the form. Saying it was wrong
   in the Patch Log is explicitly welcome.

   The anti-thrash intent is kept. The old line existed because
   exploration burned budget (net-mgmt/ipv6mon: 3.5M tokens into the turn
   cap), so the new wording still says start from it rather than from
   nothing.

2. The Automation Context gains the missing exit: explore further if it
   has been tried, if it doesn't work, or if reading the source shows it
   would be the wrong change - naming the case the build cannot report.

3. TRIAGE_SYSTEM asks for the direction in prose: which file, what must
   become true, why, and what kind of file it is, since that decides the
   form. No patch bodies, no REINPLACE_CMD, no dops ops, no ready-to-paste
   snippets, with the reason stated - triage cannot see the source or run
   a build, so anything in applicable form is copied without being
   checked. It is also told the playbook recipes are addressed to the
   patch agent: cite the pattern, do not transcribe it.

The ## Suggested Fix heading is unchanged; the runner's parsers key off
it. tests/test_triage_is_not_authoritative.py pins the contract by
substance, with whitespace collapsed so a re-wrap is not a failure.

NOT DONE: the exemplar loop. The payload still carries prior agent_fixed
results with "Rebuild Status: success" and their full diffs, so a fix that
compiles and is wrong is offered to the next run as precedent. Separate
issue; related to poly-3aa.

title: Toolchain playbooks never fire: detection reads a directory the bundle path does not materialize
description:
Every toolchain-*.md playbook - 10 of the 17 - is silently dropped from
every payload, for every port.

detect_toolchains(port_dir) reads <port_dir>/Makefile from the
filesystem. Both call sites (runner.py, in build_triage_payload and
build_patch_payload) pass `bundle_dir / "port"`. That directory is only
present when the bundle was materialized to disk, and the patch path does
not materialize it - steps.py says so outright: "Patch doesn't materialize
the bundle into a tempdir (unlike triage)". The read finds nothing and the
detector returns an empty set.

An empty set is not an error. The selector treats it as "no toolchain
context known", every toolchain-tagged entry fails its trigger, and the
payload still looks populated because the untagged entries are all still
there. The playbooks_selected activity row reported only included/skipped
counts, so there was no way to see it from the outside either.

The payload renders that very Makefile without trouble. read_bundle_text
tries bundle_dir first and then falls back to artifact_get(bundle_id,
relpath); detection had no such fallback. One reader has it, the other
does not.

MEASURED 2026-09-01, devel/libunwind bundle devel_libunwind-20260901-194535Z.
  logged: triage included=1 skipped=16 / patch included=5 skipped=12
  reproducing the selector locally, those counts match exactly
    role=triage cls=None          toolchains=[] -> 1
    role=patch  cls=compile-error toolchains=[] -> 5
  and with the tags the Makefile actually carries
    role=patch  cls=compile-error toolchains=[autoconf] -> 6
  The bundle's own port/Makefile has both:
    USES=  compiler:c11 cpe libtool pkgconfig
    GNU_CONFIGURE= yes
  Feeding it straight to the detector returns
    ['autoconf', 'c', 'libtool', 'pkg-config']
  and the same call against a missing directory returns []. The detector
  is correct; the path it is handed does not exist.

No on-disk bundle directory exists under the evidence tree at all, so this
is not specific to one port or one run.
design:
playbooks.detect_toolchains_from_makefile(text) infers the same tags from
the Makefile's text, so a caller holding bundle contents through the
artifact store can detect without a directory. Both payload builders now
try the directory first and fall back to
read_bundle_text(bundle_dir, bundle_id, "port/Makefile").

Only the Makefile signals (USES=, GNU_CONFIGURE, USE_GMAKE) are reachable
that way. The file-presence signals (configure.ac, CMakeLists.txt,
meson.build, Cargo.toml) need a source tree, and a bundle only ever
carries port/* - Makefile, distinfo, pkg-descr, pkg-plist - so nothing is
lost that a bundle could have provided.

The playbooks_selected row now names the detected toolchains, or "none".
The failure was invisible because an empty set and a genuine no-match
looked identical in telemetry; the count alone could not distinguish them.

A test asserts the directory and text paths agree, so the fallback cannot
drift into a second implementation.
notes:
toolchain-autoconf.md item 2 corrected in the same change.

It told the agent that a dops `mk target set dfly-patch` body with
REINPLACE_CMDs "is durable across upstream regenerations" while a static
dragonfly/patch-*.c "works but rots on every version bump". That is
backwards for hand-written source, and it is the direct opposite of
error-prefer-dops-over-static-patches Step 2, which says a whole-line
substitution silently no-ops when upstream edits the line while a patch
fails loudly.

It was harmless while the playbook was dead. Fixing the detection makes it
live, so it had to be corrected in the same commit rather than left to
land as newly-active wrong advice.

Rewritten to route by target kind rather than by symptom: hand-written
source (.c, .h, configure.ac, Makefile.am) takes a static patch; generated
output (configure, Makefile.in, libtool m4) takes a dops op, or better,
patch the autotools source and let it regenerate. It now points at
error-prefer-dops-over-static-patches for the full decision instead of
restating a rule that can drift out of agreement with it.

Kept general - no reference to any particular port. Item 1's REINPLACE for
config.sub/config.guess is consistent with the corrected rule (those are
vendored generated files) and was left alone. The other nine toolchain
playbooks were surveyed for the same inversion; only this one had it.
toolchain-gmake.md already says upstream patches are the durable form.

Verified after the edit: the file still parses, priority 100,
toolchains=('autoconf',), est_tokens 832, and it fires for an autoconf
port. Suite 2898 passed.

title: The bundle branch is never dropped: the drop helper does not pass drop_branch, and its success row reads a key that is never set
description:
Step 30 slice 4 states the contract plainly, in
tests/test_bundle_branch_drop_per_job.py:

  "Patch end (either outcome) -> branch is dropped (changes.diff was
   already captured at patch success; on failure the branch's state is
   moot)."

The branch is never dropped. Two bugs stacked, and the second hides the
first.

BUG 1 - the drop helper does not drop.
runner.py:3147, inside _drop_bundle_branch_for_job, whose own docstring
says "drop the bundle's branch at terminal job end":

    # Keep the branch: a bundle's convert->patch chain shares it, and a
    # later job in the chain still wants its commits. Only the worktree
    # goes.
    result = worker.destroy_job_worktree(env, bundle_id, "patch")

destroy_job_worktree's drop_branch defaults to False. The keep-the-branch
rationale was pasted from destroy_job_worktree into the drop helper and
drop_branch=True was never passed, so only the worktree is removed.

BUG 2 - the success signal reads a key that is never set.
The helper gates its "bundle_branch_dropped" activity row on
result.get("removed"). destroy_job_worktree returns dropped_branch, never
removed, so the row never fires. Neither does the failure row, because
ok is True. The operation is silent in both directions.

WHY THE TESTS STAYED GREEN.
test_drop_helper_logs_success_when_removed stubs destroy_job_worktree with
a lambda taking **kw and returning a canned {"ok": True, "removed": True}.
It pins the logging, never the argument, and supplies the "removed" key
the real worker does not.

MEASURED 2026-09-01 in env 2026Q3:
  activity rows  bundle_branch_checkout      36
                 bundle_branch_dropped        0
                 bundle_branch_drop_failed    0
  bundle branches in ports-main              70
    with commits of their own                 0
    based on a stale master                  53

Not one branch carries a commit, so the "a later job still wants its
commits" rationale is earning nothing. They are 70 stale pointers.

CONSEQUENCE, measured on devel/libunwind.
Re-running bundle devel_libunwind-20260830-160338Z reused
bundle/devel_libunwind-20260830-160338Z, still pinned at ed604d3b3b6
where it was cut on 08-30 ("branch: Created from master", one reflog
entry, zero commits). master is at 04ebd5953f3, ten commits ahead.
create_job_worktree(kind="patch") reuses an existing branch as-is - there
is no fast-forward on that path, only kind="verify" recuts with -B.
changes.diff is `git diff <base>` from inside that worktree, so it
reported the agent's real libunwind fix PLUS every file master had gained
since, as reversions:

  ports/devel/binutils/diffs/Makefile.diff        (the gcc12 unblock)
  ports/devel/gamin/overlay.dops                  (merged, PR #1574)
  ports/graphics/vulkan-loader/overlay.dops       (merged, PR #1571)
  ports/multimedia/svt-av1/{overlay.dops,patch-*} (merged, PR #1572)
  ports/www/w3m/overlay.dops                      (merged, PR #1573)
  special/Mk/diffs/@2026Q3/bsd.default-versions.mk.diff  (default to gcc12)

Recorded agent_fixed. Applying it would revert four merged PRs, the
binutils change that unblocked gcc12, and the gcc12 default.
design:
1. Pass drop_branch=True in _drop_bundle_branch_for_job and replace the
   pasted keep-the-branch comment with the slice 4 rationale. This is the
   whole fix for bug 1; the contract and the helper's name already say
   drop.

2. Gate the activity row on dropped_branch, the key destroy_job_worktree
   actually returns, so the operation stops being silent.

3. Make the test assert the argument instead of only the logging: capture
   the kwargs the stub receives and assert drop_branch is True. As written
   it also supplies a "removed" key the real worker never returns, which is
   what let bug 2 through.

Deliberately NOT rebasing or fast-forwarding a reused branch. ports-main's
master is itself moved by `dev-env update --force`, so base is not a fixed
point and a re-run's diff would depend on when the env was last updated; a
rebase that conflicts in an unattended runner stalls the job mid-operation.
Dropping at patch end makes a re-run cut a fresh branch from the current
base, which is correct by construction and needs no conflict handling.

Worth having as an independent backstop: refuse a changes.diff whose files
fall outside the bundle's own origin. It would have caught the libunwind
case loudly rather than recording agent_fixed. Tracked separately in
poly-3aa.
notes:
Implemented in the commit refs'ing this bead. Suite 2890 passed.

CORRECTION to this bead's design. I first made the drop unconditional,
matching the slice 4 docstring. That was wrong. Git history shows
test_patch_drop_keeps_the_bundle_branch ("must not delete the bundle
branch") arrived in 5cc4931, the B1 per-job-worktree change, while the
"Patch end -> branch is dropped" docstring dates from the initial import
3414779. Keeping is the newer, deliberate decision, and convert does
commit to the branch (overlay.dops creation), so dropping unconditionally
would have broken the convert->patch chain. Reverted, implemented the
conditional instead.

What landed:
- destroy_job_worktree gains drop_branch_if_unused. It asks git for
  rev-list --count base..branch and deletes only at 0, so a branch with
  commits is never touched. Skips entirely when the base cannot be
  resolved, since there is no safe answer then.
- _drop_bundle_branch_for_job passes it. drop_branch itself is still never
  passed on the patch path, so test_patch_drop_keeps_the_bundle_branch
  holds unchanged.
- Both drop helpers now gate their activity row on dropped_branch instead
  of the absent "removed".
- The two stubs that returned a canned "removed" key now return
  dropped_branch, and a new test asserts drop_branch_if_unused=True is what
  gets passed. Four worker-level tests cover empty / non-empty / no-flag /
  unknown-base.
- The stale module docstring now describes the actual contract.

Env swept: 70 empty bundle branches deleted, 0 failed, 0 remaining, none
were held by a worktree. master unchanged at 04ebd5953f3.

Not done: a stale branch that DOES carry commits is still reused as-is.
Rebasing it was considered and rejected - ports-main's master is moved by
dev-env update --force, so base is not a fixed point, and a rebase
conflict would stall an unattended job mid-operation. The changes.diff
origin guard in poly-3aa is the backstop for that case.
Third review pass on the implementation. Four more issues, all folded in
before pushing.

1. The drop signal was the bare token DROPPED, sniffed out of the shell
   chain's stdout - a chain that also runs `worktree remove` and
   `worktree prune`. `worktree prune -v` prints lines like
   "Removing worktrees/<name>: gitdir file points to non-existent
   location", so a path containing that word would have been read as a
   successful drop. Now __POLY_BRANCH_DROPPED__, with a test that feeds
   exactly that git chatter in and asserts dropped_branch stays False.

2. branch -D changed to branch -d on the conditional path. rev-list has
   already established the branch is fully merged into base, and -d makes
   git enforce that independently: if the rev-list reasoning is ever
   wrong, git refuses instead of destroying commits. -D stays on the
   explicit drop_branch path, where forcing is the point.

3. Removed a redundant `echo DROPPED` on the drop_branch path. That flag
   already determines the return value, so the echo only polluted
   stdout_tail.

4. test_patch_drop_keeps_the_bundle_branch still passed but its prose
   ("Only the worktree is disposable") no longer described what happens.
   Rewritten to say what it actually pins: the patch path never *forces*
   the branch away; whether an empty one is cleaned up is the worker's
   call.

Checked and found sound, no change needed:
  - Nothing outside worker.py/runner.py references bundle branches, and
    reconcile.py confirms the delivery diff is captured before removal,
    so no downstream consumer needs the branch after the job.
  - A failed branch delete short-circuits the && and the chain exits
    non-zero, so ok=False and the drop_failed row fires. Failure is loud.
  - A missing branch makes rev-list error, the || sets n=-1, and the
    branch is kept. No spurious deletion.
  - _resolve_bundle_base_branch runs before the worktree is removed and
    reads PORTS_MAIN_DIR, whose HEAD worktrees never move.

Still open, unchanged: convert failure is contractually supposed to drop
the branch but no call site does it, and a stale branch that carries
commits is still reused as-is.

Suite 2891 passed.

title: The regenerate-a-patch flow dead-ends: genpatch stages where install_patches never looks
description:
The sanctioned way to fix a source file is
make_extract -> make_patch -> dupe -> edit -> genpatch -> install_patches.
On the second and every later attempt in a runner process, that flow
cannot complete: genpatch stages its output where install_patches never
looks, and the WRKSRC it diffs still carries the previous attempt's
edits. The agent's only remaining move is to hand-author the patch,
which is the behaviour poly-n78 records and poly-7jw's guard now
refuses - so the attempt dead-ends with no legal path forward.

MEASURED 2026-09-01. devel/libunwind, bundle
devel_libunwind-20260901-113146Z, job
20260901-113257Z-2026Q3-devel_libunwind-970328-patch.job.
4 attempts, 251 tool calls, 4,278,456 tokens, agent_gave_up at 12:50Z.
Stack: polytropos 5f7c781, model nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b.

1. GENPATCH STAGES WHERE INSTALL_PATCHES DOES NOT LOOK

genpatch has two staging conventions. On a _WRKSRC_CACHE hit the patch
lands in WRKSRC under a WRKSRC-relative name; on a miss it lands in
/work/genpatch-out/. install_patches only ever reads
<writable>/work/genpatch-out.

_WRKSRC_CACHE is process-lifetime. reset_attempt_caches (worker.py:1261)
clears _READ_CACHE only. So the first make_extract in the runner process
populates it and every genpatch afterwards takes the cache-hit path.

Attempt 3 walks into it exactly:
  T13 genpatch                      ok, "generated patch-tests_test-ptrace.c"
  T14 get_file /work/genpatch-out/  ok=false, "no such file"
  T15 get_file <WRKSRC>/patch-...   ok - the patch is here
  T16 install_patches               FileNotFoundError: missing patches

2. WRKSRC AND THE DUPE BASELINE CARRY THE PREVIOUS ATTEMPT'S EDITS

make_extract runs `make extract`, which is a no-op once the extract
cookie exists, so a later attempt inherits whatever the earlier one
wrote. Attempt 4 read the file after make_extract and reported:

  "the upstream source already has the DragonFly support (lines 365-366
   and 378-379). The patch is no longer needed."

Those lines were attempt 1's edit. It then duped that file, so genpatch
diffed against a baseline that already contained the change. Attempt 4
worked it out at T22:

  "the .orig file doesn't have the DragonFly branches at all, but the
   current source has them in both cases (INSTRUCTION already had it,
   SYSCALL I added). The genpatch only captured one hunk."

Any patch generated this way is structurally incomplete.

3. GENPATCH-OUT IS NEVER CLEARED

/work/genpatch-out is shared by every job and nothing empties it. It
still held libunwind's malformed patch from 02:54Z nine hours later.
install_patches with patches=None installs every patch-* found there
into whichever origin is current, so one job's leftover can be
installed into an unrelated port.

4. REGRESSION IN 5f7c781: THE TRAILING-NEWLINE REJECTION

_validate_unified_diff refuses a patch that does not end with a
newline, and _reject_malformed_patch_write applies that to every
dragonfly/patch-* write. 15 of the job's 19 put_file calls and both
install_patches calls died on it:

  attempt 3 T17-T23   7 consecutive put_file, all "does not end with a newline"
  attempt 3 T26       install_patches, same
  attempt 4 T22-T28   7 more, same

The model never appended the newline; it re-sent identical 415-byte
content until the turn cap. The rule earns nothing to pay for that.
Run over all 4199 dragonfly/patch-* in DeltaPorts it flags 6, and every
one is benign: devel/jwasm and x11/xfce4-taskmanager end mid-line;
devel/readline, shells/bash, net/openslp and net/hostapd210 have a
final hunk one trailing-context line short at EOF, which patch(1)
accepts. graphics/dcp2icc's own agent_fixed patch trips both rules and
built successfully. The genuinely broken artifact (libunwind's
28-context-line hunk under an @@ -358,13 +358,16 @@ header) is caught by
the body-longer-than-declared and no-change-lines rules without it.

5. GET_FILE'S SEPARATOR IS A TAB

worker.py:550 renders f"{n:6d}\t{line}". A tab-indented line comes back
as number, TAB, then the file's own TAB, and nothing marks which is
furniture. edit_file then demands byte-exact reproduction of that
distinction. Across the job the model guessed \t\t, \t, two spaces, six
spaces, tab+six spaces, and once a literal backslash-t, before finding
the real \t + two spaces at attempt 2 T11 and succeeding immediately.
The not-found error names no bytes, so each guess costs a turn.

WHAT HELD

poly-7jw's truncation fix held. The file went 10075 -> 10070 -> 10161
-> 10166 bytes and was never truncated or emptied, and there was no
whole-file put_file on a source file.
design:
1. genpatch always stages into /work/genpatch-out, in addition to the
   WRKSRC-relative copy the cache-hit path writes. One staging location
   for install_patches to read; the canonical naming is preserved.

2. Clear /work/genpatch-out at attempt start, so one attempt's output
   cannot be installed by the next and a stale malformed file cannot
   block an unrelated port. Belongs with reset_attempt_caches, which
   attempt_loop already calls per attempt.

3. Clean the port's WRKDIR at attempt start so make_extract really
   re-extracts and dupe snapshots a pristine baseline.
   _clean_port_workdir already exists and drops the caches.

4. Drop the trailing-newline rejection from _validate_unified_diff.
   Keep no-change-lines and body-longer-than-declared; tolerate a final
   hunk short at EOF, which is the readline/bash/openslp/hostapd210/
   dcp2icc shape.

5. edit_file's not-found error returns the closest matching region of
   the file verbatim, so the tab/space distinction is readable rather
   than guessable. This is what aider's SearchReplaceNoExactMatch
   already does ("Did you mean to match some of these actual lines?").
notes:
Implemented in 7e6ce8a. Suite 2878 passed (51 cases in
tests/test_worker_edit_file.py).

1. genpatch now copies its cache-hit output into /work/genpatch-out as
   well as leaving it in WRKSRC, so install_patches can find it whichever
   staging path genpatch took.

2. reset_attempt_workspace(env, origin) added and called from
   attempt_loop at every attempt start, beside reset_attempt_caches. It
   clears patch-* from genpatch-out and runs _clean_port_workdir so
   make_extract really re-extracts and dupe snapshots a pristine
   baseline. Both stages best-effort; the result is emitted as an
   attempt_workspace_reset event. Side benefit: _clean_port_workdir
   drops _WRKSRC_CACHE, which is what made the staging path
   process-lifetime in the first place.
   patch.run now forwards origin to attempt_loop.run - it accepted the
   argument but dropped it, so the WRKDIR could not have been cleaned.

3. Trailing-newline rejection removed from _validate_unified_diff. A
   final hunk short at EOF is tolerated too, but only at EOF and only
   when the shortfall is equal on both sides (i.e. trailing context, no
   missing change line); short mid-file is still an error. Kept:
   body-longer-than-declared, no-change-lines, bad body-line prefix,
   change line past a satisfied hunk.
   Re-run over all 4199 dragonfly/patch-* in DeltaPorts: 0 rejected,
   down from 6. The libunwind artifact is still caught, now as
   'declares 13 old / 16 new ... but the body carries more (16 / 16)'.

4. edit_file returns nearest_line + nearest_text on a missed anchor,
   found by scoring whitespace-normalised lines and returning the file's
   real bytes. Tested against the exact anchor that failed on libunwind
   (two tabs vs tab + two spaces): it returns the correct
   '\t  ptrace (...' region, and a round-trip test feeds nearest_text
   straight back as old_string and the edit lands. When the region holds
   tabs the message also names the get_file separator problem.

Not done: get_file's separator is still a tab (worker.py:550). Changing
it would alter every read the model has been trained on this session;
nearest_text makes the ambiguity recoverable instead. Worth revisiting
if anchors keep missing.

Not committed by me beyond this: nothing pushed.
Re-review found three issues in the first implementation; amended into
7728159 before pushing.

1. The WRKDIR was cleaned on EVERY attempt, including the first. That is
   redundant and expensive: reset_port already runs _clean_port_workdir
   as its first stage when a patch job ends (steps.py:1296 ->
   worker.py:1992), so between jobs the WRKDIR is already pristine. The
   real gap is only BETWEEN ATTEMPTS within a job. Cleaning on attempt 1
   bought nothing and forced a full re-extract every time - painful on a
   large port. Now gated on attempt_idx > 1, with attempt_idx threaded
   from attempt_loop. genpatch-out is still cleared on every attempt: it
   is shared across jobs, cheap to clear, and nothing else sweeps it.

2. _nearest_region would return a region on a single incidental line
   match. On a 24-line window that is not a near miss, and pointing the
   model at an unrelated region is worse than staying quiet. Now requires
   best_score * 3 >= span. Verified it still fires on the libunwind
   shape (most lines right, indentation wrong) and declines a
   contrived weak match.

3. _validate_unified_diff carried a redundant hit_eof flag alongside the
   i >= len(lines) test that already implied it. Removed; the two could
   have drifted.

Suite 2882 passed (55 cases). Corpus re-checked after the amendments:
0 of 4199 rejected.
Third review pass, tracing the live codepaths rather than the diff.
Two more issues found and folded in.

4. reset_attempt_workspace dropped the materialize baseline. It calls
   _clean_port_workdir, which pops _MATERIALIZE_STATE as well as
   _WRKSRC_CACHE. That coupling is right for reset_port but wrong here:
   _MATERIALIZE_STATE tracks ports/<origin>/ against the compose tree at
   /work/artifacts/compose, and cleaning a WRKDIR under /work/obj does
   not invalidate it. dsynth_build gates on that baseline
   (worker.py:3078) and refuses with blocked_by=stale_compose when it is
   missing, so every retry would have burned a turn on a needless
   materialize_dports. Now snapshotted and restored around the clean,
   confined to this function so reset_port is untouched. Safe because
   dsynth_build still re-checks _port_subtree_hash, so a baseline that
   has genuinely gone stale is caught there.

5. The attempt_workspace_reset event reached tool_trace.jsonl but not
   the activity log: PatchEventDispatcher.__call__ appends every event
   then routes by type, and there was no branch for this one. The reset
   deletes staged patches and wipes a WRKDIR - it needs to be visible in
   the feed, which is where this whole investigation was done. Branch
   added, reporting the count cleared and whether the wrkdir clean
   succeeded.

Also checked and found sound, no change needed:
  - genpatch staging block: paths/genpatch_out/patch_path/patch_basename
    are all in scope at the insertion point.
  - origin really does reach the reset: steps.py:1187 -> patch.run ->
    attempt_loop.run -> reset_attempt_workspace.
  - CRLF patches and blank context lines both validate clean; the
    trailing \r does not trip the body-prefix check.
  - the dispatcher tolerates unknown event types without raising.

Suite 2884 passed (57 cases).

title: put_file whole-file writes truncate source files, so genpatch diffs a corrupted baseline
description:
put_file is the only write primitive the patch agent has. There is no
line-oriented edit tool - no str_replace, no replace-range. To change one
line of a source file the agent must re-emit the entire file verbatim,
and on multi-kilobyte sources it does not do that reliably.

MEASURED 2026-09-01, devel/onetbb and devel/libunwind.

  devel/onetbb, test/common/memory_usage.h (real size 6771 bytes):
    dupe memory_usage.h                       correct order
    put_file memory_usage.h (1247 bytes)      truncated 6771 -> 1247
    genpatch ok
    install_patches installed=0 FAIL          nothing to install
    put_file memory_usage.h (6771 bytes)      restored

  same job, test/common/utils_concurrency_limit.h (19229 bytes):
    put_file utils_concurrency_limit.h.patch (1133 bytes)
                                              a .patch file written INTO WRKSRC
    put_file dragonfly/patch-test_common_memory__usage.h (0 bytes)
                                              a ZERO-BYTE patch into the overlay
    put_file utils_concurrency_limit.h (47 bytes)    truncated 19229 -> 47
    put_file utils_concurrency_limit.h (19229 bytes) restored

  devel/libunwind, tests/test-ptrace.c (8017 bytes):
    put_file test-ptrace.c (730 bytes)
    put_file test-ptrace.c (0 bytes)          emptied the file

THE CHAIN

  whole-file rewrite truncates or corrupts the source
  -> genpatch diffs against a mangled baseline
  -> empty or garbage diff, install_patches installed=0 FAIL
  -> agent falls back to hand-authoring the patch file with put_file
  -> malformed hunk

The libunwind fallback patch that resulted has 28 context lines and ZERO
additions or deletions, under a header claiming @@ -358,13 +358,16 @@.
patch(1) rejects it. gcc12 produced the same class of artifact earlier
(header claimed 8 lines, body supplied 5).

RELATION TO poly-n78

  poly-n78 records the same visible symptom - hand-edited patch files -
  but its cause note attributes it to make_extract being dead (poly-cx6,
  now closed), which made dupe/genpatch physically unavailable. That is
  not this. Here make_extract works and dupe/genpatch ARE called; they
  still produce nothing usable because the file they diff has been
  corrupted by put_file first. Fixing n78's "prefer genpatch" does not
  help when genpatch's input is already wrong.

WHY IT MATTERS

  Of 13 bundles resolved on 2026-09-01, the 5 that hand-authored a
  dragonfly/patch-* file produced 4 give-ups. Every fix that landed was
  expressible as an mk / REINPLACE_CMD op - a sed expression, no file
  reproduction required. Every give-up involved trying to edit a real
  source file. devel/libunwind's one successful fix (2026-08-30) used
  REINPLACE inside `mk target set dfly-patch` for exactly this reason.

FIX DIRECTION

  Add a line-oriented edit tool: replace-range or str_replace with an
  expected-context guard, so editing a source file never requires
  re-emitting it. That removes the truncation class entirely.

  Secondary, cheap, and worth having regardless: nothing currently acts
  on the loud signals. `install_patches installed=0 FAIL` and a 0-byte
  patch file are both written and ignored. A generated patch should be
  rejected before an attempt may claim success unless its hunk counts
  match its body, it contains at least one non-context line, and it ends
  with a newline.
notes:
Implemented.

edit_file(path, old_string, new_string, expected_sha256?, replace_all?)
worker.py, registered in tools.py. Anchored replace: unique match
required, zero and ambiguous both fail rather than guess. Reuses
put_file's write guards plus the line-number check on BOTH strings, so
a numbered anchor says why instead of a bare no-match. Returns new
sha256 + a context window so confirming an edit costs no extra turn.
Non-UTF-8 is directed back to put_file base64.

install_patches hardened, both loud signals from the bead:
- empty genpatch-out now ok=False, not the old ok=True/installed=[]
- every candidate structurally validated before any copy; the batch is
  refused whole rather than half-installed

_validate_unified_diff: hunk header counts vs body, at least one +/-
line, trailing newline, body-line prefixes. Regression-tested against
the measured libunwind signature (header 13->16 over 28 context lines,
zero changes) and the gcc12 class (header claims 8, body supplies 5).

Guidance updated so the model reaches for it: prompts.py (WRKSRC edit
step, overlay.dops write loop, discipline list) and playbooks
flow-patch.md + error-dragonfly-source-patches.md. runner.py activity
summarizer prints edit_file's RESULTING size — the same signal that
made the truncations visible.

tests/test_worker_edit_file.py, 25 cases. Suite 2852 passed.

Not done, deliberately out of scope: revert_file (restore from the
.orig dupe already writes). Without it a bad write is still terminal.
Re-review found four defects in the first implementation; all fixed.

1. _validate_unified_diff over-consumed. The hunk-body loop read on to
   the next header, so a blank separator line or a trailing newline at
   EOF was folded into the hunk's tally and a VALID patch was rejected.
   Now it stops as soon as the header's own counts are satisfied.

2. That stop then under-detected: trailing body lines past the declared
   counts were never examined ('-a/+b/+c' under a header claiming 1/1
   passed). Added an explicit check for a +/- line immediately after a
   satisfied hunk.

3. edit_file wrote with a plain write_bytes. A write dying partway
   leaves a truncated file - the exact failure the tool exists to
   prevent. Now temp-file + atomic replace, mode carried over.

4. THE IMPORTANT ONE. The validation was only on install_patches, but
   that is not the path the malformed patch took. The bead says the
   agent 'falls back to hand-authoring the patch file with put_file' -
   straight into ports/<origin>/dragonfly/, never through
   install_patches, and nothing was refusing it. Added
   _reject_malformed_patch_write, wired into both put_file and
   edit_file. Scoped to dragonfly/patch-* basenames so whole-file
   'file materialize' sources under dragonfly/ are not parsed as diffs.

VALIDATED AGAINST THE REAL CORPUS. Ran the validator over all 4199
dragonfly/patch-* files in the DeltaPorts checkout: 6 flagged, every one
pre-existing and genuinely malformed, none agent-written.
  devel/readline patch-terminal.c and shells/bash patch-lib_readline_
  terminal.c - header @@ -580,7 +580,7 @@ over a 6/6 body; the closing
  context line is missing from both.
  net/openslp, net/hostapd210 - same class.
  devel/jwasm, x11/xfce4-taskmanager - file ends mid-line, no newline.
0.14% flag rate on a corpus that predates the guard, and the guard only
governs new writes, so it does not touch these.

Also corrected: the missing-newline message claimed patch(1) would
reject the hunk. patch(1) commonly tolerates it - the message now says
what the signal actually means for a freshly written patch.

Three placeholder fixtures in test_worker_guardrails.py used
'@@ -1 +1 @@' as stand-in patch content; they test the
Makefile.DragonFly authoring lock, not diff validity, so they now carry
a real one-line diff.

tests/test_worker_edit_file.py now 34 cases. Suite 2861 passed.
Fifth defect, found and fixed: replace_all had no type coercion.

It is the only boolean in the whole tool registry, and dispatch passes
LLM arguments through untouched. Models do emit the STRING "false" for
a boolean; `not "false"` is False in Python, so that would have
silently turned a single anchored replace into a whole-file one - the
opposite of what this tool is for. _as_bool now accepts real booleans
and the common string spellings and refuses anything else rather than
guessing.

Suite 2865 passed (38 cases in test_worker_edit_file.py).

put_file is NOT removed. 18 tools registered, both write primitives
present. put_file keeps its role (create a file, write base64/binary);
only its description changed, plus the malformed-patch guard on its
text path.
Follow-on: poly-dq5. The libunwind verification run for this bead
gave up, and the dominant cause was the trailing-newline rejection added
here in 5f7c781 - it blocked 15 of 19 put_file calls and both
install_patches calls across attempts 3 and 4. The truncation fix itself
held (file never truncated, no whole-file put_file on a source). The
newline rule is removed under poly-dq5.

title: patch apply writes to disk outside the FileTransaction, so a preceding mk op silently reverts it
description:
compose reports the op applied (applied=N errors=0) while the patched
content is absent from the output tree. 48 of the 84 overlays that patch
a Makefile are affected.

MECHANISM, read off the code

  engine/fsops.py    FileTransaction buffers writes in _writes: dict and
                     read_text() returns the buffered copy when present
  engine/apply.py    txn = FileTransaction(...) is created once (:262)
                     and committed once, after the op loop (:498)
  engine/apply.py    _exec_patch_apply starts with `_ = txn` (:63) and
                     shells out to patch(1) with cwd=port_root, mutating
                     the file directly on disk

So for an overlay whose ops touch the same Makefile:

  1. `mk ...` reads Makefile from disk, stages modified text in _writes
  2. `patch apply` edits Makefile on disk, transaction knows nothing
  3. txn.commit() writes the staged (pre-patch) text over the file

The patch is reverted by the commit. patch(1) exited 0, so the op row is
recorded as applied and no error or warning is emitted.

ORDER DEPENDENT, not merely co-presence

An mk op AFTER patch apply is harmless: read_text() falls through to disk
and picks up the patched content. Only an mk op that stages a write
BEFORE patch apply runs loses it.

  mk op before patch apply, patch clobbered   48
  mk op after  patch apply, survives           3
  patch apply with no mk op at all            33

REPRODUCTION, verified 2026-08-31 on @2026Q3

  devel/binutils   mk target set dfly-patch, then patch apply
                   -> composed Makefile keeps the block the diff deletes
                      (.if ARCH == x86_64 / CONFIGURE_TARGET=
                      x86_64-portbld-freebsd) and lacks the line it adds
                      (--with-lib-path=/lib:/usr/lib).
                      The dfly-patch target IS present, i.e. the mk op won.

  devel/gdb        same shape. Composed Makefile still has
                   x86_64-portbld-freebsd and still says "for FreeBSD",
                   both of which its Makefile.diff rewrites. Its five mk
                   ops all landed.

  lang/gcc13       CONTROL: patch apply with no mk op.
                   binutils@native present in the composed Makefile.

The diff is not at fault. Applying devel/binutils' Makefile.diff by hand
with compose's own command line, passing the diff to -i, exits 0 and
produces exactly the intended output:

  patch --batch --forward -V none -r - -p0 -i DIFFPATH

IMPACT

devel/binutils is the reason lang/gcc12 cannot build. Without
--with-lib-path and with CONFIGURE_TARGET left at
x86_64-portbld-freebsd, the ports ld is a FreeBSD-targeted linker and
rejects /usr/lib/libc.so with "file in wrong format", killing gcc12 at
the stage1 libgcc_s.so link. The reference DPorts tree that avalon builds
has both changes applied, which is why the same port version built there.
No change inside ports/lang/gcc12 can route around it.

FIX DIRECTIONS

Either route patch.apply through the transaction (read the subject via
txn.read_text, run patch on that text, stage_write the result), or have
it flush/invalidate the transaction's entry for any path it touches so
the commit does not overwrite it. A cheap interim guard: make the planner
reject or warn when an overlay has an mk op and a patch apply against the
same subject, since today that combination silently drops the patch.

Whatever the fix, an op whose effect does not reach the output must not
be reported as applied.
notes:
CODE RE-READ 2026-08-31. Mechanism confirmed line by line; no claim in the
description changed. Added detail and one more control.

engine/apply.py
  :262  txn = FileTransaction(dry_run=dry_run) — one per port
  :265+ ordered_ops = @any ops first, then target ops, then the rest;
        within a group, plan order = overlay.dops file order
  :498  txn.commit() sits AFTER the op loop, inside the try. Called once.
        The only other calls are txn.rollback() on error paths.
  :63   _exec_patch_apply opens with `_ = txn`, then subprocess patch(1)
        with cwd=port_root. Nothing it does is visible to the transaction.

engine/fsops.py
  read_text()  returns self._writes[path] when staged, else path.read_text()
  commit()     iterates _writes and does NamedTemporaryFile + replace(path).
               Unconditional: no mtime check, no re-read, no merge. Whatever
               is in the buffer wins.

engine/executors/mk_ops.py
  Every executor ends in txn.stage_write(path, updated), and path is always
  _resolve_path(context.port_root, None, default="Makefile") (:84 and the
  same call in each op). So mk ops can only ever collide with
  `patch apply diffs/Makefile.diff` — the conflict class is exactly Makefile.

FULL SWEEP over every patch apply op in the tree, not just Makefile ones
(subject = the diff basename, files_X.diff -> files/X):
