  patch apply ops total                                        133
    staged write to the same subject BEFORE the patch (lost)    48   all Makefile
    staged write to the same subject only AFTER  (survives)      3
    no competing staged write at all                            82

text line-* ops stage writes too, but no overlay stages one against a
subject it later patches, so pkg-plist/pkg-message patches are unaffected
today. The exposure is latent for them, not active.

THIRD CONTROL — order dependence proven empirically, devel/jna
  Its overlay runs `patch apply diffs/Makefile.diff` FIRST and
  `mk target set dfly-patch` LAST. Composed Makefile contains all three:
    S/x86_64/x86-64/ in ANT_ARCH        (patch)   present
    dragonflybsd-${ANT_ARCH}.jar        (patch)   present
    dfly-patch:                         (mk)      present
  Same two op kinds as binutils and gdb, opposite order, patch survives.
  That is the ordering claim, demonstrated rather than reasoned.

So the three cases line up exactly with the model:
  mk before patch  -> patch lost      devel/binutils, devel/gdb
  mk after  patch  -> patch kept      devel/jna
  no mk at all     -> patch kept      lang/gcc13
CAUSAL PROOF, single-variable experiment on devel/binutils itself.

The controls (jna vs binutils/gdb vs gcc13) were different ports, so they
only established correlation. This changes one variable on one port.

Took devel/binutils/overlay.dops and moved the `mk target set dfly-patch`
block from before `patch apply diffs/Makefile.diff` to after it. Nothing
else touched: same diff, same six materialize ops, same target, same
freebsd-ports tree, composed to an empty scratch dir both times.

  mk BEFORE patch apply (as committed)
    --with-lib-path                     absent
    CONFIGURE_TARGET=x86_64-portbld-freebsd   still present
    dfly-patch:                         present

  mk AFTER patch apply (reordered)
    --with-lib-path                     present
    CONFIGURE_TARGET=x86_64-portbld-freebsd   gone
    dfly-patch:                         present

Both runs reported ops=8 applied=8 errors=0.

Order is the only input that differed, so the staged-write-overwrites-
patch mechanism is established, not inferred. It also rules out the
competing explanation that the binutils diff simply fails to apply under
compose for some unrelated reason: the same diff applies cleanly in the
reordered run.

The overlay was restored to its committed content afterwards (git status
clean for that path) and the scratch trees were removed.

Practical note for whoever fixes this: reordering an overlay is a valid
per-port workaround today, but it is a trap — the correct behaviour must
not depend on op order within a dops file, and 48 overlays currently
depend on it silently.
close_reason: Fixed in b5c9c5e (engine: stop the commit from reverting a patch it never saw). patch.apply now calls txn.flush_pending() before shelling out, so the subprocess sees staged edits and commit has no stale buffer to write back. Two regression tests added; the mk-before-patch one fails without the fix reproducing the exact binutils signature. Suite 2827 green. Verified on the real tree: devel/binutils composes with --with-lib-path and without the FreeBSD CONFIGURE_TARGET, devel/gdb's patch lands, controls devel/jna and lang/gcc13 unregressed. End to end, lang/gcc12 then built SUCCESS in 00:54:22 (27 packages, 0 failed) after failing at the stage1 libgcc_s.so link at 4:27 every prior attempt.

title: An interrupted build leaves the run open, and every later build silently stops being tracked
description:
A dsynth run that does not reach hook_run_end leaves its build_runs row with
finished_at NULL. Every later build then fails to start tracking, keeps
building normally, and records nothing. The operator sees a tracker that has
simply gone quiet.

MEASURED 2026-08-31. A build was killed at 08:47 (operator stopped a batch
that had pulled a heavy dependency). Result over the next 2.5 hours:

  builds run                    9 batches, 137 ports built, 30 failures
  build_results recorded        0   (last row 08:47:01)
  runs rows created            14
  runs with a build_run_id      2
  build_runs still open         1   <- id 20, started 08:43:47

The failure surfaced only as "the last build in the tracker has no gcc12" —
a port that had in fact been built and failed twice.

MECHANISM

  db.py:73   get_active_run  -> newest build_runs row with finished_at IS NULL
  db.py:102  create_build_run -> raise ActiveBuildError(active_run)

hook_run_start POSTs /api/builds, gets 409, and disables tracking for the
whole run:

  tracking disabled for profile=2026Q3: start-build failed:
  Tracker API error (409) for POST /api/builds: {'error': 'Active build
  already exists for @2026Q3 test: run 20 (started_at=...)'}

Recovery is one command once you know: dportsv3 tracker finish-build --run 20.
Afterwards the next build recorded correctly end to end (run 21: started,
marked building, recorded result, finished).

NOT SILENT, BUT INVISIBLE

The message is logged 12 times — in /work/dsynth/logs/dportsv3-hooks.log,
INSIDE the chroot. Nothing reaches anywhere an operator looks:

  tracker.log                   0 mentions
  dsynth stdout                 nothing; the build looks normal
  tracker UI                    no banner, no stale-build warning

"tracking disabled" is also the wrong default for a data-collection tool: it
degrades to collecting nothing, quietly, for an unbounded time.

SCOPE, roughly in order of value

- Surface an open build run. The tracker knows; the UI should say so, and
  `tracker status` should report it. get_active_run already returns the row
  and its started_at, so a stale run is trivially detectable by age.
- Have the 409 reach the operator rather than only the in-chroot hook log —
  at minimum log it on the tracker side, since that is the process that
  knows the conflict exists.
- Consider auto-closing a run whose start is older than some bound, or
  offering `finish-build --stale`, so recovery does not require knowing the
  numeric run id.
- Reduce the blast radius: a build that cannot start tracking could still
  record results against a fresh run rather than disabling tracking wholesale.

Found while exercising ports for the agent; the interrupted build in question
was itself a consequence of poly-c47 / operator intervention, so this will
recur whenever a build is stopped by hand.
close_reason: Duplicate of poly-gd5 (filed 2026-08-27), which already covers the stale active build_runs row disabling tracking via the 409 from start-build. Filed without searching first; today's evidence — 137 builds / 30 failures / 0 recorded over 2.5h, the in-chroot-only logging, and the confirmed finish-build recovery — has been merged into poly-gd5.

title: A dead patch job leaves /work/DeltaPorts pointing at its worktree, so later composes read the wrong overlays
description:
`/work/DeltaPorts` in a dev-env is a SYMLINK that the agent repoints at its
per-job git worktree while patching. Nothing restores it when a job dies, so
every later compose silently reads a dead job's branch as its overlay source.

OBSERVED 2026-08-31. A patch job for devel/llvm19@lite was killed mid-flight.
Hours later:

  /work/DeltaPorts -> job-patch-devel_llvm19_lite-20260831-084657Z
  gitdir: /work/ports-main/.git/worktrees/job-patch-devel_llvm19_lite-...
  branch: bundle/devel_llvm19@lite-20260831-084657Z  @ ed604d3b3b6

  git -C /work/ports-main worktree list
    /work/ports-main                                   3dbd7cebdad [master]
    /work/job-patch-devel_llvm19_lite-20260831-084657Z ed604d3b3b6 [bundle/...]

WHY IT IS SILENT, AND WHY IT SURVIVES AN UPDATE

compose takes `--delta-root /work/DeltaPorts` (layout.py:35, PORTS_DIR), but
`dports-dev-env update` fast-forwards `/work/ports-main` (its ENV_REPOS
entry, confusingly labelled "DeltaPorts" in the output). So:

  dports-dev-env update  ->  DeltaPorts: ed604d3b3b6b -> 3dbd7cebdadb   [ports-main]
  compose --delta-root   ->  still reading ed604d3b3b6                  [dead worktree]

The update reports success and names the new commit. Nothing warns that the
path compose will actually read is a symlink somewhere else, on another
branch, at another commit.

HOW IT PRESENTS

A committed, pushed, verified DeltaPorts change simply does not appear in the
composed tree, and compose looks healthy while ignoring it:

  apply_special: changed=41 skipped=0 warnings=0 errors=0
  special/Mk: 30/30 patched
  reconcile_output: changed=1

`30/30 patched` is true of the stale source. `changed=1` is compose correctly
observing that the scratch tree matches what is already live. Every signal
says success. Two full composes were run before the cause was found; both
"succeeded" at composing the wrong input.

Repointing the symlink (`ln -sfn ports-main /work/DeltaPorts`) and recomposing
produced the expected tree immediately.

SCOPE

- Restore the symlink when a job ends, by any path — success, failure,
  abandon, kill, or runner restart. A killed job is the case that matters;
  it is exactly when nothing runs cleanup.
- Failing that, make it detectable: `dports-dev-env status` should report
  where /work/DeltaPorts actually points and on which branch, and `update`
  should refuse or warn loudly when the compose delta-root is not the repo
  it just fast-forwarded.
- Consider whether compose should record the delta-root's resolved path,
  branch and commit in its report. It has all three and prints none, which
  is why this was invisible.

Related: poly-3sq (bootstrap overlay stubs left in the shared checkout) is
the same family — job state that outlives the job. Found while landing the
GCC_DEFAULT fix for poly-c47.

title: GCC_DEFAULT is pinned to a gcc that no longer exists, so dsynth aborts the whole run
description:
The composed @2026Q3 tree asks every port that needs the default compiler
for `lang/gcc11`, which does not exist in freebsd-ports 2026Q3. dsynth
cannot probe it and aborts the ENTIRE run, not just the affected port.

REPRODUCED 2026-08-31 08:39Z, building 24 unrelated ports:

  lang/gcc11: make: chdir /work/artifacts/compose/@2026Q3/lang/gcc11:
              No such file or directory
  DPort not found: lang/gcc11
  make -V* command for lang/gcc11 failed
  4 packages failed to probe
  unable to continue, aborting

None of the 24 ports asked for gcc11. One missing dependency killed the
whole batch.

THE CHAIN, each link verified

  freebsd-ports 2026Q3   Mk/bsd.default-versions.mk:65  GCC_DEFAULT?= 14
  DeltaPorts patch       special/Mk/diffs/@2026Q3/bsd.default-versions.mk.diff
                         -GCC_DEFAULT?= 14
                         +GCC_DEFAULT?= 11
  composed tree          Mk/bsd.default-versions.mk:68   GCC_DEFAULT?= 11
  upstream lang/gcc11    absent (oldest mainline upstream is gcc12)
  composed lang/gcc11    absent
  DeltaPorts             ports/lang/gcc11/overlay.dops exists, `type port`

`type port` means "patch this upstream port". The upstream base was removed,
so there is nothing to overlay and the origin never appears in the output —
while the Mk patch keeps pointing every default-GCC consumer at it.

gcc ports actually in the composed tree: gcc gcc12 gcc12-devel gcc13
gcc13-devel gcc14 gcc14-devel gcc15 gcc15-devel gcc16 gcc16-devel
gcc17-devel gcc6-aux gcc8 gcc9 gcc9-aux. No gcc11.

NOT NEW — it has been quietly eating builds

The 2026-08-29 atril run shows the same fault as a cascade rather than an
abort:

  [XXX] lang/gcc11 lost in the ether [flags=0000000c]
  [XXX] devel/qt6-base 5 skipped due to ... lang/gcc11 ...
  [XXX] graphics/mesa-libs 2 skipped due to ... lang/gcc11 ...
  [XXX] multimedia/ffmpeg@default 4 skipped due to ... lang/gcc11 ...
  [XXX] multimedia/aom 8 skipped due to ... lang/gcc11 ...
  [XXX] graphics/libavif 2 skipped due to ... lang/gcc11 ...

That run reported 67 skipped. An unknown share of them trace to this.

SCOPE

Primary fix is in DeltaPorts, not here: point GCC_DEFAULT at a gcc that
exists in the target branch, and retire or retarget the lang/gcc11 overlay
(`removed_in @2026Q3`, or re-base onto gcc12). Whoever does it should check
Uses_qt.mk.diff too — it sets USE_GCC_VERSION=${GCC_DEFAULT}, so qt inherits
the same pin.

OPEN QUESTION FOR THIS REPO

compose already has the detection: compose_stages.py:586 raises
E_COMPOSE_STALE_OVERLAY for "type port but upstream origin is missing", and
compose_stages.py:421 downgrades it to a warning only when
prune_stale_overlays is on (it is off by default, compose.py:62).

So this SHOULD have failed compose loudly. The 2026-08-30 22:33 compose
reported no such error — preflight_validate came back errors=0. I could not
determine why from the artifacts alone; it needs a fresh compose with the
current freebsd-ports checkout to see whether the check fires now. If it
does not, the check has a hole and that is a bug here: an overlay whose base
vanished should never reach dsynth as a missing origin.
notes:
SCALE MEASURED 2026-08-31 08:51Z. Not an edge case — it blocks essentially
the whole tree.

A driver walked 118 random 8-port batches drawn from the composed tree
(~840 ports, all categories), vetting each batch's full dependency graph
via `dsynth list-only` before building:

  batches vetted                118
  skipped, unprobeable dep      105   <- all of them: DPort not found: lang/gcc11
  skipped, heavy dep             10   <- operator exclusion (rust, llvm, jdk, node)
  skipped, graph too large        2
  actually built                  1

Excluding the 12 rejected by my own filters, 105 of 106 otherwise-buildable
batches were blocked by the missing lang/gcc11 — 99%. A batch is 8 unrelated
ports, so this is not a few unlucky ports: gcc11 is a near-universal
transitive dependency through GCC_DEFAULT, and every graph containing one
default-GCC consumer is unbuildable.

Consequence for the agentic system specifically: broad port exercising is
impossible while this stands. Random building cannot reach the agent,
because the run aborts at dependency resolution and no port ever fails a
BUILD — so no dsynth hook fires and no job is enqueued. The 2026-08-29
atril run's 67 skips are the same fault seen from inside a curated set.

Workaround while the real fix is pending: vet each batch with `list-only`
and skip any graph containing an unprobeable origin. That converts a
whole-run abort into a per-batch skip, which is what let the measurement
above be taken at all, but it does not recover the ports.

FIX LANDED, BUT gcc12 ITSELF DOES NOT BUILD (2026-08-31 10:55Z).

DeltaPorts 3dbd7cebdad bumped GCC_DEFAULT 11 -> 12. Verified in the composed
tree (Mk/bsd.default-versions.mk:68, GCC_DEFAULT?= 12) and dependency
resolution is fixed: the batch that aborted this morning now scans 473
packages with lang/gcc12 in the graph and no "DPort not found".

But lang/gcc12 fails to build, twice, ~5.5 min in:

  *** This configuration is not supported in the following subdirectories:
  gmake[3]: *** [Makefile:995: libgcc_s.so] Error 1
  gmake[2]: *** [Makefile:19102: all-stage1-target-libgcc] Error 2
  gmake[1]: *** [Makefile:24839: stage1-bubble] Error 2
  gmake:    *** [Makefile:25187: bootstrap-lean] Error 2

So GCC-consuming ports are still blocked — but the failure mode is now
strictly better: they are SKIPPED with a missing dependency instead of
aborting the entire dsynth run at probe time. Batches now complete and
report, which is how 137 ports got built and 30 failures collected in the
same session.

Remaining work is therefore a port bug in lang/gcc12 on DragonFly
(libgcc_s.so in stage1), not the version pin. Worth its own bead if someone
wants to take it; deliberately not filed here to keep this one about the pin.
close_reason: Resolved. The pin itself was fixed by DeltaPorts 3dbd7cebdad (GCC_DEFAULT 11 -> 12); dependency resolution stopped aborting and batches completed again. The remaining blocker recorded here — that lang/gcc12 itself failed to build at libgcc_s.so — was not a gcc12 port bug: it was poly-bqo, where compose silently reverted devel/binutils' Makefile patch, leaving a FreeBSD-targeted ld that could not read DragonFly's libc.so. With poly-bqo fixed, lang/gcc12 builds SUCCESS in 00:54:22. That note in this bead is superseded; nothing gcc-specific remains.

title: mk eval OPTIONS_DEFAULT lands after options are computed, so the filtering silently does nothing
description:
`mk eval OPTIONS_DEFAULT "${OPTIONS_DEFAULT:N...}"` is the standard way
DeltaPorts turns options off. In a port that includes bsd.port.options.mk
or bsd.port.pre.mk partway down its Makefile, it lands too late to have
any effect, and fails silently.

MECHANISM

exec_mk_var_eval appends the assignment at the END of the port Makefile
body. Its own comment says so:

  "Append a verbatim immediate (`:=`) assignment at the end of the port
   Makefile body ... unlike `mk set` it never rewrites the upstream line
   (which would make `=` recursive)."

That is correct and deliberate for a TERMINAL-ONLY port -- one whose only
framework include is a trailing `.include <bsd.port.mk>`. The appended
line still precedes it, so options are computed afterwards and the
filtering counts.

It is wrong for a SANDWICHED port. bsd.port.options.mk computes
PORT_OPTIONS from OPTIONS_DEFAULT at the point it is included; an
assignment appended after that cannot affect a value already derived.

WORKED EXAMPLE, devel/llvm19 (composed @2026Q3):

  269: .include <bsd.port.options.mk>     <- PORT_OPTIONS computed here
  358: .include <bsd.port.pre.mk>
  687: .include <bsd.port.post.mk>

The overlay says

  reason "disable LLDB/FLANG/COMPILER_RT/OPENMP; ..."
  mk eval OPTIONS_DEFAULT "${OPTIONS_DEFAULT:NLLDB:NFLANG:NCOMPILER_RT:NOPENMP}"

which is appended near the end of the body -- after line 269. So none of
LLDB, FLANG, COMPILER_RT or OPENMP is actually disabled by it, despite
the overlay existing to do exactly that.

BLAST RADIUS

193 overlays use `mk eval OPTIONS*` (189 of them OPTIONS_DEFAULT).
Classified against their composed Makefile:

  sandwiched (filtering lands too late):  79
  terminal-only (filtering works):        96
  no composed Makefile:                   14

So on the order of 79 overlays carry option filtering that silently
does nothing. Some of those ports may build anyway -- an option can be
off for other reasons -- so 79 is the upper bound on affected ports,
not a count of broken builds.

VERIFICATION BOUNDARY -- READ BEFORE ACTING

The mechanism is inferred from exec_mk_var_eval's documented behaviour
plus the include order in the composed Makefile. It has NOT been
confirmed by evaluating PORT_OPTIONS. An attempt to do so with
`make -V PORT_OPTIONS` outside the dsynth builder jail is worthless --
it cannot open /usr/dports/Mk/bsd.port.mk and dies with
"Variable PORT_OPTIONS is undefined", which looks like a real answer
and is not. Confirm inside the jail on one sandwiched port before
changing 79 overlays.

HOW IT SURFACED

The patch agent, given an unbounded token budget (poly-w3s), diagnosed
this unaided on devel/llvm19: it noticed the filtering was landing after
PORT_OPTIONS had been computed and rewrote the overlay to place an
`OPTIONS_DEFAULT:=` earlier via `text replace-once`. Its fix was
incomplete -- it anchored on bsd.port.pre.mk (line 358) rather than
bsd.port.options.mk (line 269), so the assignment still landed 87 lines
too late and the rebuild failed identically. But the diagnosis is sound
and pre-dates the agent: this is a bug in the committed overlays.

FIX DIRECTION

There is no dops op that can place an assignment relative to a framework
include. Every mk op is position-agnostic -- var.set, var.eval,
var.unset, var.token_add/remove, var.shell, block.*, target.*. The one
exception is mk.include.ensure, which inserts "before the terminal
include" using the Makefile AST (document.nodes, IncludeNode,
_insert_before_last_include_line). So the placement machinery already
exists and is exposed for exactly one op.

Options worth weighing:
  * make mk.var.eval aware of the sandwich -- insert before the first
    options-computing include when one exists, keeping today's
    append-at-end for terminal-only ports. Fixes all 79 with no overlay
    edits, but changes the meaning of an op 193 overlays already use.
  * add an explicit placement op / modifier (e.g. before <include>) and
    migrate the affected overlays. More honest, more churn.

Either way `text replace-once` on the port Makefile -- which is what the
agent had to reach for -- should not be the answer for a recurring ports
idiom: it matches on literal text (".endif\n\n.include <bsd.port.pre.mk>")
and breaks on any upstream reformatting.
notes:
CONFIRMED IN-JAIL, and it is not only OPTIONS_DEFAULT.

devel/libunwind verify (2026-09-02) hit the same append-at-end placement on
OPTIONS_DEFINE, and the framework itself reported it from inside the dsynth
builder -- which is the confirmation the VERIFICATION BOUNDARY above asks for.

Composed Makefile:

  43: TESTS_CONFIGURE_ON= --enable-tests
  44: TESTS_CONFIGURE_OFF= --disable-tests
  45: .include <bsd.port.options.mk>
  55: OPTIONS_DEFINE:= ${OPTIONS_DEFINE} TESTS

overlay.dops declares the correct order -- mk eval OPTIONS_DEFINE first, then
the mk set helpers. Compose inverts it: mk set is written inline (before the
include), mk eval is appended at the end. So TESTS is not a known option when
bsd.port.options.mk processes helpers.

Mk/bsd.sanity.mk turns that into a fatal check-sanity error:

  The following options helpers are incorrectly set after bsd.port.options.mk
  and are ineffective: TESTS_CONFIGURE_OFF TESTS_CONFIGURE_ON

Two consequences for the fix direction above:

1. The sandwich problem is wider than OPTIONS_DEFAULT filtering. Here the
   option is never DEFINED in time, so its helpers are dead rather than its
   default being unfiltered. Any fix scoped to OPTIONS_DEFAULT would leave
   this case.
2. The mk set / mk eval split is the sharp edge: two ops written adjacently in
   one overlay land on opposite sides of a framework include. The overlay
   author cannot see that from the source.

Only visible under DEVELOPER=1, which dsynth test sets and dsynth build does
not -- see the gate-asymmetry bead. That is why this port passed the patch
loop and failed the verify gate.

title: Give a model a free-tier property that lifts the token budget
description:
The per-attempt token budget exists to bound COST. On a free endpoint
there is no cost to bound, and the budget is the only thing stopping
the patch loop from finishing. Give a configured model a property that
says spending is free, and skip the budget for it.

WHY THIS MATTERS

DeepSeek pricing moved. Roughly $3 of patch work in three days at a
handful of ports; the target is hundreds. Nemotron is free and its
triage output is good (12 of 19 triaged cleanly, correct dops proposed,
including an independent rediscovery of the C.UTF-8 locale fix). The
blocker is purely that the patch loop cannot finish inside a budget
calibrated for a different provider.

MEASURED, same harness, same tool loop, both providers, from the runner
log:

  deepseek  turns=225  cache hit 98%  mean_in=59629  mean_cached=57147
            mean_billable=  3836
  nemotron  turns= 55  cache hit 65%  mean_in=29155  mean_cached=13588
            mean_billable= 15744

DeepSeek's cache tracks the growing prompt -- in=31589 cached=31360,
later in=48728 cached=48640, 99%+ throughout. NIM caches a FIXED early
chunk that never extends: cached sat at exactly 17280 for turns 3-10
while the prompt grew, and in a controlled test sat at 8448 while the
prompt went 16243 -> 17461. Everything appended after that chunk is
re-billed on every turn.

Net: nemotron bills 4.1x more per turn on prompts half the size -- as a
fraction of prompt, 54% against 6.4%, about 8.4x. At the ASSIST tier's
120k budget DeepSeek gets ~31 turns and nemotron ~7.6. Every patch
attempt died at the cap having done sane work: the tool sequence was
env_verify -> emit_diff -> get_file -> put_file -> validate_dops ->
materialize_dports -> dsynth_build -> dsynth_log, which is correct. It
ran out of budget, not out of ideas.

Also confirmed: prompts below roughly 15k tokens never cache at all
(cached=0 across turns at ~3.5k-6k). And note the runner logs
usage.total_tokens while the cap is on billable_tokens, so logged
"205k-317k" attempts were ~120-152k billable.

SCOPE

A per-model / per-role property -- free_tier = true, or a general
properties table on the model -- that makes token spend unbounded for
that model.

The plumbing is already there and needs almost nothing:
  * tool_loop already treats max_tokens=0 as unbounded: both budget
    checks read `if max_tokens and total.billable_tokens >= cap`.
  * attempt_loop computes budget = tier.max_tokens or 0, so a 0 budget
    already flows through untouched.
  * So free_tier simply means: pass 0 instead of the tier budget.

What still bounds a runaway loop, and must keep doing so:
  * max_tool_turns, currently 30 from patch.py (attempt_loop's own
    default of 12 is overridden), and
  * tier.max_iterations, 4 at ASSIST.
Worst case per job becomes 4 x 30 turns. At ~15.7k billable/turn that
is ~1.9M tokens, free but slow -- turns took 10-30s, so an attempt can
run 5-15 minutes and a job up to about an hour. That is the accepted
trade: if we have to wait, we wait. Make it a conscious setting, not a
surprise.

OPEN QUESTION: whether 30 turns is actually enough for nemotron to
converge, given it has never been allowed to run past the budget. Worth
measuring on the first run with the toggle on, before assuming the
budget was the only obstacle.

RELATED, not required for this: a predictive budget check. The current
test fires at `billable >= cap` BEFORE the call, so one turn can
overshoot by its whole cost -- observed 119,861 -> 152,599. Harmless
once the budget is off, still worth fixing for paid models.

DO NOT let the free_tier flag disable the turn or iteration caps. Those
are the runaway protection; only the token budget goes away.
notes:
Companion to poly-4av (transient provider errors kill the job). Both
came out of the same atril run on nemotron; neither blocks the other.
Together they are what makes a free provider usable for the patch loop:
poly-4av keeps a job alive across an outage, poly-w3s lets it finish.

title: A transient provider error kills the job: no requeue, and the SDK retries for 1.5s
description:
A transient provider error kills a job outright. There is no retry above
the openai SDK's default, and the SDK's default is 1.5 seconds wide.

MEASURED, one atril run (19 build failures raised, 31 jobs). Distinct
API failures, 01:10:00-01:13:20:

  7 x 404   5 on patch, 2 on triage
  1 x 500   Internal server error
  1 x 503   Service temporarily overloaded

  -> 6 patch jobs and 3 triage jobs dead
  -> 12 patch jobs enqueued, 0 survived, 0 fixes delivered

Successful triage calls are interleaved BETWEEN the 404s, seconds
apart, same model and key. So individual requests fail while their
neighbours succeed: this is per-request routing failure, not
per-model, not request-shape, and not payload size (a 48,112-token
triage succeeded inside the window).

WHY NOTHING RETRIED

Layer 1, the SDK. We build OpenAI(api_key=..., base_url=...) with no
max_retries, so DEFAULT_MAX_RETRIES = 2 applies. _should_retry covers
408, 409, 429, >=500 and timeouts, honours Retry-After, and backs off
0.5s -> 1s capped at 8s. Total window ~1.5s. 404 is never retried.

Layer 2, the job. There is none. Any exception out of triage.run or
patch.run (the except-branches in steps.py) goes to _err(...) ->
failed/ -> DEAD, with no transient-vs-terminal distinction and no
requeue.

WHAT THE 404 IS

"404 page not found" is Go's http.NotFound default -- no route matched
-- not an application-level model error, which would be JSON. It means
"this model id is not routable right now", and it is returned
identically for:

  * a misspelled model id,
  * a correct id whose vendor prefix was stripped by the client,
  * a valid, entitled id that is temporarily unroutable.

Established locally: /v1/models lists the model; same key and second,
ultra 404s while super-120b, lightning-30b and nano-30b return 200;
8 retries over ~4 minutes of backoff did not clear it; the same model
later returned 503 "Service temporarily overloaded" with
nvcf-status: errored; and it recovered to 200 on its own about 40
minutes later with no action taken.

So there are TWO timescales, needing different remedies:
  * sub-second flap -- neighbouring requests succeed. In-call retry
    fixes this, and only this.
  * model-level outage lasting tens of minutes. Only a requeue or a
    fallback to another model survives it.

EXTERNAL CORROBORATION

  * openclaw issue 71552: their gateway stripped the "nvidia/" prefix
    (normalizeStaticProviderModelId splits on the first slash) and got
    exactly "404 page not found" with failoverReason: model_not_found.
    Same body, from a WRONG id. Independent confirmation both that the
    body cannot discriminate, and that our poly-ajd model-id fix was
    the right call -- they shipped the mirror-image fix.
    https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/71552
  * earendil-works/pi issue 6364: NIM returns 503 "ResourceExhausted:
    All workers are busy, please retry later"; their retry predicate
    did not match the substring so it reached users without backoff.
    Fix was adding it to the retryable set.
    https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/6364
  * pi's retry policy retries 429, 500, 502, 503, 504, 524 and
    excludes 404, with exponential backoff base * 2^(attempt-1). That
    is the sane default. Treating 404 as retryable is an
    NVIDIA-specific deviation and must be scoped to that provider.
  * LangChain's official NVIDIA integration validates the model at
    client init against a static registry plus the endpoint's
    /v1/models listing. Vendor-adjacent precedent for preflight.
  * NVIDIA guidance treats 503 "All workers are busy" / "Service
    temporarily overloaded" as transient overload, not quota or
    billing, and points at Retry-After and X-Error-Classification.
  * Forum reports of a BLANKET 404 on every model while /v1/models
    works are a different fault -- a personal org missing the "Public
    API Endpoints" permission. Ours is per-request with other models
    and other calls succeeding, so we are not that case.

SCOPE

(b) Requeue a transient API failure instead of killing the job.
    Mirror the confirm-backoff idiom -- _confirm_backoff_seconds /
    _next_eligible_at in the runner, min(cap, base << min(n-1, 30))
    over runner.confirm_backoff_seconds / _max_seconds. New settings
    in the same shape. _err needs to carry retryable-vs-terminal, and
    the job needs an attempt tally for the backoff to count. A
    provider outage should park the queue, not destroy it. This is
    what covers the 40-minute case.

(c) Validate the configured model once at startup against the
    provider's model list, provider-agnostic. This is what makes
    retrying a 404 safe: without it, a typo is indistinguishable from
    unroutability and would retry forever. It also catches the typo on
    providers that answer correctly, which is the commoner everyday
    error. Fail loudly at startup, not per call.

    Retryable set: 5xx, 429, timeouts, connection errors, the
    "ResourceExhausted" substring, and -- for NVIDIA only, gated
    behind (c) having passed -- a bare 404.

RELATED FINDING, worth its own bead: opencode issue 24264 reports NIM
HANGING INDEFINITELY, no error and no status, for reasoning models when
chat_template_kwargs is absent from the payload root. We only send that
key when `reasoning` is set, and the chat role never passes reasoning
at all -- so llm.chat against a nemotron model can hang until timeout
rather than fail. A 300s hang was observed here during testing.
https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/24264

DELIBERATELY NOT IN SCOPE, recorded so it is not lost:
  * Model fallback ladder (ultra -> super -> lightning). Would have
    saved this run: three sibling models were healthy throughout, and
    during the 40-minute outage only a fallback would have helped.
  * In-call retry around llm.complete. Covers the sub-second flap,
    which (b) cannot: a failure at turn 9 discards nine turns of
    context, so retrying in place is far cheaper than requeuing.
  * Setting max_retries on the SDK client from a setting. One line.
notes:
Companion to poly-w3s (free-tier token budget). Neither blocks the other.

IN-CALL RETRY LANDED. Two items move out of "deliberately not in
scope" above: the retry around llm.complete, and max_retries on the
SDK client. What promoted them was a second atril run.

MEASURED, agent queue 18:09-23:38, 11 patch jobs:

  2 success   devel/libunwind, devel/gamin
  1 killed    devel/llvm19 (terminated by hand, swept as stranded)
  8 dead      429 after exhausting the job ladder

Two provider waves: 29 x 404 at 18:xx, then 33 x 429 + 2 x 500 from
22:15 to 23:34. No Retry-After on any of them.

The requeue from (b) worked and is not what failed: all 14 triage
jobs survived the 404 wave and reached done/, where before (b) they
would have died. What killed the run is that the endpoint stayed up
throughout — 126 calls succeeded against 41 failures in the same
window, neighbours seconds apart:

  22:43:49 -> 22:45:18  bash-completion T1..T13   all OK
  22:45:20              T14                       429 -> job destroyed
  22:45:45              vulkan-loader T1          OK

So the damage was never the failure rate, it was the blast radius of
one request. A single 429 discarded 13 good turns, the worktree, and
one of five lives. graphics/jbig2dec died at T6 having already spent
96,994 billable tokens. Five of the eight died to six ISOLATED
failures spread over 50 minutes, each landing in a fresh cold attempt.

Confirmed in code: steps.py catches any exception out of patch.run and
requeues on the first one. The attempt 1/4 loop is INSIDE the harness,
so an API error blows past it — jbig2dec never reached attempt 2/4.
runner.llm_retry_max is therefore not "5 failures before requeue", it
is "5 requeues before dead", each costing a whole attempt.

WHAT LANDED

Staged backoff inside complete(), so both backends and all three call
sites (tool_loop, triage, chat) are covered with no plumbing:

  retry 1-3   3s    the flap; most 429s clear here
  retry 4-5   5s
  retry 6+   15s    last entry repeats, so it is the ceiling

Staged rather than exponential on purpose. Exponential assumes
contention grows with time; the data says otherwise — recovery came
25s later while three quarters of requests were succeeding.

The ladder is local to the call, so a success resets it: the next
request starts at 3s and cannot inherit a delay earned by an earlier
one.

Settings: llm.retry_max (6), llm.retry_backoff_schedule
("3,3,3,5,5,15"), llm.retry_total_seconds (180.0),
llm.sdk_max_retries (0).

Each ceiling answers a known opencode failure:
  #13591  a 2-week Retry-After     -> clamped to the schedule ceiling
  #21960  retries forever          -> llm.retry_max, hard
  #25041  hangs indefinitely       -> 180s wall-clock bound
  #30510  ladders multiply         -> SDK max_retries=0, asserted

The wall-clock bound is not decoration: APITimeoutError is transient,
so at a 300s request timeout six retries would sit inside one call for
35 minutes, which is #25041 rebuilt. A per-retry ceiling cannot
express that; only elapsed time can.

Retries log at WARNING ("llm: retry N/M in Xs"), so the next run can
be measured instead of guessed at.

31 tests, suite 2794 -> 2825.

CONSEQUENCE TO WATCH: under a real outage every job now spends up to
180s before requeueing, where it used to fail instantly. On a serial
runner with 8 jobs that is ~24 min a cycle. Believed correct — it
paces against an overloaded endpoint rather than hammering it — but it
is a behaviour change, not a free win.

STILL OPEN

- Model fallback ladder (ultra -> super -> lightning). Unchanged from
  above: sibling models were healthy throughout both outages.
- The per-job retry tally never resets. record_transient_failure only
  increments; nothing clears it on a successful call, so a job carries
  scars between unrelated outages. Affected 3 of the 8 deaths
  (bash-completion, vulkan-loader, libinput each arrived at the 429
  wave with lives already spent on the 404 wave). Deliberately NOT
  fixed: in-call retry should make requeues rare enough that this
  stops mattering, and leaving it tells us on the next run whether
  that is true.
- Verification needs a real atril run. The 429s only appear under load.

title: OpenAI-compat path is DeepSeek-shaped: model id mangled, thinking knob single-dialect
description:
The openai-SDK path in dportsv3/agent/llm.py was written for one
provider and has two DeepSeek-specific assumptions hardcoded in it.
Both break for any other OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Found while
evaluating NVIDIA NIM (integrate.api.nvidia.com), which offers free
nemotron models and speaks the OpenAI wire format end to end.

1. THE MODEL ID IS MANGLED. _complete_openai does
   `model.split("/", 1)[-1]` unconditionally, on the assumption that a
   slash is a litellm routing prefix to discard. True for
   "deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro"; false for NIM, where the namespace IS
   part of the id. Simulated through the real client:

     model="nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b" provider="openai"
       -> sent model = "nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b"

   which is a 404. Same for meta/llama-*, qwen/*, deepseek-ai/*.

2. THINKING CONTROL SPEAKS ONE DIALECT. _reasoning_kwargs emits either
   extra_body={"thinking": {"type": "disabled"}} or
   reasoning_effort=<level>. Nemotron uses neither -- it wants
   extra_body={"chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": false}}.
   So reasoning="none" would send a field NIM ignores and leave
   thinking ON, which is the exact cost problem poly-r1g exists to
   fix, reintroduced for the new provider.

3. NIM IS NOT REACHABLE BY NAME. _OPENAI_COMPATIBLE is a literal
   allowlist without "nvidia", and the generic api_base escape hatch
   at _use_openai_sdk only fires when the provider is "" or "openai" --
   the "nvidia/" prefix already supplies a name, so it does not.
   Workable today only by forcing llm.*.provider = "openai".

Routing through litellm instead is not a fix: litellm 1.65.0 resolves
nvidia_nim/ and keeps the namespace, but it cannot send thinking
controls for any provider, which is why the SDK path exists.

SCOPE: make both constants provider-keyed. Strip the leading segment
only when it names the resolved provider and that provider does not
use namespaced ids; dispatch the reasoning kwargs on provider. Add
nvidia to the allowlist and to _PROVIDER_API_BASE so a bare model name
works with no api_base.

NOT IN SCOPE: whether nemotron supports tool calling well enough for
the triage/patch loops. Unverified. fix-chat uses no tools and never
passes reasoning, so it is the cheap first test.
notes:
Implemented in bf5ab57. Not verified against the live endpoint yet -- no
API key on the box. Remaining before triage/patch can use nemotron:
confirm tool calling works, and whether NIM tolerates reasoning_content
echoed back on the assistant message (tool_loop.py does that for
DeepSeek's sake).

title: The 2026Q3 locale fix misses WRK_ENV, so the build phase is unchanged
description:
e268ac9a871 patched Mk/bsd.port.mk lines 995/996 (the global LANG/LC_ALL) from C.UTF-8 to C, to stop docutils' setlocale(LC_ALL, '') failing on DragonFly, which has no C.UTF-8 locale.

That fix does not reach the build.

  Mk/bsd.commands.mk:89   SETENVI?= /usr/bin/env -i
  Mk/bsd.port.mk:3359     DO_MAKE_BUILD?= ${SETENVI} ${WRK_ENV} ${MAKE_ENV} ...

Four phases run under the ISOLATED environment and therefore discard the exported globals entirely: the configure sanity check (3342), do-build (3359), do-install (3459) and do-test (3466). For those, the only locale in scope comes from WRK_ENV, which still says:

  Mk/bsd.port.mk:1607   WRK_ENV+= HOME=${WRKDIR} LANG=C.UTF-8 ...

Everything else -- fetch, extract, patch, plist generation, QA, sed_checked -- goes through plain ${SETENV} and does inherit the globals, so the existing change is doing real work; it is incomplete, not wrong.

CONFIRMED BY MEASUREMENT
x11-toolkits/pango failed again at the build phase with the identical locale.Error after the fix was composed into the tree, in a build whose top-level env showed LANG=C.

An earlier apparent success was a FALSE POSITIVE: the port had a WRKDIR left from the agent's own successful build (which used a per-port MAKE_ENV LC_ALL=C), so ninja skipped rst2man. A later full compose changed the port content -- dsynth logged DELETE-PACKAGE ... (port content changed CRC) -- invalidating that WRKDIR, and the next build actually ran rst2man and failed.

CONSEQUENCE FOR AN ALREADY-TAKEN DECISION
The pango bundle was rejected on the reasoning that the infrastructure fix superseded it. That was wrong: the agent's 'mk add MAKE_ENV "LC_ALL=C"' is correct for the real mechanism, because MAKE_ENV is expanded after WRK_ENV on line 3359 and LC_ALL outranks LANG. Note it would still not cover 3342 (no MAKE_ENV) or 3466 (TEST_ENV).

FIX
Add a hunk changing WRK_ENV's LANG=C.UTF-8 to C in special/Mk/diffs/@2026Q3/bsd.port.mk.diff, alongside the existing 995/996 change. That covers all four isolated phases for every port at once.

Re-test from a CLEAN WRKDIR; a stale one produced the false pass the first time.

title: error_signature is a constant: the fingerprint hashes errors.txt's fixed banner line
description:
Every failure in the tree fingerprints to the same value. Measured on the state DB after a 317-package build:

  distinct error_signature : 1
  distinct origins         : 19
  total bundles            : 28

All 28 carry 8724e0ed59ddb432 -- glib20's patch failure, jpeg-turbo's configure failure, rust's fetch failure, pango's locale failure, llvm13's build failure. Identical.

CAUSE
fingerprint.normalize_error() takes 'the first non-empty line' of logs/errors.txt and hashes it. But the distiller writes a fixed banner first:

  == Summary ==
  logfile: /work/dsynth/logs/devel___json-glib.log

  == First error candidates (max 60 matches) ==

so every port hashes the literal string '== Summary =='. The _PATH normalizer that would have differentiated the logfile: line is never reached, because that is line 2.

WHY IT HID
issue_key() hashes (target, origin, fingerprint), and origin differs per port, so issues stay separated and the worklist looks correct. The signature is only load-bearing where origin is NOT part of the key.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY BROKEN
1. Same-origin discrimination. devel/llvm19@default failed at configure and devel/llvm19@lite failed at build in the same run; both fingerprinted identically and collapsed into ONE issue with times_seen=2. A fix for one will be judged against occurrences of the other.
2. Branch convergence. delivery.branch_template's {signature_short} is always 8724e0ed, so the documented property 'retries against the same root cause converge on one branch' is vacuous -- convergence comes entirely from origin being in the template.
3. Anything comparing signatures to decide 'same problem or new one' is comparing a constant.

ALSO OBSERVED
lang/rust and devel/nspr produced an EMPTY logs/errors.txt (failed at fetch and patch). Per issue_key's docstring, a missing fingerprint collapses all such failures for one (target, origin) into a single fallback issue. Those are phases the distiller has no patterns for -- see poly-m8m.

FIX DIRECTION
normalize_error must skip the distiller's banner and pick the first line that is actually an error candidate, or the distiller must write the root-cause line first. Whichever, the two are coupled and the contract between them is currently unstated: normalize_error's docstring asserts 'the first non-empty line of logs/errors.txt' IS the root-cause line, and the distiller does not honour that.

A test should assert two different failures in the same origin produce different signatures -- today they do not.

title: Delivery is unreachable on a deployed host, and its default config points at the real upstream repo
description:
Phase 1 of poly-cu8: make delivery reachable on a deployed host, without
touching the config format. Scoped deliberately small so it can ship ahead of
the unification.

What is broken today, in order of severity:

1. The unconfigured default is a live GitHub config for the real upstream
   repo, not an inert placeholder.
   DPORTSV3_CONFIG_DIR is unset on a packaged install (no rc script sets it;
   the console script at pyproject.toml:48 does not either), so
   delivery/orchestrator.py:87-95 falls through to
   paths.BUNDLED_CONFIG_DIR/"delivery.toml.sample". That file exists, so
   resolve_config loads it rather than returning None. It declares
   type = "github" and repo = "DragonFlyBSD/DeltaPorts", with a clone_dir path
   that does not exist. Token resolution fails, load_delivery_config raises,
   and every bundle Accept takes the create_failed branch
   (bundle_actions.py:112-118) instead of skipped/no_config just below it.
   tracker/delivery_sync.py:196-205 swallows the same exception, so PR merge
   reconciliation silently never runs.

2. Nothing installs the delivery config. commands/deploy.py:40-47
   (OPERATOR_FILES) lists four files; delivery.toml and delivery.token are not
   among them, and there is no delivery sample under deploy/.

3. Nothing sets DPORTSV3_CONFIG_DIR for the services, so even a
   hand-placed delivery.toml would not be found.

4. The documented file mode is wrong for the process that reads it.
   delivery/config.py:26 and config/README.md say delivery.token is 0400.
   Delivery runs only in the tracker (bundle_actions.py, delivery_sync.py),
   and the tracker drops to ${polytropos_user} (polytropos_tracker:91). A
   root-owned 0400 token is unreadable by its only consumer. provider.clone_dir
   needs to be writable by that same account, and nothing checks that either —
   the failure surfaces at the first Accept.

5. resolve_config's docstring (:67-71) documents a third search tier,
   <repo-root>/config/delivery.toml, that line 95 does not implement.

6. Two resolvers disagree on the search order. paths._config_candidates
   (paths.py:108-115) tries <dir>/<name>, then <dir>/<name>.sample, then the
   bundled sample. resolve_config skips the middle tier, and when
   DPORTSV3_CONFIG_DIR is set but holds no delivery.toml it returns None
   rather than falling back.
acceptance_criteria:
- A fresh install with no operator edits performs no delivery and logs
  skipped/no_config — not create_failed, and never against a real repo name.
- deploy.py installs delivery.toml (0640, group-owned) and both rc scripts
  export DPORTSV3_CONFIG_DIR.
- delivery.token is documented as 0640 root:${polytropos_group} in
  delivery/config.py and config/README.md, and an operator following the docs
  ends with a token the tracker can read.
- provider.clone_dir is checked at service start for existence, git-ness,
  cleanliness and writability by the tracker account; a failure names the
  path and the account.
- resolve_config's docstring matches its code, and the search-order
  difference from paths._config_candidates is either removed or stated in the
  code as deliberate.
- Out of scope: the TOML unification, the schema table, any change to
  polytropos.conf beyond adding polytropos_config_dir.
notes:
Validated on hardware 2026-08-29 (DragonFly 6.5, packaged install: venv at
/usr/local/lib/polytropos, both services under rc.d).

BEFORE, installed code, DPORTSV3_CONFIG_DIR unset, as root and as the
polytropos account alike:

  DeliveryConfigError: delivery.toml: provider type 'github' requires a
  token. Set $DPORTSV3_DELIVERY_TOKEN or place it at
  $DPORTSV3_CONFIG_DIR/delivery.token.

That is the create_failed branch, confirmed firing on the real host.

AFTER:
- resolve_config -> None both with and without the config dir set.
- deploy install placed delivery.toml.sample 0640 root:polytropos, and the
  polytropos account can read it. polytropos.conf was correctly left alone;
  the rc scripts carry their own polytropos_config_dir default, so the
  wiring works without an operator edit.
- Tracker startup log:

  INFO: Waiting for application startup.
  INFO: delivery preflight: delivery is not configured; Accept will skip
        with no_config. Copy delivery.toml.sample to delivery.toml in
        /usr/local/etc/polytropos to enable it.
  INFO: Application startup complete.

  The path in that message could only come from DPORTSV3_CONFIG_DIR, so it
  proves the rc export end to end.
- Preflight against three scratch configs: local-patch with an unwritable
  outbox, github with a missing clone_dir, github with a real clean git tree
  not owned by the service account. Each produced the right error naming the
  path and the account, plus a world-readable-token warning.
- Both services restarted clean; tracker serves /agentic 200.

Two follow-up defects found by this validation and fixed (2b12dbc, 05722dc):
the preflight ran and logged nothing, because uvicorn attaches handlers only
to its own loggers and leaves root bare, so every INFO record this package
emits was dropped. That also silently swallowed the delivery-outcome lines
bundle_actions documents as "one activity row + one daemon log line per
outcome", and merge detection. The handler writes to stderr, not stdout,
because stdout is block-buffered once daemon(8) points it at a file.
close_reason:
Landed in dbced36.

resolve_config searches $DPORTSV3_DELIVERY_CONFIG then
$DPORTSV3_CONFIG_DIR/delivery.toml, and gives up. The bundled-sample tier is
gone: it was a live github config for the real upstream repo, and with
DPORTSV3_CONFIG_DIR unset (every packaged install) it turned every Accept into
create_failed. The asymmetry with paths.config_file is now stated in the code
- a policy sample is a usable default, a delivery config names one repo, one
clone and one credential.

Both rc scripts export DPORTSV3_CONFIG_DIR from polytropos_config_dir.
deploy install places delivery.toml.sample (0640, group-owned) - the template,
not the live name, so a fresh install stays inert and logs no_config.

Token documented as 0640 root:<service group> in delivery/config.py,
config/README.md, deploy/README.md and the design record; the tracker delivers
and does not run as root.

New delivery/preflight.py runs at tracker startup: config resolvable, token
mode, clone_dir exists/git/writable/clean/on-branch, outbox writable. Never
raises. delivery_sync now logs once why merge reconciliation degraded instead
of swallowing the exception.

30 tests in tests/test_delivery_config_wiring.py; suite 2643 passed.

Deviation from the plan as filed: item (d) said ship type="local-patch" in the
bundled sample. Not loading the sample at all is the better fix - the sample
stays a github template, which is what most operators want, and safety comes
from nothing auto-loading it. The deploy-side template does default to
local-patch, as a no-credential smoke test.

Not verified on hardware yet.

title: Configuration is six formats and ~67 env vars, and the delivery half is not installed at all
description:
Configuring an install means editing six files in five formats and setting
environment variables that in many cases have nowhere to be set. The delivery
half of it is not installed at all, and its unconfigured default is not inert.

--- A. The six mechanisms -------------------------------------------------

1. <prefix>/etc/polytropos.conf          sh `: ${var:=...}`, 16 settings.
                                         Sourced by both rc.d scripts
                                         (polytropos_tracker:39, polytropos_runner:44).
2. <prefix>/etc/polytropos/harness.env   sh `export`. Sourced by the runner
                                         prestart (polytropos_runner:152).
3. <prefix>/etc/polytropos/chat.env      sh `export`. Sourced by the tracker
                                         prestart (polytropos_tracker:131).
                                         19 exports across (2) and (3).
4. $DPORTSV3_CONFIG_DIR/delivery.toml    TOML.  delivery/config.py
5. $DPORTSV3_CONFIG_DIR/agentic-policy.json  JSON.  agent/policy.py, via
                                         agent/runner.py:97
6. $DPORTSV3_CONFIG_DIR/delivery.token   raw bytes.  delivery/config.py:257

(A seventh, <prefix>/etc/newsyslog.conf.d/polytropos.conf, is newsyslog's
format and not ours to choose. It is out of scope.)

Only (4) and (5) are read by Python from a file. Everything else reaches the
code as environment.

--- B. The env layer ------------------------------------------------------

71 distinct names are read from os.environ / env.get across dportsv3/ and
dev-env/: 24 DP_HARNESS_*, 26 DPORTS_DEV_*, 9 DPORTSV3_*, 9 DP_TEST_*, plus
TERM and DPORTS_DELTA_ROOT.

Five more are invisible to grep:
  - DP_HARNESS_{TRIAGE,PATCH}_REASONING are built with an f-string at
    agent/steps.py:618, so `grep DP_HARNESS_PATCH_REASONING dportsv3/` finds
    only the sample file, never the reader.
  - DP_HARNESS_CHAT_{API_KEY,API_BASE,PROVIDER} go through a local _clean()
    helper at tracker/routes/_common.py:180-182.

39 of them are read by code but appear nowhere in deploy/ or bin/ — no sample
names them, no rc script sets them. On a packaged install there is no place to
put a value. That list includes DP_HARNESS_PATCH_TIMEOUT, DP_HARNESS_POLICY,
DP_HARNESS_ATTEMPT_WINDOW_HOURS, DP_HARNESS_SIGNATURE_STICKINESS,
DP_HARNESS_BUNDLE_BACKSTOP, DP_HARNESS_MIN_ATTEMPT_BUDGET_FRACTION,
DP_HARNESS_HEALTH_CACHE_SECONDS, DP_HARNESS_DUMP_SESSION{,_CAP},
DP_ACTIVITY_LOG_MAX, DPORTSV3_GIT_TIMEOUT, DPORTSV3_DELIVERY_{CONFIG,TOKEN},
DPORTSV3_TRACKER_TARGET, and all 24 DPORTS_DEV_* knobs.

--- C. Why the rc scripts source shell files ------------------------------

Not a design choice. os.environ is the only channel any of these settings has
into Python — there is no config-file reader for anything but delivery.toml
and agentic-policy.json. The .env files exist because the values have to
become environment somehow, and `export` in a sourced file is what rc.subr
offers.

The same absence makes the scripts translate rc variables into env variables
by hand:

    polytropos_state_db      -> DPORTSV3_STATE_DB
    polytropos_artifact_root -> DPORTSV3_ARTIFACT_ROOT
    polytropos_tracker_url   -> DPORTSV3_TRACKER_URL

(polytropos_tracker:86-88, polytropos_runner:89-91). One setting, two names,
two formats, each declared in a different file.

--- D. Delivery is not installed, and its default is not inert ------------

- commands/deploy.py:40-47 (OPERATOR_FILES) installs four files. Neither
  delivery.toml nor delivery.token is among them.
- Neither rc script sets DPORTSV3_CONFIG_DIR. The packaged `dportsv3` console
  script (pyproject.toml:48) never sets it either; only bin/dportsv3:24-26
  does, and only when <checkout>/config/ exists.
- So on a packaged install DPORTSV3_CONFIG_DIR is unset, and
  delivery/orchestrator.py:87-95 falls through to
  paths.BUNDLED_CONFIG_DIR/"delivery.toml.sample". That file exists, so
  resolve_config does not return None — it loads it.
- The bundled sample is a live GitHub configuration, not a placeholder:
  type = "github", repo = "DragonFlyBSD/DeltaPorts", and
  clone_dir = a path that does not exist. Token resolution then fails and
  load_delivery_config raises DeliveryConfigError, so every bundle Accept
  takes the create_failed branch at bundle_actions.py:112-118 rather than the
  skipped/no_config branch immediately below it.
- tracker/delivery_sync.py:196-205 swallows the same exception and returns
  None, so PR merge reconciliation silently never runs either.
- The documented file mode is wrong. delivery/config.py:26 and
  config/README.md describe delivery.token as 0400. Delivery runs in the
  TRACKER (bundle_actions.py, delivery_sync.py) and never in the runner, and
  the tracker drops to ${polytropos_user} (polytropos_tracker:91). A
  root-owned 0400 token is unreadable by the only process that wants it.
  provider.clone_dir has to be writable by that same account.
- orchestrator.resolve_config's docstring (:67-71) lists a third tier,
  <repo-root>/config/delivery.toml, that the code does not implement — line 95
  uses the bundled sample instead.
- Two resolvers disagree. paths._config_candidates (paths.py:108-115) tries
  <dir>/<name>, then <dir>/<name>.sample, then the bundled sample.
  resolve_config skips the middle tier, and when DPORTSV3_CONFIG_DIR *is* set
  but holds no delivery.toml it returns None rather than falling back.

--- E. Which env vars have a reason to exist ------------------------------

Test applied: a variable earns an override only if its value is not knowable
when the config file is written.

  Bootstrap (1) — DPORTSV3_CONFIG_DIR. A config file cannot name itself.
  Stays environment by definition.

  Inter-process argument, not configuration (5) — DPORTSV3_CMD,
  DPORTS_DEV_ENV_CMD, DPORTS_DEV_TOOL_ROOT, DPORTSV3_NO_BOOTSTRAP,
  DPORTSV3_TRACKER_TARGET. A parent tells a child something about this one
  exec: bin/dportsv3:34-46 tells its children where it lives, the runner rc
  tells the agent which dev-env command to use (polytropos_runner:163), the
  dsynth hook tells the runner which target fired
  (dev-env/dports_dev_env/hooks.py:59). These are arguments spelled as
  environment; several would be better as CLI flags, but they are not config.

  Test-only (9) — DP_TEST_*. Not shipped.

  Everything else (~56) — knowable when the config is written: model names,
  timeouts, attempt caps, cache TTLs, URLs, package lists, directory paths.
  No reason to be environment at all.

Of that last group about eight are genuinely per-run and worth keeping an
override for: DP_HARNESS_DUMP_SESSION (debug), DP_HARNESS_LLM_BACKEND (the
documented escape hatch, agent/llm.py:92), DP_HARNESS_POLICY (point one run at
an alternate policy, agent/runner.py:91), DPORTS_DELTA_ROOT (already paired
with a CLI flag, paths.py:138), DPORTSV3_DELIVERY_TOKEN,
DPORTSV3_DELIVERY_CONFIG, and the two *_REASONING knobs while poly-r1g's
workaround stands.

API keys are not in that count. They are secrets: they belong in a
mode-restricted file, not in the environment and not in a 0644 TOML. The
current two-file split is right for a reason worth keeping — harness.env is
0600 root because the runner runs as root, chat.env is 0640 root:group because
the tracker does not. That split follows the two service identities, and the
tracker is documented in its own rc script as unauthenticated with an API that
can spend LLM credit, so keeping the patch key out of it is a real defence.
design:
One TOML for settings, one file per secret, one schema table in code that
generates both. Two phases: make delivery work with today's formats first,
unify second.

=== Phase 1 — delivery, in today's shape (poly child 1) ===================

No schema work, no new format. Just make the feature reachable.

  a. deploy.py OPERATOR_FILES installs delivery.toml from a sample into
     <prefix>/etc/polytropos/, mode 0640, group-owned.
  b. Both rc scripts export DPORTSV3_CONFIG_DIR, from a polytropos_config_dir
     knob in polytropos.conf.
  c. delivery.token documented as 0640 root:${polytropos_group}, not 0400 —
     the tracker is the reader. Fix delivery/config.py:26 and
     config/README.md.
  d. The shipped sample defaults to type = "local-patch", so an unconfigured
     install is inert instead of raising create_failed against the real
     upstream repo on every Accept.
  e. resolve_config's docstring corrected, and the resolver asymmetry with
     paths._config_candidates settled deliberately — either reuse
     paths.config_file or say in the code why not.
  f. A health check for provider.clone_dir: exists, is a git work tree, clean,
     writable by the tracker account. Checked at start, not at the first
     Accept.

=== Phase 2 — one config (poly child 2) ==================================

--- The file ---

<prefix>/etc/polytropos.toml, mode 0644, read by Python directly. Absorbs
delivery.toml, agentic-policy.json, the non-secret half of both .env files,
and every polytropos.conf setting that is really Python's (state_db,
artifact_root, queue_root, logs_root, tracker_url, tracker_bind, tracker_port,
runner_dev_env).

    schema = 1          # same shape as dev-env/dports_dev_env/runtime-profiles.toml

    [paths]
    logs_root     = "/build/synth/logs"
    state_db      = "{logs_root}/evidence/state.db"
    artifact_root = "{logs_root}/evidence"
    queue_root    = "{logs_root}/evidence/queue"

    [tracker]
    bind = "0.0.0.0"
    port = 8080
    url  = "http://127.0.0.1:8080"

    [runner]
    dev_env              = ""
    max_patch_attempts   = 3
    attempt_window_hours = 2
    bundle_backstop      = 10
    signature_stickiness = 3

    [llm.triage]
    model        = "..."
    api_key_file = "secrets/triage.key"
    reasoning    = "none"
    timeout      = 120

    [llm.patch]
    model        = "..."
    api_key_file = "secrets/patch.key"
    reasoning    = "low"
    timeout      = 600

    [llm.chat]                    # section absent = chat disabled, which is
    model        = "..."          # today's DP_HARNESS_CHAT_MODEL gate
    api_key_file = "secrets/chat.key"

    [delivery]                    # was delivery.toml
    type       = "local-patch"
    outbox     = "/var/spool/polytropos-delivery"
    token_file = "secrets/delivery.token"

    [policy.tiers]                # was agentic-policy.json
    AUTO = {max_iterations = 2, max_tokens = 30000}

--- Secrets stay one value per file ---

Named by the TOML's *_file keys, resolved relative to the config dir. This is
the ordinary *_FILE pattern, and it earns its place three ways: a TOML syntax
error cannot take out the credential set, rotation is a single write, and the
mode is per secret — which is exactly the granularity the privilege split
needs.

    secrets/triage.key, secrets/patch.key      0600 root       (runner only)
    secrets/chat.key, secrets/delivery.token   0640 root:group (tracker reads both)

The loader refuses a secret that is readable beyond what its declared reader
needs, the way the runner rc already warns at polytropos_runner:149.

--- A schema table in code is the single source of truth ---

One entry per setting: TOML path, type, default, and env= (or None). From it:

  - the sample TOML is generated, so it cannot drift from the code;
  - `dportsv3 config show` prints every resolved value and where it came from;
  - the f-string hole at steps.py:618 closes, because every name is a literal
    in one table;
  - "read by code, settable nowhere" (39 names today) becomes structurally
    impossible.

Env override is opt-in per entry, NOT a blanket file-then-env layer. A blanket
layer is cheaper to write and recreates today's problem under a new name: 67
undocumented variables, none of them in the sample. Roughly 8 entries carry
env= (listed in section E of the description).

--- polytropos.conf shrinks to rc's own business ---

Keeps only what is consumed before any Python runs: the enable flags,
polytropos_cmd, polytropos_dev_env_cmd, polytropos_user, polytropos_group,
polytropos_home, polytropos_path, and the path to the TOML. The rc scripts
stop sourcing .env files and stop translating rc vars into env vars;
${name}_env carries only HOME, DPORTSV3_NO_BOOTSTRAP and DPORTSV3_CONFIG_DIR.

One real coupling remains: the runner prestart's `install -d` on queue_root
and log_dir (polytropos_runner:143-146). Rather than duplicating those values
back into the .conf, have the prestart ask the tool —

    polytropos_queue_root=$(${polytropos_cmd} config get paths.queue_root)

One exec at service start, and no second copy of the value.

--- The dev-env constraint ---

26 of the variables belong to dports_dev_env, a separate distribution.
dportsv3 imports it (agent/health.py:88, agent/env_resolver.py:60-61) and
nothing imports back. So a SHARED loader has to live in dports_dev_env and be
imported by dportsv3, never the reverse. Either that, or dev-env keeps its own
file with its own copy of the machinery. Decide this before writing the
loader: getting it backwards reintroduces exactly the coupling paths.py was
written to remove.

--- Migration ---

`dportsv3 config migrate` reads an existing polytropos.conf plus the two .env
files, writes polytropos.toml and the secret files, and leaves the originals
untouched. For one release the loader warns when it still finds a .env.

--- Non-goals ---

newsyslog.conf.d/polytropos.conf keeps its own format. The five
inter-process variables in section E stay environment. DP_TEST_* is untouched.
close_reason:
Both children delivered.

poly-cu8.1 (dbced36 + follow-ups): delivery reaches the operator's config,
and an unconfigured install is inert instead of raising create_failed
against the real upstream repo on every Accept.

poly-cu8.2 (423f832 + follow-ups): six config mechanisms became one
polytropos.toml plus one file per secret; the environment surface went
from 69 variables to 8 declared overrides; and a structural test now
fails the suite on an undeclared one, so "read by the code, settable
nowhere" cannot come back.

Both validated on hardware.

title: The compose tree is regenerated on the wrong side of the worktree reset
description:
Observed on hardware 2026-08-29. A build reported

  packages built: 3   failed: 0

for devel/glib20, which had been failing all day. It was a phantom: the
composed tree it built carried only three of the port's five patches --
patch-gio_meson.build and patch-gmodule_gmodule-dl.c were absent, which
is exactly why nothing failed. A fresh reapply from the clean baseline
produces all five (ops=5 applied=5 errors=0), so the tree really was
wrong, not the repo.

MECHANISM. worker.reset_port stage 2 runs `reapply <origin>` to
regenerate /work/artifacts/compose/<target>/<origin>/, and its docstring
says "from the now-reset substrate". But the same docstring records that
it no longer resets the source checkout:

  "What it no longer does is reset the source checkout. That stage
   existed to stop one job's escaped writes reaching the next one;
   since B1 each job works in its own worktree, which is destroyed
   with the job."

The worktree is destroyed in runner.py (destroy_job_worktree), AFTER
steps.py calls reset_port. So reapply composes whatever the agent last
left in the worktree. It succeeds -- it composed something -- so
reapply_ok is True, patch_post_reset logs plain success, and nothing
warns. Confirmed in the activity log: ts 2026-08-29T14:51:21, stage
patch_post_reset, "reset ports/devel/glib20/ to baseline after patch",
no failure entry, and the tree left behind was the agent's abandoned
state with two patches removed.

WHY THIS IS WORSE THAN A NORMAL BUG. The failure mode is a GREEN build
that contradicts the repository. A red build gets investigated; a green
one gets believed. If this ever reaches the delivery path it would
"verify" a fix in which the failing patches were deleted rather than
repaired -- the exact outcome poly-2xd and poly-28j are about.

FIX, per the operator's suggestion: compose the single origin BEFORE
work happens rather than after a reset.

  - at attempt start, so the agent begins from a tree derived from the
    repo it can see and cannot inherit a predecessor's discarded state
  - before a build, so dbuild can never build a phantom

That turns an ordering dependency spread across two modules into an
invariant each consumer establishes for itself. The post-reset reapply
stays as belt and braces instead of being what correctness rests on --
note the current ordering already broke silently, and the docstring
still describes the pre-B1 world.

SECOND BENEFIT. dsynth_build today refuses unless materialize_dports ran
in the current attempt, which is why one measured attempt called it four
times. With a compose at attempt start the baseline always exists and
the guard reduces to its real question -- has the source changed since
the last compose -- instead of forcing a ritual call. Partly addresses
poly-47d.

CONSTRAINTS. Scope it to the one origin: a full compose is ~20 minutes,
a single-origin reapply is seconds. And if that reapply fails the
attempt must REFUSE to start, not proceed against an unknown tree --
the opposite of today's best-effort.
close_reason:
Landed in aec41a4. The patch step composes the one origin before the agent
runs, after the clean check, so an attempt cannot inherit a predecessor's
discarded worktree state. A failed compose refuses the job
(patch_preflight_compose_failed, PATCH_GAVE_UP) rather than proceeding against
an undescribable tree; the success path logs patch_preflight_composed.
reset_port's docstring no longer claims it composes from a reset substrate.
Using materialize_dports here also seeds the dsynth_build staleness baseline
from turn one. Covered by tests/test_patch_preflight_compose.py.

title: Reasoning cannot be controlled: litellm 1.65.0 drops extra_body, so thinking is always on
description:
Model output is ~51% of billable spend (60,762 of 120,106 on the
measured glib20 attempt) and 94% of that output is reasoning_content.
It is the single largest cost in the patch loop and nothing in the
harness has ever asked for less of it.

THE API SUPPORTS CONTROLLING IT. Per DeepSeek's Thinking Mode guide,
thinking is ON by default at effort "high", and is controlled with:

  extra_body={"thinking": {"type": "disabled"}}   # off
  reasoning_effort="low" | "high" | "max"

OUR LITELLM CANNOT SEND EITHER. py311-litellm-1.65.0, and 1.65.0 is the
newest in the DragonFly repo.

  - reasoning_effort / thinking as top-level kwargs are rejected outright:
    "litellm.UnsupportedParamsError: deepseek does not support
    parameters". allowed_openai_params does not help; the deepseek config
    validates first.
  - extra_body is accepted and then sent as a LITERAL top-level key.
    Captured off the wire against a local sink:

      {"model": "deepseek-v4-pro", "messages": [...],
       "extra_body": {"thinking": {"type": "disabled"}}}

    DeepSeek sees a field called extra_body (unknown, ignored) and no
    thinking field. That is why the setting appeared to do nothing.

MEASURED IMPACT, real API, identical prompt:

  deepseek-v4-pro   effort=high (default)  completion=6346  reasoning=24955
  deepseek-v4-pro   effort=low             completion=4483  reasoning=17640
  deepseek-v4-pro   thinking disabled      completion= 350  reasoning=    0
  deepseek-v4-flash effort=low             completion=4186  reasoning=13309
  deepseek-v4-flash thinking disabled      completion= 694  reasoning=    0

Disabling thinking is a ~92% cut in completion tokens; effort=low is
~29%. Output is billed at full rate and never cached at generation, so
this is a direct saving, not a caching artifact.

THE FIX IS AVAILABLE WITHOUT AN UPGRADE. py311-openai-1.70.0 is already
installed and unpacks extra_body correctly -- verified off the wire:

  openai SDK wire keys: ['messages', 'model', 'thinking']

llm.py has exactly one call site (litellm.completion), so routing
OpenAI-compatible providers through the openai SDK, or pip-installing a
newer litellm over the package, are both contained changes.

NOT YET ANSWERED -- QUALITY. Every measurement here is cost. On the probe
prompt the no-thinking answer was LONGER (1404 vs 847 chars) but that is
not evidence it was better, and patch work is exactly the kind of task
reasoning is supposed to help. Before switching anything, decide per
role: triage is a cheap classification and may not need thinking at all,
while the patch loop probably wants effort=low rather than off. Wants an
A/B on real bundles, not a single prompt.

Related: poly-pg4 (reasoning spent renumbering lines), poly-3f9 (litellm
import fragility on this host), poly-170 (DragonFly package limits).
notes:
UPGRADING LITELLM IS NOT AVAILABLE ON THIS PLATFORM. Tested 2026-08-29.

  pip install litellm          -> fastuuid needs maturin; maturin fails
                                  to build (poly-170: needs rustc >= 1.89,
                                  base has 1.85.1)
  pip install --no-deps litellm -> 'Could not build wheels for litellm'

So 1.65.0 is the ceiling here, not a version we happen to be behind on,
and 1.65.0 structurally cannot send the parameter. The choice is not
'upgrade or not'.

WHAT LITELLM ACTUALLY EARNS, having read the call site. Exactly one:
llm.complete -> litellm.completion. Everything else in the codebase is
comments. From the response we use only OpenAI-shaped fields --
choices[0].message, .tool_calls, .reasoning_content -- plus one thing
that is genuinely not free:

  usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens

litellm normalizes cache-read tokens across providers (DeepSeek
prompt_cache_hit_tokens, Anthropic cache_read_input_tokens, OpenAI
cached_tokens). The whole budget gate is billable = uncached + output,
so that field is load-bearing. Replacing litellm means owning that
mapping per provider.

The other thing it earns is provider routing from the model string, and
tool-schema translation for providers that are not OpenAI-shaped. Today
we only run DeepSeek, which is OpenAI-compatible, so neither is being
exercised -- but *_PROVIDER and *_API_BASE are documented knobs, so the
capability is intended rather than accidental.

OPTIONS, in increasing cost:
  1. openai SDK for OpenAI-compatible providers, litellm kept as the
     fallback path for anything else. One backend switch in llm.complete,
     which is already the only call site. Keeps the abstraction, unblocks
     the parameter. We would own cached_tokens mapping for the SDK path
     (DeepSeek: prompt_cache_hit_tokens).
  2. Drop litellm outright for the openai SDK. Simplest code, loses
     non-OpenAI-shaped providers entirely.
  3. Leave it and accept ~50% of spend going to forced reasoning.

Recommend 1. It is the smallest change that unblocks the saving without
throwing away multi-provider support we have not yet needed but have
deliberately designed for.
WHICH LITELLM VERSION WOULD FIX IT, checked against the source at each tag.

  1.65.0   2025-03-28  ours. deepseek config has no thinking or
                       reasoning_effort at all.
  1.80.10  2025-12-14  first release after PR #17712. Adds both params,
                       but ENABLE ONLY.
  1.85.0-1.92.x        still enable-only. The mapping reads:
                         if thinking.type == 'enabled': set it
                         elif reasoning_effort != 'none': set enabled
                       so {'type':'disabled'} is silently dropped and
                       reasoning_effort='none' sets nothing, leaving the
                       API default (enabled). This is issues #27439 and
                       #27453; PR #27829 would have fixed it and was
                       closed stale 2026-08-23.
  1.93.2   2026-08-09  FIRST RELEASE THAT CAN DISABLE. Accepts both
                       'enabled' and 'disabled', and maps
                       reasoning_effort='none' -> disabled.
  1.98.0   2026-08-22  latest stable.

So the required version is >= 1.93.2, which is three weeks old. Waiting
on the DragonFly package means waiting for a 17-month jump onto
something very recent, AND the package still cannot build until poly-170
is resolved -- newer litellm pulls fastuuid, which needs maturin, which
needs rustc >= 1.89.

Two things follow:
  - 'wait for the package' is not a near-term plan; it is blocked behind
    poly-170 and then behind a very large version jump.
  - the openai-SDK path (option 1) needs no upgrade at all: py311-openai
    1.70.0 is already installed and already puts thinking on the wire,
    verified by wire capture.

title: init_db cannot open a state.db that predates a column: index built before its migration
description:
The tracker refuses to start against any evidence tree carrying a
state.db from an earlier generation of the tool:

  sqlite3.OperationalError: no such column: issue_key
    db/schema.py in init_db -> conn.executescript(SCHEMA)

Two independent defects, either one enough to break startup.

1. MIGRATIONS had an entry for jobs.owner_id but none for
   bundles.issue_key.

2. init_db ran executescript(SCHEMA) BEFORE MIGRATIONS. SCHEMA builds
   indexes, so idx_bundles_issue_key was asked to index a column three
   steps before the ALTER that adds it. Every table is CREATE TABLE IF
   NOT EXISTS, so the outdated table is left alone and the index is what
   fails.

jobs.owner_id has no index, which is the only reason it never surfaced.
The ordering defect is general: it fires for whichever migrated column
gets indexed next.

Measured drift on a real pre-existing DB: 24 tables, 0 missing, exactly
2 missing columns. So the data is one ALTER away from usable -- the
wipe that a startup crash invites is not warranted.

Distinct from poly-cka, which is about a WIPED evidence tree letting the
runner create a state.db the tracker cannot write. This one is the
opposite: an intact DB the tracker cannot open.
notes:
FIXED, not yet verified on hardware.

Both halves:
  - MIGRATIONS gains ALTER TABLE bundles ADD COLUMN issue_key TEXT
  - the MIGRATIONS loop moves ahead of executescript(SCHEMA)

Reordering is safe on a fresh DB: every ALTER raises 'no such table',
which the existing tolerant except already swallows, and SCHEMA then
creates the columns inline.

tests/test_schema_migration_ordering.py, 15 tests. 4 fail against the
pre-fix code. The parametrized one is the general guard: for every
column MIGRATIONS adds, simulate a DB predating it and require init_db
to restore both the column and any index over it.

An earlier draft of that guard asserted every INDEXED column needs a
migration entry -- false, most are original columns, 46 failures. The
invariant is the narrower one above.

Still open: a deployed host with the old DB stays broken until either
the fix ships to it or the two columns are added by hand.

title: make_extract is dead in the dev-env: stale perl 5.36 vs a 2026Q3 tree that needs 5.42
description:
Every patch attempt that needs the port source fails at step 1.
Measured on x6 2026-08-28, devel/glib20, both attempts, from
analysis/tool_trace.jsonl:

  make_extract ok=false rc=1
  "===>  glib-2.86.4,2 Invalid perl5 version 5.36.
   *** Error code 1"
  wrkdir="" wrksrc=""

Mechanism: bsd.default-versions.mk:141 derives PERL5_DEFAULT from the
installed perl binary rather than the tree's default -

  PERL5_DEFAULT:= ${_PERL5_FROM_BIN:R}

The chroot has /usr/local/bin/perl5.36.3 installed. The 2026Q3 tree
declares PERL5_DEFAULT?=5.42, so perl5.mk:56 fires
IGNORE= Invalid perl5 version 5.36 and extract stops.

WHY IT HID: the dsynth build itself gets past extract fine - it failed
at the patch phase, which is the failure we were chasing. dsynth builds
inside its own builder with its own package set; make_extract runs
directly in the chroot where the stale perl lives. The agent's tooling
and the build it is trying to repair do not run in the same
environment, and only one of them is broken.

BLAST RADIUS: any USES=perl5 port, which for the patch flow means any
port whose repair needs the extracted source. The re-cut procedure
(make_extract -> make_patch -> dupe -> genpatch -> install_patches) is
unreachable start to finish.
notes:
Is this just old packages that will age out? Checked 2026-08-28. No.

NOTHING AUTO-REMEDIATES IT. dev-env update is git-only - update.py:77
"Refresh mirrors + fast-forward the env's git checkouts". It never
touches pkg. So updating an env moves the ports tree forward and leaves
the package set where it was: the skew this bug depends on gets WIDER
