with every update, not narrower.

IT IS NOT AN OLD ENV. perl5-5.36.3_3 was installed 2026-08-27 11:32:57
- yesterday. Something is actively putting 5.36 into fresh envs, from a
binary repo older than the tree. Waiting does not help.

THE PACKAGE IS ORPHANED, NOT MERELY BEHIND. Its origin is
lang/perl5.36, and the 2026Q3 tree has only perl5-devel, 5.40, 5.42 and
5.44. The installed package points at a port that no longer exists
there, so no in-tree upgrade path reaches it.

THE MECHANISM CUTS THE OTHER WAY THAN EXPECTED. bsd.default-versions.mk
declares the tree default at :131 with ?=

  PERL5_DEFAULT?= 5.42

and then :141 OVERRIDES it from whatever perl is installed

  PERL5_DEFAULT:= ${_PERL5_FROM_BIN:R}

So with no perl installed at all, the tree's own 5.42 default holds and
extract works. It is the PRESENCE of an orphaned perl that breaks it,
not its absence. That makes "provision perl 5.42" and "do not preinstall
perl" both valid fixes, and the second is cheaper.

ON PINNING perl5=5.42 AS A STOPGAP: fine, but placement decides whether
it is acceptable.
  - env make.conf: legitimate. It only restores the default the tree
    already declares, and stays inside the throwaway env.
  - port overlay.dops: not acceptable - that ships a local env
    workaround to every DeltaPorts consumer for a port whose failure
    has nothing to do with perl. This is exactly what poly-28j caught
    the agent doing, and that objection stands even though its stated
    reason ("unrelated") was wrong.
CORRECTION 2026-08-28, second pass. The note above is wrong where it
says waiting does not help. It does.

The env's pkg repo is the official mirror:

  Avalon: https://mirror-master.dragonflybsd.org/dports/${ABI}/LATEST
  pkg rquery %n-%v perl5  ->  perl5-5.36.3_3

So LATEST itself currently ships 5.36. The env installs exactly what the
official repo offers; nothing here is provisioning wrongly, and when the
DragonFly builders publish against a newer snapshot the derived
PERL5_DEFAULT becomes 5.42 and extract starts working with no change on
our side. Dropped to P3 - this is not ours to fix.

WHAT IS STILL OURS, and is the reason to keep the bead open:

A dev-env pairs official DragonFly LATEST packages with a freebsd-ports
checkout on a release branch. Those two move on independent schedules,
so the tree routinely runs ahead of the packages. This is a permanent
structural property of the env design, not a one-off. It is perl today;
it will be something else the next time a Uses/*.mk gates on a version
derived from an installed binary.

And nothing detects it. env_health_status probes python_runtime,
writable_overlay and dports_compose - none of which exercise the ports
machinery. It took a 49-call agent tool trace to find that this env
could not extract a port. A probe that runs make_extract against any
cheap port at health time would have said so in one second, named the
IGNORE line, and stopped the patch flow from ever claiming the job.

Retitle when picked up: the bug is "env health does not probe whether
the env can extract a port", not the perl version.

The bad failure mode this exposed - a failed make_extract not aborting
the attempt - stays on poly-n78 and is independent of the cause.
TRIED THE make.conf SHORTCUT 2026-08-28. It works for perl and does not
get us a working extract. Recording so nobody retries it.

/etc is read-only in the chroot: the base is null-mounted ro and only
/work, /root, /tmp, /var/tmp, /etc/dsynth and /construction are
writable. So no /etc/make.conf, and no /usr/local/etc either. Note
/etc/dsynth IS writable - it is dsynth's per-profile make.conf, which a
bare make never reads, so it is the wrong file anyway.

__MAKE_CONF does work:

  make __MAKE_CONF=/work/make.conf ... -V PERL5_DEFAULT  ->  5.42

and the perl IGNORE disappears. Then extract fails one layer down, on
the same skew:

  glib depends on g-ir-scanner - not found
  gobject-introspection-bootstrap depends on bison - not found
  bison depends on m4 ... m4 depends on makeinfo ... texinfo depends on
  help2man ... help2man depends on p5-Locale-gettext ... depends on
  gettext-runtime>=0.26
  ===> An older version of gettext-runtime is already installed
       (gettext-runtime-0.23.1)
  *** Error code 1

make -V WRKSRC names /work/obj/devel/glib20/glib-2.86.4 and that
directory does not exist - extract-depends must pass before do-extract
runs, so nothing is unpacked.

THE REAL SHAPE, and it is not about perl. dsynth builds glib20's
dependencies without trouble - they were Already-Built in the same run.
dsynth builds inside its own builders against packages it built itself.
make_extract runs a bare make in the chroot proper, against packages
installed from the official mirror. Those are two different package
universes and only one of them matches the tree.

So no env-level pin fixes this. Either the agent's extract runs in the
same context dsynth builds in (or is driven through dsynth), or the
chroot's installed package set has to track the ports tree. That is a
design question for the patch flow, not a workaround.

Left /work/make.conf in the env; inert unless __MAKE_CONF names it.
The design question this exposed - two package universes, and no per-env override channel for base-owned config - is poly-0oe. This bead stays scoped to the perl/mirror lag and the missing health probe.
Any token figures quoted in these notes are raw cache-inclusive totals and overstate real cost by ~18x; see the correction on poly-7eh. The make_extract failure and its consequences are unaffected.
REPRODUCES ON A FRESH ENV, 2026-08-29. Not stale-env rot: this
env was provisioned the same day from a current world, and the perl is
still 5.36.3 while the tree declares 5.42.

Root cause is the package universe, not the env's age. The mirror the
base provisions from (dragonfly:6.6:x86:64/LATEST) offers:

  perl5-5.36.3_3   perl5.38-5.38.4   perl5.40-5.40.2   perl5-devel-5.41.3

There is no 5.42 at any version. The official binary repo is behind the
quarterly tree, so no amount of re-provisioning fixes this.

CONFIRMED AS THE GATE ON poly-0oe. Full agent run on hardware, glib20:
triage -> ASSIST -> patch job -> attempt 1 -> 4 LLM turns -> make_extract
-> blocked on 'Invalid perl5 version 5.36'. NO_DEPENDS was never
exercised, because the IGNORE verdict fires before dependency resolution
is attempted. NO_DEPENDS cannot be tested in the agent until this lands.

The abort itself behaved: stopped at turn 4, 39962 billable of a 120000
budget, status=environment-blocked.

LEAD: the tree honours NO_IGNORE (bsd.port.mk:2867 .if !defined(NO_IGNORE)).
With NO_IGNORE=yes the extract dry-run runs through to .extract_done
instead of dying. Needs a decision, because it collides with the poly-n78
abort: two different things are called IGNORE.

  - 'this port genuinely cannot build here'  -> abort is right
  - 'the dev-env package universe is stale'  -> abort is wrong; extract,
    dupe and genpatch would all work

Candidate rule: extract and patch bypass IGNORE, the build honours it.
Extract only unpacks a distfile and needs no perl at all.

NOT viable: installing a correct perl into the chroot. dsynth DID build
perl5-5.42.3 into the env's own repo during this run, but the chroot's
/usr/local is the shared provisioned base, null-mounted read-only, and
making it writable is not wanted.
FIXED AND VERIFIED ON HARDWARE 2026-08-29. Three commits.

1cee55f  worker: set PACKAGE_BUILDING on the agent's make calls
17be7b4  worker: ask the probes the same question the extract asked

ROOT CAUSE, from the tree rather than inference: bsd.port.mk:2931 does
not add a check to the build when IGNORE is set, it REPLACES the build
graph. Fourteen targets -- check-sanity fetch checksum extract patch
configure all build install reinstall test package stage restage -- are
redefined to 'echo the reason; exit 1'. The real extract target, with
its extract-depends prerequisite and its do-extract, is never defined.
That is why NO_DEPENDS was never exercised: there was no dependency
resolution to suppress.

THE FIX IS ALIGNMENT, NOT A BYPASS. dsynth writes PACKAGE_BUILDING=yes
into every builder's make.conf (dsynth build.c:2095, dsynth.c:250).
bsd.default-versions.mk:130 keys the tree's declared default on exactly
that variable. So the agent was reading the tree differently from the
builder it was repairing; setting it removes the divergence and the
framework itself stops objecting. Its side effects run the same way --
NO_PACKAGE and MANUAL_PACKAGE_BUILD ports now IGNORE for the agent as
they do on the farm, so it declines what dsynth declines.

SCOPE IS SMALLER THAN FEARED. Only 2 of 52 _DEFAULT knobs consult the
installed system (_PERL5_FROM_BIN, OPENSSL_INSTALLED); the other 50 are
static declarations the chroot cannot influence. One flag closes the
class.

MEASURED: PERL5_DEFAULT 5.36 -> 5.42, IGNORE cleared, and WRKSRC
PATCHDIR PATCH_LIST EXTRACT_ONLY DISTFILES DISTNAME all identical.

TWO DEFECTS FOUND WHILE VERIFYING, both fixed in 17be7b4:
  - the -V IGNORE probe ran without the flag, so a port that extracted
    fine was reported IGNOREd over a perl version the real command never
    objected to, with a summary claiming the source could not be
    extracted while it sat unpacked on disk
  - post-extract runs AFTER the distfile is unpacked, so a port whose
    post-extract needs a skipped EXTRACT_DEPENDS leaves a complete
    WRKSRC. That is no longer reported as a failed extract; emptiness is
    checked on disk, since a do-extract that fails outright also leaves
    WRKDIR behind.

END-TO-END ON HARDWARE, glib20:
  before  attempt 1 -> turn 4  -> make_extract FAIL -> environment-blocked
  after   attempt 1 -> turn 23 -> make_extract ok -> make_patch ->
          dsynth_build x2, reaching glib20@default
The remaining limit is budget (poly-7eh), not a wall.

title: The patch agent hand-edits patch files instead of running dupe/genpatch
description:
Measured on x6 2026-08-28, devel/glib20, bundle
devel_glib20@bootstrap-20260828-111113Z.

After poly-2xd the agent aims at the right outcome: it re-cut the
drifted patch and left overlay.dops alone. But it did not use the
re-cut procedure. The 49-call tool trace contains no dupe, no genpatch
and no install_patches. It made one put_file (call 37) straight onto
ports/devel/glib20/dragonfly/patch-gio_meson.build.

That is text-editing the diff, which flow-patch.md forbids in the same
section:

  "Do not text-edit the diff to 'fix' line numbers. ... Patch files are
   output artifacts - treat them as regenerate-only."

The result looks plausible and is probably invalid. It rewrote a
deletion line of the unified diff:

  -  libelf = cc.find_library('elf', required : get_option ('libelf'))
  +  libelf = declare_dependency(link_args: '/lib/libelf.so.2')

A "-" line has to match upstream exactly. declare_dependency(...) is
DragonFly's replacement text, not anything upstream ships, so the hunk
cannot apply. It also adjusted the hunk header (@@ -934,20 -> @@ -964,20)
and the .orig timestamp by hand - exactly the "shifts the hunk body but
not its header" shape the playbook warns about.

Never verified either way: the run hit budget-exhausted before any
rebuild (poly-7eh), so rebuild_proof.json is synthetic:true.
notes:
CAUSE FOUND 2026-08-28, same trace. The hand-edit is downstream, not an
independent judgment failure.

make_extract failed (poly-cx6) on both attempts, returning wrksrc="".
With no WRKSRC there is nothing to dupe, nothing to edit and nothing to
genpatch - the procedure the playbook prescribes is physically
unavailable. Calls 8-36 are the agent hunting for an extracted tree by
hand (/work/obj, /work/dsynth/build/SL00), trying to reach the distfile
(blocked: "path must be under /work"), and grepping /work for upstream
source that was never unpacked. Call 37 is it giving up and editing the
patch from what it could infer.

So this bead should NOT be read as "teach it to prefer genpatch". Fix
poly-cx6 first, then re-measure - the hand-edit may simply stop.

WHAT SURVIVES REGARDLESS: a failed make_extract does not abort the
attempt. The tool returns ok=false and the loop carries on for 44 more
calls, burning the whole budget and emitting a plausible-looking but
probably invalid patch. A step-1 failure that makes the entire
procedure impossible should stop the attempt and report the
environment, not degrade into improvisation. That is the durable defect
here and it is worth keeping even after cx6 is fixed.
Token figures cited here (2,160,584) are raw cache-inclusive totals from patch_audit.json, not the metric the budget uses. Real spend was 120,064 billable against a 120,000 cap. See the correction on poly-7eh. The behavioural finding - hand-edit instead of dupe/genpatch - is unaffected.
SETTLED by the session dump, x6 2026-08-28, bundle
...-20260828-120749Z, patch attempt 1, assistant message 13 - the turn
that issued the put_file:

  "The make_extract failed with an environment error ("Invalid perl5
   version 5.36") - different from the real build's patch failure. Let
   me investigate the available sources to regenerate the patch
   without it."

So this is not the agent failing to read the playbook. Verified present
in that same prompt: "never text-edit the diff", "regenerate-only",
"`overlay.dops` needs no edit at all", plus dupe and genpatch. It had
the guidance, correctly identified the environment as broken,
correctly separated it from the failure it was sent to fix, and then
chose to route around it.

That is a reasonable thing for an agent with nowhere to report a broken
environment to do. It is the wrong thing for this system to allow.

CONFIRMS the re-scope: the fix is not "prefer genpatch". It is that a
failed precondition must end the attempt with an environment verdict
the operator sees. Teaching it harder cannot beat an agent that already
knows and is working around a wall.

REPRODUCED n=2: same in-place re-cut, same untouched overlay.dops, same
invalid rewritten deletion line, both runs.
FULL SESSION READ 2026-08-28 (patch attempt 1, 85 records, 29
assistant turns). My earlier notes were built on a targeted extract and
got three things wrong.

1. THE REBUILD DID RUN. I wrote that budget exhaustion stopped it
before any rebuild. Not so: turns A19-A20 ran materialize_dports
(ok) then dsynth_build, and A21-A24 read the resulting log. The agent
tested its own fix.

2. THE FIX DID NOT WORK, and now we know rather than guess. From the
dsynth log it fetched:

  ===>  Applying dragonfly patches ... from /xports/devel/glib20/dragonfly
  1 out of 1 hunks failed--saving rejects to gio/meson.build.rej
  ===>  FAILED Applying dragonfly patch-gio_meson.build

Same failure as before the edit. So "probably invalid" was the right
conclusion.

3. MY REASON FOR IT WAS WRONG. I argued declare_dependency(link_args:
'/lib/libelf.so.2') could not sit on a removal line because upstream
never ships it. The agent found otherwise, at A07:

  "The FreeBSD files/patch-gio_meson.build already performs the
   cc.find_library -> declare_dependency substitution. That means the
   DragonFly patch (which applies after FreeBSD's) is failing because
   its removal hunk still lists the now-replaced cc.find_library line."

That is correct and it is the actual root cause of the port failure -
FreeBSD added a files/ patch that collides with the DragonFly one.
Putting declare_dependency on the removal line was reasonable. Why the
hunk still rejects is undetermined; likely the remaining context lines
or the recomputed @@ -964 header.

AND IT CITED THE PLAYBOOK. A18, the turn that made the edit:

  "The fix per the playbook: re-cut the DragonFly patch (hand-maintained
   Meson file -> keep static patch, keep file materialize), updating
   the re[moval hunk]"

Explicit attribution. Strongest evidence yet that the corpus is what
drives the behaviour.

OPEN QUESTION worth its own look: if FreeBSD's files/ patch now performs
the same substitution, is the DragonFly patch still needed at all, or
does it only need to stop removing a block FreeBSD already handles?
Nobody has asked that. It is a ports question, not a tooling one.
IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-28.

make_extract asks `make -V IGNORE` when extract fails, rather than
matching error text - IGNORE reasons are free text set by any
Uses/*.mk, so a phrase list would miss every reason nobody has hit yet.
Verified against the real env: glib20 answers "Invalid perl5 version
5.36", editors/vim answers empty.

A blocking result is recorded in the message history first (so the
session dump still shows what the model was told), then raises
EnvironmentBlocked out of the dispatch loop carrying the spend so far -
otherwise a blocked attempt looks free in the audit. attempt_loop
returns status=environment-blocked with a verdict that names the
operator and says it is not a port problem, and does not spend the
remaining attempts.

Ordinary extract failures - bad checksum, missing distfile - stay the
agent's to work. Only an IGNORE stops the loop.

Downstream needed nothing: steps.py branches on status == "success"
only, and manual_handoff renders the status verbatim.

10 tests, 8 of which fail against the previous code. The 2 that pass
either way are the negative cases, which is the point.

STILL OPEN on this bead: whether the agent prefers dupe/genpatch when
the procedure is actually available. Unmeasurable until poly-0oe, since
make_extract has never succeeded in this env.
RELATED, different cause: poly-7jw (filed 2026-09-01). This bead attributes the hand-edit to make_extract being dead (poly-cx6, since closed), which made dupe/genpatch unavailable. Measured again on 2026-09-01 with make_extract working: the agent DOES call dupe and genpatch, and they still yield nothing usable, because put_file truncated the source first (onetbb 6771 -> 1247 bytes, libunwind 8017 -> 0 bytes). The hand-edit is then a fallback after install_patches reports installed=0 FAIL. So 'teach it to prefer genpatch' remains insufficient on its own; the missing line-oriented edit primitive is tracked in poly-7jw.
poly-dq5 explains why the hand-edit persists after poly-cx6 closed.
make_extract works now, but genpatch stages into WRKSRC on a
_WRKSRC_CACHE hit while install_patches only reads /work/genpatch-out,
so the dupe/genpatch/install_patches route dead-ends and hand-authoring
is the only move left.

title: Playbooks contradict each other on a drifted patch: two say delete the fix, one says keep it
description:
A patch-error payload attaches three playbooks that give incompatible
instructions for the same situation — an existing dragonfly/ patch that
no longer applies after an upstream version bump.

KEEP IT (correct):
  error-prefer-dops-over-static-patches.md:69
    "-> Re-cut the patch (next section), KEEP the file materialize."
  ...:87
    "genpatch, write the refreshed patch back under dragonfly/, and
     keep the file materialize line."

DELETE IT FIRST (wrong for this case):
  error-dragonfly-source-patches.md:126
    "If a patch is wrong or drifted, remove its install line from
     overlay.dops and regenerate."
  flow-patch.md:243
    "1. Remove its install line from overlay.dops (rewrite via
     put_file) so compose stops referencing it. 2. Regenerate..."

Two of the three say remove-first, and the word "drifted" is in the
remove instruction — which is exactly the glib20 case. The agent's
reading was defensible; it followed a playbook. So poly-28j is not
only an agent-judgment failure, it is a playbook defect, and no amount
of prompt tightening fixes a corpus that disagrees with itself.

Note the two situations really are different and the playbooks conflate
them. flow-patch's recovery section is written about a MALFORMED patch
("malformed patch", "a patch that lies about its own bytes") where the
file is genuinely garbage and removal is right. A drifted patch is
well-formed and still encodes the wanted change; it needs refreshing,
not deleting. One section currently covers both.
design:
Two separate defects; both are edits to the playbook corpus, no code.

1. SPLIT MALFORMED FROM DRIFTED. flow-patch.md's "Recovering from a
broken patch" should say up front which case it is about (malformed /
lies-about-its-own-bytes) and route drift to
error-prefer-dops-over-static-patches.md. Delete "or drifted" from
error-dragonfly-source-patches.md:126 and point at the same place.
One procedure per situation, named by the situation.

2. FIX THE ORDER, NOT JUST THE WORDING. Even where removal is correct,
remove-then-regenerate has an intermediate state that is a silent
regression: the materialize line is gone and the refreshed patch does
not exist yet. If the attempt dies in that window the build goes GREEN
with the platform fix missing and nothing reports a problem.

That is not hypothetical — it is what happened. glib20 hit
budget-exhausted after 4 attempts (patch_audit.json, 4,545,810 tokens),
and the last state on disk was the deleted materialize line. See the
token bead for why the budget died.

Prescribe regenerate-then-swap instead: build the refreshed patch under
dragonfly/ first, verify it, and only then touch overlay.dops — so
every intermediate state either has the old fix or the new one, never
neither. Where compose must be made green before the new patch exists,
say so explicitly and name the deferred-patch channel (flow-patch.md
already mentions it at the make_patch step) rather than leaving a bare
"remove the line".

ACCEPTANCE: grep the corpus for every instruction that removes a
materialize/patch-apply line and confirm each one states its situation
and leaves no window where the fix is absent from a green build.
notes:
RE-REVIEW 2026-08-28. Three corrections and one addition.

1. RENDER ORDER MAKES IT WORSE THAN DESCRIBED. Selection sorts by
(priority, path.name) — playbooks.py:445 — so the payload reads:
prefer-dops (50) first, flow-patch (55) second, dragonfly-source (100)
last. The CORRECT "keep the materialize line" guidance renders first
and both contradicting passages come after it. Worst possible order.

2. flow-patch's recovery section does not merely omit the drift case,
it CLAIMS it. Its trigger list is "applies dirty, malformed patch,
wrong hunk count, line-number mismatch" — a drifted patch presents as
exactly that. So a reader holding a drifted patch lands in the
malformed-patch procedure legitimately, not by misreading.

3. error-dragonfly-source-patches.md is titled "Creating
DragonFly-specific source patches" and is scoped to authoring. Its
repair prescription at :126 is outside its own stated scope; that is
the cleanest thing to cut.

4. NOT COVERED BY ANY TEST. tests/test_playbooks.py exercises the
parser and selector against tmp_path fixtures only; nothing asserts
anything about the shipped corpus. So the contradiction was
reintroducible at zero cost and would stay invisible. The fix needs a
corpus-level guard, not just an edit.

SCOPE CONFIRMED: prose plus one new test. No code change.
close_reason: Validated on x6 2026-08-28 (bundle devel_glib20@bootstrap-20260828-111113Z). The agent re-cut the drifted patch and left overlay.dops untouched; triage now names the delete-the-fix hazard in its own Notes. Follow-on defects: poly-n78 (hand-edits instead of genpatch), poly-7eh (budget).

title: The tool-venv bind-mount shadows the env's own checkout and breaks it
description:
Self-inflicted, by the poly-7z1 fix in commit 406c7db. It breaks a
working env.

prepare_root_runtime bind-mounts the host's tool venv read-only at
/work/polytropos. That path is not free: layout.py:41 defines
TOOL_DIR = "/work/polytropos" and documents it as "this tool's own
checkout", exported into every chroot as POLYTROPOS_ROOT, with the
repository's own shell wrapper at TOOL_BIN = $TOOL_DIR/bin/dportsv3 and
an in-env venv at TOOL_VENV_RELATIVE = work/polytropos/.venv.

So the mount shadows a full, working checkout.

CONSEQUENCES OBSERVED ON x6

env_health_status went to broken:

    dports_compose: $POLYTROPOS_ROOT/bin/dportsv3 --version failed
    (rc=127): /bin/sh: /work/polytropos/bin/dportsv3: not found

rc=127 on a file that exists is the shebang: with the mount in place that
path resolves to a venv console script naming /usr/local/lib/polytropos/
bin/python, a HOST path absent from the chroot. worker.py's validate_dops
runs the identical command for `dsl check`, so patching is broken the
same way — health is just where it surfaced.

Unmounting proves it. With the mount gone, /work/polytropos/bin holds
agent-queue-runner, artifact-store, artifact-store-client and dportsv3,
and `/work/polytropos/bin/dportsv3 --version` prints 3.0.0-dev from
inside the chroot.

WHAT THIS SAYS ABOUT poly-7z1

Its premise was wrong. "In-chroot hooks cannot reach the tool" — they
could; the checkout has been there since env creation. The real defect
was narrower and is already fixed: dportsv3-hooks.conf shipped
DPORTSV3_BIN=/build/synth/polytropos/bin/dportsv3, a path on no machine,
when the answer was the checkout already mounted at TOOL_BIN. The bead
read the stale conf value as evidence the tool was absent.
design:
Revert the mount, and the machinery built to work around the shebang it created.

REMOVE
- runtime.TOOL_VENV_TARGET, tool_venv_target() and the mount in prepare_root_runtime
- config.tool_venv / DPORTS_DEV_TOOL_VENV
- POLYTROPOS_PYTHON and polytropos_run in hook_common.sh, and the -r/-x
  branch it added to tracker_load_config. The checkout wrapper is a shell
  script; no interpreter indirection is needed for anything.
- POLYTROPOS_PYTHON from env_hook_settings and the conf example

KEEP
- env_hook_settings writing DPORTSV3_BIN and ARTIFACT_STORE_CLIENT, but
  sourced from layout.TOOL_BIN / TOOL_DIR rather than the mount path.
  This is what poly-7z1 actually needed.
- DPORTSV3_TRACKER_TARGET from the env's target (poly-5v6), verified.
- the tracker_config_defaults split, which is independently correct: a
  hook with artifact-store work to do must not exit 0 because the tracker
  is unusable.
- artifact-store-client as a package module and console script; that
  fixed a real gap for packaged installs.

RESTORE
- bin/artifact-store-client in the checkout, as a stdlib-only shim that
  imports dportsv3.artifact_store_client. Moving it into the package fixed
  the packaged install and broke the checkout case, where the env's
  /work/polytropos/bin/artifact-store-client is what the hooks call. One
  implementation, two entry points.
acceptance_criteria: 1. env health reports ok for dports_compose with no manual step. 2. $POLYTROPOS_ROOT/bin/dportsv3 and $POLYTROPOS_ROOT/bin/artifact-store-client both run directly inside the chroot. 3. No mount lands on TOOL_DIR. 4. An env synced to this commit still has bin/artifact-store-client.
notes:
Fix committed as 6e9c7c5; NOT yet verified on hardware. Verification needs the env recreated, since x6's current env has the bind-mount live and four modules hand-installed into the host venv. Close only after env health reports dports_compose ok with no manual step.
VERIFIED ON HARDWARE 2026-08-27 after a full teardown: DB wiped, env destroyed and recreated from the fixed commit 05139c8.

- nothing mounts on TOOL_DIR (mount | grep work/polytropos is empty)
- the env's checkout is at 05139c8 and carries bin/artifact-store-client
- both tools run DIRECTLY in-chroot, no interpreter indirection:
  /work/polytropos/bin/dportsv3 --version -> 3.0.0-dev
  /work/polytropos/bin/artifact-store-client ... health -> ok
- env-health: python_runtime ok, writable_overlay ok, dports_compose ok
  (detail 'dportsv3 3.0.0-dev' — the exact probe that returned rc=127)
- hooks-install wrote DPORTSV3_BIN=/work/polytropos/bin/dportsv3 and
  ARTIFACT_STORE_CLIENT=/work/polytropos/bin/artifact-store-client, with
  no POLYTROPOS_PYTHON

title: In-env hook outputs are chroot paths the host cannot resolve
description:
CORRECTED SCOPE 2026-08-27, after actually completing the cycle by hand.

The earlier framing pointed at poly-fij.1 and a job-model change. Both
were over-scoped. The real fix is small, and here is why.

ONLY ONE JOB TYPE EVER CROSSES THE BOUNDARY. hook_common.sh writes
"type=triage" and nothing else. patch, verify and confirm jobs are all
created by the runner, on the host, where the filesystem queue works
fine. So only hook-created triage jobs are stranded.

AND A TRIAGE JOB IS ALREADY FULLY IN THE DB. Its fields are
created_ts_utc, profile, target, origin, flavor, bundle_id, run_id,
type, snippet_round, has_snippets. The jobs row carries type, origin,
flavor, created_ts_utc, target and bundle_id directly; the rest join:

    jobs.bundle_id -> bundles.run_id -> runs.profile

snippet_round=0 and has_snippets=false are the fixed values for a fresh
hook job. The only fields with no DB source are iteration,
max_iterations and previous_bundle, which the hook writes only when
detect_rebuild_iteration finds a repeat — two columns, or derive the
count from the store.

Verified today: the runner picked the job up 5s after the file was moved
by hand, materialized 18 artifacts from the store over HTTP into a
tempdir, triaged correctly (patch-error, high confidence) and
auto-enqueued the patch job. Everything except locating the work already
crosses the boundary.
design:
Derive queued triage jobs from the DB instead of globbing pending/.

  SELECT j.*, b.run_id, r.profile
    FROM jobs j
    JOIN bundles b ON b.bundle_id = j.bundle_id
    JOIN runs    r ON r.run_id    = b.run_id
   WHERE j.state = 'queued' AND j.type = 'triage'

Materialize the job dict from that row and claim by UPDATE ... WHERE
state='queued' (rowcount is the claim). The runner keeps writing and
reading files for the jobs it creates itself — those never cross a
boundary — so this is additive, not a rewrite of dispatch.

No spec_json, no job-model change, no Step 32. Those matter for the
abandon race and for remote builders carrying patch/verify jobs; they do
not gate this.

The put-fs half is separate and unchanged: the hook must stop handing the
store a chroot path for the compressed full log. Fall back to put-blob.

WHY THIS IS P1: without it the loop cannot run unattended at all. Every
failure a build produces sits queued forever, and the only reason the
cycle completed today is that a file was copied by hand.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A dsynth failure inside an env produces a job the runner actually picks up. 2. Every artifact_refs row the store writes is readable by the store. 3. Neither fix depends on the builder sharing a filesystem with the tracker.
notes:
CONFIRMED ON HARDWARE 2026-08-27, both halves, with a real dsynth build in the 2026Q3-editors_vim env.

Three genuine failures fired hook_pkg_failure: devel/glib20@bootstrap (patch phase, rejected DragonFly hunk), graphics/jpeg-turbo (configure), lang/rust (fetch).

QUEUE HALF. Three .job files landed in the env's chroot-path queue at /work/dsynth/logs/evidence/queue/pending/. The host runner queue (/tmp/polyverify/logs/evidence/queue/pending/) stayed empty. Measured, not inferred.

PUT-FS HALF. artifact_refs now holds three backend='fs' rows whose fs_path is /work/dsynth/logs/evidence/full-logs/<bundle>.full.log.gz — chroot paths the store cannot open. One per bundle, exactly as predicted.

WHAT WORKED ANYWAY, and it matters for scoping: everything HTTP crossed the boundary fine. All three bundles reached the store with the correct target @2026Q3, carrying real artifacts — glib20 alone has 19, including port/files/patch-gio_meson.build, the very patch that failed to apply. Only the two path-carrying outputs failed.
RECONFIRMED 2026-08-27 on a completely clean stack — DB wiped, env destroyed and recreated, 25-minute from-scratch build of 188 packages. Neither half is an artefact of accumulated state.

  env (chroot) queue/pending:  3 files
  host runner queue/pending:   0 files
  runner_status:               idle / waiting

and three artifact_refs rows with backend='fs' and fs_path under
/work/dsynth/logs/evidence/full-logs/ — chroot paths the store cannot
open, one per bundle.

Everything upstream of the runner now works: build_runs 1 opened and
closed (total_expected=188), 3 bundles at target @2026Q3, 43 artifacts,
3 distinct fingerprinted issues, 3 jobs rows delivered over HTTP, and
runs.build_run_id=1. The runner is the only thing that cannot see the
work, and only because it looks in a directory.
FIXED AND VERIFIED ON x6 2026-08-27, branch fold-artifact-store.

Both halves.

PUT-FS HALF. hook_pkg_failure sends the gzipped full log with put-blob.
The store now also refuses a put-fs whose path it cannot open, so a
chroot path fails loudly at 400 instead of writing a row with size NULL
that 404s forever. Verified: a real hook run produced five artifacts,
all backend='blob', logs/full.log.gz among them, zero 'fs' rows.

QUEUE HALF. claim_next_job_batch tries pending/ first, unchanged, and
when it is empty derives queued triage jobs from jobs -> bundles -> runs.
The claim is lifecycle.apply(CLAIM), already under BEGIN IMMEDIATE, so
the state machine is the mutex rather than a rename. The job file is
then written into inflight/ as the carrier for process_job and as an
operator breadcrumb.

Reproduced the exact bug on hardware — hook writing to
/tmp/b2rtest-chroot/logs/evidence/queue while the runner watched
/tmp/b2rtest-logs/evidence/queue — and then, against that real DB:

  pending/ on the runner side: []
  jobs rows: [(...editors_vim-662250.job, 'queued')]
  claim_next_job_batch -> ...editors_vim-662250.job
  landed in: inflight | siblings: 0
  profile=2026Q3-editors_vim   (joined through bundles -> runs)
  run_id=run-2026Q3-editors_vim-unknown
  state now: 'claimed'
  no chroot path in the file: True
  second call (a second runner): None

17 unit tests cover siblings, both no-double-claim directions, non-
triage exclusion, already-claimed rows, and a missing runs row (left
queued and logged rather than claimed incomplete).

SCOPE HELD. Only type=triage is derived. patch/verify/confirm stay on
files; carrying those needs the spec payload poly-fij.1 owns.

NOT VERIFIED END TO END THROUGH THE RUNNER PROCESS. The runner refuses
to start as a non-root user (it enumerates dev-envs from
/root/.cache/dports-dev/envs), and running it as root would have put the
production dev-env in scope, so the claim path was exercised in-process
against the real DB instead. A root run inside a real dev-env is still
worth doing.
Dependency on poly-fij.1 removed 2026-08-27: stale. This bead's own CORRECTED SCOPE says fij.1 does not gate it — only type=triage crosses a boundary and a triage job is already fully in the DB — but the edge was never dropped when the scope was corrected.

title: Upgrading the rc.d scripts orphans a running stack
description:
The pidfile fix renamed what each file holds: the supervisor moved from \${name}.sup.pid to \${name}.pid, and the child moved to \${name}.child.pid. An operator upgrading a running stack keeps the old files, so `service stop|status` reads \${name}.pid, finds the CHILD pid there, fails to match procname (/usr/sbin/daemon) and reports 'not running' while all three services are alive. Observed on a live install: three running services, all reported not running, uncontrollable by service(8).

Consequence: the operator sees 'not running' and starts a second stack. The runner is protected by its flock (exit 3) but artifact-store and tracker race for their ports and share the DB.

The old processes have to be killed by pid, from the .sup.pid files, and those files removed. Nothing in deploy install does that or warns about it.
acceptance_criteria: 1) deploy install detects pidfiles from the previous layout and either refuses with the exact commands to run, or handles the changeover. 2) A running pre-change stack can be upgraded without the operator having to find pids by hand. 3) Documented in the runbook's 'when a service will not run' table.
notes:
MADE CONCRETE BY THE FOLD (poly-g19, branch fold-artifact-store) 2026-08-27.

Deploying that branch onto x6 as it stands leaves a live orphan, verified on the box:

  /usr/local/etc/rc.d/polytropos_artifact_store   still installed
  polytropos_artifact_store_enable="YES"          still in /etc/rc.conf
  127.0.0.1:8788                                 still listening

deploy install stopped shipping that script — RC_SCRIPTS no longer lists it — but nothing removes the copy already on disk, clears the rc.conf line, or stops the process. The orphan keeps writing the same state.db as a third process. WAL makes that safe rather than corrupting, so the symptom is a stale service nobody notices, not a failure.

Operator steps until this bead lands:
  service polytropos_artifact_store stop
  sysrc -x polytropos_artifact_store_enable
  rm /usr/local/etc/rc.d/polytropos_artifact_store

A retired service is the case this bead should cover alongside an upgraded one.

title: Base-branch resolution reads the symlink and silently defaults to master
description:
_resolve_bundle_base_branch (worker.py) determines the branch every job worktree cuts from. Three problems, all found while auditing poly-m7o:

  * It runs 'cd /work/DeltaPorts' — the agent-facing symlink — when this is plumbing and should address PORTS_MAIN_DIR. layout.py is explicit that agent-facing code uses the symlink and plumbing names ports-main. Same class as the two stale tool paths in poly-iyk.
  * It swallows any failure into '|| echo master'. A dangling or mid-repoint link yields empty stdout and the base silently becomes 'master'.
  * The result is cached per env for the process lifetime, so one bad early read pins the wrong base for every job that runner handles.

For an env whose default branch is not master this produces worktrees cut from the wrong base, silently.

VERIFIED: the function's body, its use as 'base' in create_job_worktree, and that base is passed to 'git worktree add -b <branch> <wt> <base>'.
NOT VERIFIED: whether any env in practice has a non-master default. If they are all master the impact is latent rather than active — worth checking before prioritising.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Base resolution reads PORTS_MAIN_DIR, not the symlink. 2. A failed resolution is an error, not a silent 'master'. 3. The cache cannot pin a value derived from a failed read.
notes:
VERIFIED ACTIVE ON x6 2026-08-23, not latent. The bead said the impact was unknown until someone checked whether a real env has a non-master default. Checked, and that was the wrong question:

  git -C /work/ports-main symbolic-ref --short refs/remotes/origin/HEAD
  -> fatal: ref refs/remotes/origin/HEAD is not a symbolic ref

The symbolic-ref FAILS on a real env, so '|| echo master' fires on EVERY call. The base is never actually resolved from the repo — it is always the hardcoded default, and the per-env cache then pins that for the process lifetime. _resolve_bundle_base_branch('2026Q3-editors_vim') returns 'master'.

Benign on this env only because ports-main happens to be on master (rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD = master, confirmed). Any env whose checkout sits on another branch gets worktrees cut from the wrong base, silently, with no diagnostic anywhere.

So this is not 'a fallback that might fire'. The resolution does not work at all; the right answer is currently arriving by coincidence.

LIKELY ROOT CAUSE to confirm when fixing: dev-env clones the ports mirror with 'git clone --mirror', and a mirror clone does not necessarily set refs/remotes/origin/HEAD. Worth checking whether the fix belongs in the clone (set origin/HEAD) as well as in the resolver (stop swallowing the failure).
CODE RE-REVIEW 2026-08-23. Root cause found in the tree, and it is stronger than the bead's guess.

ROOT CAUSE, VERIFIED: RepoCache.clone_branch clones the env's ports checkout with
  git clone --single-branch --branch <branch> <mirror> <dest>
--single-branch does not create refs/remotes/origin/HEAD. So the resolver's stated premise — 'rare; clones from a mirror usually have it' — is false BY CONSTRUCTION for every env dev-env builds. Not rare, universal. The bead listed this as a likely cause to confirm; it is confirmed, in repos.py, not just inferred from the x6 symptom.

CHOSEN FIX: resolve from the branch actually checked out in PORTS_MAIN_DIR —
  git -C /work/ports-main rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD
Correct because clone_branch checks out exactly state.repos.deltaports_branch. Safe because nothing detaches that HEAD: sync.py's reset_env_repo does 'reset --hard <sha>' on the current branch (moves the branch pointer, stays symbolic) and update.py fast-forwards. Both were checked, and both already address PORTS_MAIN_RELATIVE explicitly with comments about not going through the symlink — the dev-env side already learned this lesson; only the agent resolver missed it. Works on EXISTING envs, which a clone-side fix would not.

NO SILENT DEFAULT: failure, empty output, or a literal 'HEAD' (detached) all mean resolution failed. Returned as a failure result rather than raised, matching the module's result-dict style: create_job_worktree returns ok=False with a clear error, and under poly-m7o the job is then retired worktree_unavailable instead of being cut from a guessed base. The two changes compose — a job never silently builds on the wrong base.

CACHE KEPT but only for successful resolutions. Its rationale still holds (a subprocess per call, and an env's base does not change during its lifetime); the bug was caching a value derived from a failed read.

CONSIDERED AND REJECTED — reading state.repos.deltaports_branch from the env state. More declarative, but couples the agent worker to the dev-env state schema and would disagree with reality if anyone switched branches in the env. 'What is actually checked out' is the better authority.

CONSIDERED AND DEFERRED — also setting origin/HEAD at clone time (git remote set-head). It would repair mirror semantics, but only for NEW envs, and nothing else in the tree consumes origin/HEAD for the ports tree (grepped: only this function). Worth doing if another consumer ever appears.

TESTS TO UPDATE: three files pin the current behaviour — test_changes_diff_semantics.py, test_dev_env_job_worktree.py, test_bundle_branch_lifecycle.py.
IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-23.

_resolve_bundle_base_branch now reads 'git -C /work/ports-main rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD' and returns str | None. A failed command, empty output, or a literal 'HEAD' (detached) all return None. create_job_worktree refuses with ok=False and a plain error rather than guessing, which under poly-m7o retires the job worktree_unavailable — so a job can never silently build on the wrong base. Only successful reads are cached.

TEST THAT PINNED THE BUG: test_base_branch_fallback_to_master asserted the '|| echo master' behaviour as intended, with a docstring explaining it. Replaced. Worth noting the bug had a passing test defending it.

A GAP IN MY OWN TEST, found by mutation: 'failures are not cached' initially passed even with the guard moved after the cache write, because a failed command yields base='' and the cache lookup is truthiness-based, so an empty value never sticks. The case that actually matters is detached HEAD — 'HEAD' is truthy, so it WOULD survive in the cache and be returned as a branch name forever after. The test is now parametrized over all three failure shapes and asserts the cache stays empty.

TOOLING HAZARD worth remembering: the first mutation run reported a false pass and then a false failure on restore. Cause was stale .pyc — the script rewrote worker.py fast enough that CPython's mtime+size invalidation did not trip. Mutation runs now clear __pycache__ between steps. Any earlier mutation result in this repo taken without clearing bytecode is suspect.

Five mutations, all caught after the fix: restoring the silent master fallback, reading the symlink instead of ports-main, accepting a detached HEAD, caching failures, and letting worktree creation proceed without a base. 2150 tests pass.

NOT YET VERIFIED ON x6 — needs the commit pushed so the test clone can pull. Expect: resolution returns 'master' for the right reason (rev-parse, not a fallback), and pointing ports-main at a detached HEAD makes create_job_worktree refuse.
VERIFIED ON x6 2026-08-23 against the live 2026Q3-editors_vim env.

A. ROOT CAUSE VISIBLE IN THE ENV'S OWN GIT CONFIG:
     remote.origin.fetch = +refs/heads/master:refs/remotes/origin/master
   A single-branch refspec — exactly what 'git clone --single-branch' writes, and why refs/remotes/origin/HEAD is absent ('fatal: ref refs/remotes/origin/HEAD is not a symbolic ref', still). So the old resolver's read fails on this env today, and '|| echo master' was supplying every answer. This is the root cause confirmed from the env side, independently of reading repos.py.

B. The resolver now returns 'master' via rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD — the right answer for the right reason rather than by coincidence.

C. Refusal path exercised for real: detached ports-main HEAD -> _resolve_bundle_base_branch returned None and create_job_worktree returned ok=False with 'could not determine the base branch from /work/ports-main ... (detached HEAD, or the checkout is unreadable)'. No guess, no worktree. ports-main restored to master afterwards; env left clean.

All three acceptance criteria met.

title: Worktree-creation soft-fail can run a job against another job's tree
description:
_checkout_bundle_branch_for_job (runner.py:2720) is soft-fail by design: if create_job_worktree fails the job PROCEEDS. That rationale predates B1 and its docstring still describes the pre-B1 world — 'falls back to pre-Step-30 behavior (commits land on whatever branch is current)'. That was safe when the fallback was one shared checkout sitting on some branch.

After B1 the fallback is different in kind. create_job_worktree returns BEFORE _point_ports_link when 'worktree add' fails (worker.py:1588-1594), so /work/DeltaPorts keeps whatever it pointed at. Normally that is ports-main, because destroy_job_worktree repoints on job end. But if a previous job crashed or its teardown failed, the link still points at THAT job's worktree — so this job's agent edits a dead job's tree and its commits land on the dead job's branch. Cross-job contamination, which is the exact thing B1 exists to prevent.

NOT HYPOTHETICAL: create_job_worktree returned ok=False twice during B1 bring-up, both on the first call after deploying new code, never reproduced across 12 fresh cycles and never explained. The soft-fail path has fired for real.

CANDIDATE FIXES, not chosen: (a) hard-fail the job when the worktree cannot be created — the trade-off the original rationale rejected, but the cost of proceeding is now much higher than 'lost isolation'; (b) force the link to the idle target (ports-main) before proceeding, so a soft-fail degrades to the main checkout rather than to an arbitrary dead job's tree; (c) assert the link resolves to this job's worktree before any worker.* call.

(b) is the smallest change that removes the contamination while keeping the original soft-fail intent.

Also update the stale docstring rationale in runner.py:2731-2739 whichever way this lands.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A failed worktree creation cannot leave a job editing another job's tree. 2. The soft-fail rationale in _checkout_bundle_branch_for_job describes post-B1 behaviour. 3. The verify/confirm path (_checkout_verify_branch_for_job) gets the same treatment or a documented reason it differs.
notes:
CORRECTION 2026-08-23 — the recommendation above is WRONG. Do not implement option (b).

Option (b) was 'force the link to the idle target (ports-main) before proceeding, so a soft-fail degrades to the main checkout'. I wrote that without reading what the worktree cuts from. Having now read it:

  * create_job_worktree takes base from _resolve_bundle_base_branch, which returns a LOCAL BRANCH NAME (master by default), and cuts new bundle branches from it.
  * commit_port_changes runs 'cd /work/DeltaPorts && git add -A && git commit', i.e. into whatever the symlink points at, on whatever branch that tree has checked out.

So pointing the link at ports-main means the agent's commits land on the base branch itself — the branch every future worktree cuts from. That converts a single job's contamination into permanent poisoning of the base for all subsequent jobs. Strictly worse than the bug being fixed.

THERE IS NO SAFE FALLBACK TREE. That is the finding. Option (a), hard-fail, is the fix: no worktree, no job. A DEAD job is re-enqueueable; silent contamination is not detectable. The original soft-fail rationale ('failing hard would regress bundles that would otherwise run fine') assumed a benign fallback that B1 removed.

CRITERION 3 IS ALREADY SATISFIED, also unchecked when I wrote it: _checkout_verify_branch_for_job is explicitly NOT soft-fail and its docstring already gives the reason it differs — a failed checkout makes any verify verdict meaningless. Only the patch/convert path needs the change.

SEPARATE BUG FOUND WHILE CHECKING THIS, filed as its own bead: _resolve_bundle_base_branch resolves the base by cd-ing into /work/DeltaPorts (the agent-facing symlink) instead of PORTS_MAIN_DIR, swallows failure into '|| echo master', and caches per env.
IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-23 as hard-fail.

_checkout_bundle_branch_for_job now returns bool. process_patch_job retires the job (and its siblings) on False via a new lifecycle event, WORKTREE_UNAVAILABLE -> DEAD, retire_reason 'worktree_unavailable', and returns (False, 'worktree_unavailable') so the file lands in failed/ with an error note.

WHY A NEW EVENT RATHER THAN REUSING ONE — checked the consumers rather than assuming:
  * ENV_BROKEN feeds the health contract and decision.py's 'defer until healthy'. A git failure is not a broken env.
  * PATCH_GAVE_UP sets retire_reason 'patch_gave_up', which decision.py counts as a failed patch attempt to decide escalation. Machinery failures counted there would suppress future work on the port.
Two tests assert the new reason stays out of both signals.

STATE IT FIRES FROM: PATCHING. PATCH_START fires before the checkout in process_job, verified rather than assumed (patch_gave_up's only from-state is 'patching'). Transitions also added from CLAIMED and TRIAGED so a future earlier caller retires cleanly instead of hitting an IllegalTransition, which _apply_transition swallows.

A BUG THE TESTS CAUGHT: the call site referenced JobEvent, which is not bound at module scope in runner.py — every use is a local import. The module still imported fine because the reference sits inside a function body; only executing the path raises NameError. The call-site test executes it, and mutation-testing confirmed removing the import fails that test.

EXISTING TESTS I HAD TO CHANGE, disclosed: six tests in test_runner_orchestrator_parity.py broke, because create_job_worktree raises in the test env (no $DPORTSV3_CMD) and soft-fail used to absorb it. I stubbed create_job_worktree/destroy_job_worktree in that fixture, alongside the existing assert_port_clean stub and for the same stated reason — those tests exercise the orchestrator event chain, not worktree provisioning. Worth being clear this weakened them slightly rather than pretending they passed untouched.

ACCEPTED TRADE-OFF, NOT SOLVED: worktree_unavailable is terminal. A transient git failure now kills a job that would previously have run, and recovery is an operator re-enqueue from the bundle. That is the deliberate choice — a dead job is visible and recoverable, silent cross-job contamination is neither — but whether this class of failure should instead be retryable is a real question I did not answer. The queue has no retry mechanism I verified.

NOT VERIFIED IN A REAL CHROOT (poly-4kr). Everything above is unit-level plus mutation testing.
PARTIALLY VERIFIED ON x6 2026-08-23. The helper's contract holds against a real chroot: _checkout_bundle_branch_for_job returned False for an env that cannot produce a worktree (logged 'worktree add for bundle/b1 failed'), and True as a no-op when bundle_id is absent.

NOT verified: the call site retiring a real patch job worktree_unavailable, which still needs a live LLM job (poly-4kr).

title: Two in-chroot call sites still located the tool in the ports tree (runner could not start)
description:
Missed by the X5/X6 repository split. Both invoked the wrapper as "$DELTAPORTS_ROOT/dportsv3", which is two mistakes at once: DELTAPORTS_ROOT is the ports tree, not the tool checkout, and in this repo the repo-root 'dportsv3' name belongs to the Python package rather than the wrapper (the wrapper is bin/dportsv3). layout.py:50 documents that exact trap; these two consumers were not repointed.

  * health.py:236 _check_dports_compose — SEVERITY: total. sh returns 127, the check reports broken, _aggregate turns any broken check into a broken env, and _gate_blocked pauses the whole runner loop. The runner could not process a single job in any env built after the split.
  * worker.py:1746 validate_dops — the convert agent's cheap dsl check always failed.

Confirmed /work/DeltaPorts/dportsv3 does not exist post-split by inspecting a real DeltaPorts checkout: the repo has no dportsv3 at its root, so there was no stale vendored copy masking this.

CORROBORATING SIGNAL, worth remembering as a smell: build_env_dict has exported POLYTROPOS_ROOT since the split (helpers.py:148) and NOTHING consumed it except the showenv helper and tests. A new env var with no readers meant the consumers were never repointed.

WHY THE X5 VERIFICATION MISSED IT: criterion 5 was verified on x6 by provisioning an env, not by running the runner loop. Provisioning uses TOOL_BIN and is correct; the health gate and the agent tool path are only exercised once the runner actually starts, which poly-4kr blocks.

FIXED: both call sites now use "$POLYTROPOS_ROOT/bin/dportsv3". tests/test_chroot_tool_path.py greps the whole agent package for the old shape and asserts the built command text for both helpers; mutation-tested by reverting each fix.

STILL OPEN, low priority: docs/agentic-architecture-backlog.md:1214 shows the old invocation. Historical design record, but a copy-paste re-infection source.

NOT VERIFIED IN A REAL CHROOT — no way to run the services yet (poly-4kr). The fix is a path correction with a unit guard; an end-to-end confirmation still owes.
acceptance_criteria: 1. No agent-package call site locates the wrapper under the ports tree. 2. A post-split env passes the compose health check so the runner does not pause. 3. Verified in a real chroot once poly-4kr unblocks.
notes:
AUDIT 2026-08-23. Everything in this bead was verified by reading the code, checking a real DeltaPorts checkout for the absent wrapper, and mutation-testing the guard — with one exception already stated: the fix has NOT been confirmed in a real chroot, because poly-4kr blocks running the services.

Line numbers are stale post-fix: the call sites are _check_dports_compose in health.py and validate_dops in worker.py.
VERIFIED ON x6 2026-08-23 — acceptance criterion 3 met, the fix is confirmed on real hardware.

In the live env 2026Q3-editors_vim:
  DELTAPORTS_ROOT=/work/DeltaPorts   POLYTROPOS_ROOT=/work/polytropos
  old path $DELTAPORTS_ROOT/dportsv3      -> MISSING
  new path $POLYTROPOS_ROOT/bin/dportsv3  -> EXISTS

health.check() now returns STATUS: ready with dports_compose ok ('dportsv3 3.0.0-dev'). Before the fix that check returned broken, _aggregate turned the env broken and _gate_blocked paused the runner outright, so this confirms both the bug and the fix on hardware.

title: reconcile/diff_tree silently miss content changes: _DeepDircmp.phase3 override never runs
description: fsutils._DeepDircmp overrides phase3 to force cmpfiles(shallow=False) so classification is content-based. The override is NEVER CALLED. filecmp.dircmp.methodmap is built in the class body and captures the BASE class function objects; dircmp.__getattr__ dispatches via self.methodmap[attr](self), which invokes dircmp.phase3, not the subclass override. Verified on Python 3.11.12 (DragonFly x6) and 3.11.14 (macOS): methodmap['same_files'] is <function dircmp.phase3>, and two files with equal size+mtime but different content classify as same_files. Consequence: reconcile() skips the copy and diff_tree() reports no difference, so a real content change is silently lost. Masked on macOS/APFS because nanosecond mtime makes consecutive writes differ (1787237401268667053 vs ...740553), so the accidental shallow compare still sees a diff. Exposed on DragonFly/HAMMER2 where consecutive writes share an mtime (both 1787237404520528000) - the production platform. Realistic trigger: a same-length edit such as DISTVERSION=1.2.3 -> 1.2.4 written in one tick would not propagate to the live composed tree. Surfaced as 3 suite failures on x6: test_fsutils_reconcile.py::test_content_change_updates_dst, ::test_symlinks_with_different_content_replaced, test_fsutils_diff_tree.py::test_content_difference_is_reported.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Content-based classification actually runs - do not rely on overriding phase3. 2) A regression test pins the failure mode directly: equal size AND equal mtime, different content, must classify as a difference on every platform (force mtimes equal with os.utime so it fails on macOS too, rather than depending on filesystem granularity). 3) The three x6 failures pass. 4) Audit other dircmp/filecmp subclassing for the same methodmap trap.
notes: Hash correction: the fix commit is 4af664d (referenced as 06546ff before the attribution trailer was stripped and the unpushed commits rewritten).
close_reason: Fixed in 06546ff. _DeepDircmp.phase3 was never invoked (dircmp.methodmap binds base-class functions); the three attributes are now filled eagerly in __init__ so they shadow the lazy dispatch. Regression tests force equal size+mtime via os.utime so they fail on macOS too, not only on HAMMER2. Mutation-tested: both new tests fail with the fix disabled. Also corrected test_content_change_updates_dst, whose mtime assertion was itself granularity-dependent. 2089 passed on macOS 3.11.14 and DragonFly 3.11.12.

title: X5 Chroot: provision from two repos, keep /work/DeltaPorts unchanged
description:
The deepest coupling. Re-verified 2026-08-20 against the post-split tree; the
original notes were written pre-X8 and are corrected here.

WHAT BREAKS FIRST (not previously recorded): builder.py:154 validates the ports
tree by requiring a `dportsv3` file inside --delta-root ("Delta root does not
look like this repo") — a fossil from when the tool and the ports tree were one
checkout. X8 deleted DeltaPorts/dportsv3, so `dev-env create` now fails at
validation, before mirrors, chroot or venv. The venv failure described below is
unreachable until this is fixed.

THEN: dev-env clones exactly one repo to work/DeltaPorts (update.py:33-36
ENV_REPOS, builder.py:111), installs the generator venv from inside that
checkout (venv.py:24 requires work/DeltaPorts/scripts/generator/pyproject.toml,
venv.py:33 installs to .../.venv) and probes readiness with
/work/DeltaPorts/dportsv3 compose --help (venv.py:50, 72).

CORRECTION: hooks.py:50 is already fixed. X1 replaced the parents-walk with
package-local data in repo_hook_source(). Nothing to do there.

ALSO MISSING FROM THE ORIGINAL LIST:
- repos.py:13-27 RepoMirrors is a frozen 3-field dataclass with no slot for the
  tool repo; refresh_all() mirrors exactly 3 repos.
- state.py:24-25 SourceState has only delta_root — nowhere to record which tool
  checkout an env was built from.
- sync.py:15,91 GENERATOR_VENV_RELATIVE = scripts/generator/.venv, a dead path
  used to exclude the venv from git clean.
- builder.py:158-163 the dirty check and --allow-dirty cover only the ports
  checkout; post-split it is TOOL dirtiness that decides what reaches the chroot.

CRITICAL CONSTRAINT (unchanged): /work/DeltaPorts must keep meaning 'the ports
tree'. It is the agent's only legal edit surface — hardcoded in LLM prompt text
(prompts.py:146-360, tools.py:118) and enforced by guardrails that reject other
prefixes (worker.py:213, 251-258). The ports tree stays; the TOOL gets a second
path. cli.py:327,413,440,475 operate on the ports overlay and are correct as-is.

DESIGN AGREED:
- Tool repo reaches the chroot by mirroring the host polytropos checkout via the
  existing refresh_local_mirror, symmetric with delta_root. Keeps dev-env's
  purpose — testing local tool edits in a chroot — intact.
- In-chroot tool path is /work/polytropos (matches the repo name; avoids a
  second rename when dportsv3 -> polytropos lands).
- Host discovery: --tool-root, then $DPORTS_DEV_TOOL_ROOT, then raise —
  mirroring default_delta_root() at builder.py:226-252. bin/dportsv3 exports the
  variable; paths.py:31-34 already names the wrapper as the one component
  entitled to know repo layout, so no parents-walk enters a package.
- Venv cache key hashes BOTH pyproject.toml files. bin/dportsv3:193 notes the
  generator venv contains dev-env too, so hashing only the generator pyproject
  would silently reuse a stale venv when dev-env deps change.
- State schema 1 -> 2, hard cutover: fail loudly on schema 1 telling the operator
  to recreate. No migration — pre-split envs cannot work post-split anyway. The
  x6 2026Q3 reference chroot is expendable (confirmed with the operator).

REMAINING SURFACES: builder.py:110-114,154,158-163,195,200; venv.py:24,29,33,50,72;
repos.py:13-27; update.py:33-36; state.py:17-25; sync.py:15; helpers.py:28,30,69,
138,151-152,182; cli.py:27,35 (--delta-root help text is stale, add --tool-root);
dsynth-hooks/dportsv3-hooks.conf.example:36; bin/dportsv3 (export the variable).

OUT OF SCOPE, follow-up bead: sync-dirty for the tool repo. Resetting the tool
checkout invalidates the generator venv and needs a rebuild path; not in the
acceptance criteria.

TEST REALITY: builder.py, venv.py, repos.py, update.py and sync.py have no test
coverage — only 7 test files touch dports_dev_env and none of them these. A green
suite proves nothing here; criterion 5 on x6 is the real validation.
acceptance_criteria:
1. dev-env create provisions both repos into a chroot.
2. /work/DeltaPorts still resolves to the ports tree and every agent guardrail
   and prompt path is unchanged.
3. The generator venv is built from the tool repo, with a readiness probe that
   targets the new tool path.
4. In-chroot helpers, hook config and DELTAPORTS_ROOT are consistent with the
   new layout.
5. The tool runs end to end in a freshly provisioned chroot: compose and
   reapply from /work/polytropos against /work/DeltaPorts.

Criterion 5 originally read "a real agent job runs end to end". Narrowed
2026-08-21: that exercises the agentic loop, which needs services this repo has
no supported way to run — a separate gap, filed on its own, not something this
layout change owns or can be blocked on.
notes:
Criterion 5 run on x6 (DragonFly 6.5), 2026-08-20. Criteria 1-4 proven on real
hardware; the agent-job half of criterion 5 is NOT done.

PROVEN:
- create provisions both repos: /work/DeltaPorts and /work/polytropos side by
  side; the ports tree has ports/ and special/ and does NOT contain the tool.
- venv builds from the tool repo at /work/polytropos/.venv via the TOOL_BIN
  probe on first create, and restored from cache on the second — the key works
  across creates.
- compose in-chroot: applied=9544, which is exactly the with---lock-root
  baseline from 7ac5fb7 (the degraded path gives 9531). 136 errors, all ports
  content drift (patch conflicts, ambiguous _AR/_RANLIB), no layout errors.
- reapply editors/vim in-chroot: exit 0, cwd=/work/DeltaPorts, tool invoked
  from /work/polytropos.
- guardrails unchanged: worker.py still gates on /work/DeltaPorts/ports/.
- status reports both checkouts with branch/commit/dirty.
- schema-1 cutover: the pre-split 2026Q3 env read as invalid in list and
  destroy cleaned it via the partial-env path without stranding it.

FOUND AND FIXED, only visible by running it:
- 2c63825 initial_state() hardcoded schema=1, so every env was unreadable the
  moment it was saved. create never re-reads its own state, so it reported
  success and the next command failed. Test added.
- e17a8be showenv grepped ^DPORTS_ only, so neither source root appeared.

NOT DONE: "a real agent job runs end to end in a freshly provisioned chroot."
Needs the agentic LLM loop with credentials on x6; not attempted.

x6 state: env 2026Q3-editors_vim is ready. The checkout there carries an
uncommitted copy of builder.py/helpers.py matching 2c63825 and e17a8be, since
those are unpushed; a pull will clear it. Created with --allow-dirty for that
reason.

title: X3 Prove the seam: run the tool from outside the ports repo
description: The go/no-go gate before touching git history. With X1+X2 done, the tool should already be able to operate on a ports tree it does not live in. Run compose, migration inventory, the tracker and the full test suite with the tool checked out at a path unrelated to the ports repo, pointing at DeltaPorts via the explicit delta_root. This is what proves the extraction is mechanical rather than a rewrite. Includes fixing the tests that reach across the boundary: test_hook_record_result_alignment.py (reads scripts/dsynth-hooks), test_decision_parity.py (reads config/), test_worker_guardrails.py + test_worker_hooks_disabled.py (parents[3] walks), and the 5 test_dev_env_*.py that import across packages.
acceptance_criteria: 1) compose --delta-root <ports repo> produces byte-identical output to running in-tree. 2) Full suite green with the tool outside the ports repo. 3) No test reaches out of the tool repo except through the configured delta_root. 4) Documented as the supported way to run the tool.
notes:
CRITERION 1 VERIFIED (2026-08-20, DragonFly x6.sector.int 6.5-DEVELOPMENT): compose from the extracted repo is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the in-tree tool.

METHOD. Two detached worktrees of DeltaPorts at 1f1ee8b9d3a (the last commit that still contained the toolchain; 75dee579255 is its child and removed it). Separate worktree per run because compose WRITES BACK into the delta root - each run mutated 31 files marking stale overlays removed_in - so a shared input would have silently corrupted run B.
  Run A (in-tree, pre-split): cd <worktreeA> && ./dportsv3 compose --target @2026Q3 --output out-intree --freebsd-root ~/s/freebsd-ports --lock-root ~/s/dports   (delta-root defaults to cwd)
  Run B (extracted repo):     cd ~/s/polytropos && ./bin/dportsv3 compose --target @2026Q3 --delta-root <worktreeB> --output out-newrepo --freebsd-root ~/s/freebsd-ports --lock-root ~/s/dports

CONTROLS. 'git diff 1f1ee8b9d3a 75dee579255 -- ports special' is EMPTY, so ports data is identical across the split; the deletion commit touched only tooling (386 scripts/, 43 docs/, 5 .claude/, 2 config/). Both runs used the same freebsd-ports (branch 2026Q3) and the same ~/s/dports lock root. The tool is therefore the only variable.

RESULT. diff -qr over both trees: 0 differences, exit 0. Entries 228979 = 228979. Path lists (find | sort) identical. files=180451 symlinks=0 dirs=48527 on both. Apparent bytes 587673075 = 587673075. 'du -sh' showed 335M vs 333M, which is HAMMER2 transparent compression, not content - apparent size is identical to the byte.
Comparison deliberately used diff -r, NOT the tool's own fsutils.diff_tree, which poly-mdx shows is broken.

SIDE RESULTS. (a) Both tools reported ops=9567 applied=9544 fallback=46 errors=134 with the same breakdown (E_COMPOSE_COMPAT_FAILED=32, E_COMPOSE_STALE_OVERLAY=31, E_COMPOSE_APPLY_FAILED=3), so the 134 compose errors are PRE-EXISTING ports drift, not extraction damage. (b) The extracted tool resolved config from polytropos/config via DPORTSV3_CONFIG_DIR while the in-tree tool used DeltaPorts/config - different config dirs, identical output.

CRITERION 3 ALSO VERIFIED: full suite run on x6 with DPORTS_DELTA_ROOT UNSET gives the same 2082 passed / 3 failed as with it set, so no test depends on the ports repo. Remaining parents[N] walks in tests are parents[1] = tool repo root, which does not leave the tool repo.

STILL OPEN: criterion 2 (3 failures, all poly-mdx, a pre-existing filecmp bug that reproduces on macOS too - not an extraction regression) and criterion 4 (poly-3ze). See also poly-170 for the DragonFly dev-install blocker.

ARTIFACTS left in place on x6 for re-running after poly-mdx: ~/x3-parity/{DeltaPorts-presplit,DeltaPorts-forB,out-intree,out-newrepo} (~1.6G) plus two worktree registrations in ~/s/DeltaPorts/.git/worktrees/. Remove with 'git -C ~/s/DeltaPorts worktree remove' x2 and rm -rf ~/x3-parity.

title: X2 Break the bidirectional generator<->dev-env sys.path bridge
description: The two distributions import each other at runtime by mutating sys.path, with no declared dependency either way. Verified: env_resolver.py:52-62 inserts parents[3]/tools/dev-env and imports dports_dev_env.config/store; cli.py:884 (dev-env) inserts parents[3]/generator and imports dportsv3.agent.health; health.py:45 reads the dev-env's runtime-profiles.toml. All three assume generator/ and tools/dev-env/ are siblings under one scripts/ dir — which is exactly what extraction changes. pyproject files also cross-pin jsonschema by hand-written comment rather than a real dependency.
acceptance_criteria: 1) No sys.path mutation between the two packages. 2) The dependency direction is declared and acyclic (either dev-env depends on the generator, or the shared piece — env resolution / runtime profiles — moves to a package both can import). 3) jsonschema pinning is expressed once, not duplicated in a comment. 4) Each package imports cleanly with the other absent.
close_reason: Declared dportsv3 -> dports-dev-env, acyclic. Reverse edge (dev-env health CLI shim) moved to 'dportsv3 env-health'. Manifest moved into the package, ships in a wheel. jsonschema pin dropped from both (dead in code). Suite 53 -> 11 failures; remainder is X1. Commit fdba90e in ~/s/polytropos.

title: X1 De-couple path discovery (in place, repo still works)
description:
Do this BEFORE any file moves — it is the bulk of the work and is independently valuable. Every place the tool finds something by walking out of its own directory must take an explicit, configured path instead. Verified sites: runner.py:89 + _manual_test_triage_tier.py:182 (parents[4]/config -> agentic-policy.json), delivery/config.py:258 (delivery.token), delivery/orchestrator.py:92 (delivery.toml), snippets.py:15 (scripts/snippet-extractor), worker.py:52 + verify_fix.py:132 (parents[4]/dportsv3 wrapper), health.py:45 (parents[3]/tools/dev-env/runtime-profiles.toml), playbooks.py:345 (ancestor walk for docs/agent-playbooks), cli.py:60/210/235/261/370 (--delta-root defaults to Path('.')), builder.py:225 default_delta_root()=parents[4].

playbooks.py is the dangerous one: it returns None on failure, so after a move the agent silently loses all pattern knowledge with no error. Every one of these must fail LOUDLY or be explicitly configured.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A single documented resolution order per input (CLI flag > env var > config > packaged default), no parents[N] walking out of the package. 2) delta_root (the ports tree) is explicit — never Path('.') by accident. 3) Missing playbooks/policy/config raises or logs a clear error; nothing degrades silently. 4) Tool data that is really tool-owned (agent-playbooks, dops_quickref.md) ships as package data. 5) Suite green with the repo unmoved.
close_reason: Single resolver dportsv3/paths.py. Tool-owned data (playbooks, config templates, dsynth hooks, snippet extractor) moved into the packages; site-owned inputs named via env/flag. All raise instead of returning None. Verified via non-editable wheel install resolving everything from /. Suite 2085 passed, zero parents[N] walks left. Commit df9a668.

title: Worklist has no landing place for issues knocked off the happy path
description:
The issue worklist (/agentic, build_issue_worklist) silently loses or mislabels issues that leave the accept->deliver happy path. Two verified cases, one root cause: issue_bucket derives the band from the ACTIONABLE OCCURRENCE's resolution, so anything that changes the issue without changing its bundle (or blanks the bundle) lands wrong.

CASE 1 — red confirm build still reads 'Awaiting delivery'. reopen_issue_build_failed sets state='unresolved' and nulls delivery_bundle_id but does NOT touch the bundle, whose resolution stays 'accepted'. issue_bucket falls through and returns 'delivering' for occ_key=='accepted'. So a red confirm moves the issue from one looks-fixed band (resolving) to another (awaiting delivery) instead of 'decide'. A3's stated goal — stop an unfixed issue looking as good as fixed — is defeated. The only real signal is manual_handoff.md on a bundle the operator has no reason to open.

CASE 2 — operator bundle-reopen makes the issue VANISH. Reopening a bundle sets bundles.resolution to NULL -> fix_state.fix_status = 'unknown' -> worklist_bucket = None -> issue_bucket returns None -> build_issue_worklist DROPS it (issue_state.py:257-258, 'Issues that aren't operator-actionable right now (bucket None) are omitted'). The issue disappears from /agentic entirely and is only findable on /agentic/issues. Bucket None means 'the runner is working it, nothing to do yet', which is exactly wrong for an issue an operator just reopened by hand.

Reproduced live on the demo DB: iss-queued and iss-redconfirm both sat at bucket=None and were absent from the dashboard worklist while still listed on /agentic/issues. Confirmed via the events audit log that the state writes themselves were all correct — this is purely a projection/UX hole, not state corruption.

Compounding UX factor: there are two different Reopen buttons (bundle-level and issue-level) whose effects differ (bundle reopen never changes issue state), with nothing in the UI explaining which one moves what.
acceptance_criteria: 1) An issue whose confirm build went red lands in an actionable band (decide), not delivering. 2) An issue whose bundle an operator reopened stays VISIBLE in the worklist in an actionable band, instead of being dropped by the bucket-None rule. 3) Decide whether the bundle's resolution should move off 'accepted' when its confirm build fails. 4) Bucket None is reserved for genuinely runner-owned work; operator-touched issues never fall into it. 5) The red verdict + handoff are reachable from the issue, not only from the bundle artifact. 6) The two Reopen actions are distinguishable in the UI (what each one moves). 7) Tests pin the bucket for (a) reopened-by-red-confirm and (b) operator-reopened bundle.
close_reason: Fixed: unknown -> decide (bucket None now reserved for runner-owned work), and accepted-occurrence-on-open-issue -> decide (stale pre-resolving branch). Plus 'confirming' added to _INFLIGHT_JOB_STATES. Demo worklist 4/8 -> 8/8.

title: Confirm loop: duplicate builds on restart / lock contention / multi-runner
description: Adversarial review found 3 verified double-enqueue paths, each costing a full dsynth build. (a) RESTART: _reset_building_markers clears every building_generation at startup, but a confirm job sitting in pending/ SURVIVES — reap_orphans deliberately leaves QUEUED claimable (lifecycle.py:476 'QUEUED stays queued') and reap_stale_queued only reaps rows whose .job file is missing. So the old job is still claimable AND the feed enqueues a fresh one: two builds, two greens, and with the A4 threshold of 2 the issue resolves on what was effectively one requested confirmation. (b) NON-ATOMIC MARK: process_build_requests enqueues the job file and only then calls _mark_issue_building, which swallows sqlite3.Error and returns silently when the conn is None. If the tracker holds the write lock past busy_timeout the marker is never set, nothing is logged, and the next loop pass (<=5s) enqueues a duplicate. (c) MULTI-RUNNER: a second runner's startup sweep wipes the first runner's live in-flight markers.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A queued-but-unclaimed confirm job is reconciled on restart rather than duplicated (reap it, or make the marker sweep aware of pending confirm jobs). 2) Enqueue+mark is atomic, or the mark failing prevents/undoes the enqueue and is logged. 3) Multi-runner startup does not clear another live runner's markers. 4) Tests cover all three.
close_reason: Fixed the two in-scope paths: claim-before-enqueue (CAS, failed claim never enqueues) and coherent restart sweep (discard queued confirm jobs + clear markers, then re-derive). Multi-runner filed separately as a pre-existing system-wide gap.

title: Confirm loop: issue stuck in resolving on permanently-doomed builds
description: A machinery gave-up deliberately leaves building_generation set to avoid hot-looping a broken env, and ONLY the startup _reset_building_markers clears it. Consequences verified: (a) a long-lived runner parks the issue in resolving forever with no retry, no backoff and no operator-visible signal beyond one activity row; recovery requires a human restarting the runner, which is documented nowhere operator-facing. (b) PERMANENTLY-DOOMED builds loop: run_verify_fix raises VerifyFixError when the bundle has no changes.diff or it is empty (verify_fix.py:206-215), and the dispatch raises when no dev-env is available — so every restart clears the marker, re-enqueues, raises again, re-sets the marker. The issue never leaves resolving and each restart burns a job. Operator escape hatch does exist (manual resolve/reopen are allowed from resolving, issue_state.py:59-60) but is undiscoverable. Overlaps C4 (per-key backoff).
acceptance_criteria: 1) A doomed confirm (missing/empty changes.diff, no dev-env) is detected and does not retry indefinitely — terminal state + operator signal. 2) A stalled in-flight marker is recoverable without a runner restart. 3) The operator can see WHY an issue is parked in resolving. 4) Coordinate with C4 backoff so the two do not conflict.
close_reason: Fixed: machinery failures now clear the marker and retry without a restart, bounded by DP_CONFIRM_MAX_FAILURES (default 3), after which the issue is reopened with a manual handoff. Pacing (per-key backoff) remains C4.

title: A2 Green -> resolved (build-confirmed) + Green Head
description: A2 Green -> resolved (build-confirmed). On a green confirm build, advance the issue resolving->resolved and record the Green-Head build ordinal per (target,origin). Read-only on build_* (reads port_status).
design:
## Design

On a GREEN confirm-build verdict (from A1's report-back), make the build — not the
merge — the authority that resolves the issue.

**Transition:** in the confirm-build report-back handler, when verdict=green for the
issue currently in `resolving`:
- `state: resolving -> resolved`, `resolved_at = now`, source `'build-confirmed'`
  (reuse the `resolve_issue` writer, issue_actions.py:83, or an inline UPDATE with
  the same shape/event).
- GUARD: only from `state='resolving'` (mirror `mark_issue_resolving`'s
  `WHERE state IN (...)`, issue_actions.py:112) so a muted / unresolved / already-
  resolved issue is untouched.
- advance `last_confirmed_build_generation = generation`, clear `building_generation`.

**Green Head:** record the build ordinal at which (target, origin) went green — from
`port_status.last_success_run_id` / `build_runs.id` (schema.py:384/355). Store it as
`green_head_run_id` on the issue (new column) or a small `issue_green_head` side
row. This is the "known-good boundary" C3 derives `regressed` against (a later build
re-emitting the fingerprint at an ordinal > green head = regression).

**Authority shift (the point of the feature):** today `delivery_sync.py:148`
(`set_bundle_merged_resolution`) flips `resolved` on PR merge. A2 moves that
authority to the green build. For the MVP, merge becomes an OBSERVATION that no
