The "single writer" claim was asserted in shipped code, not just the
backlog doc: db/schema.py (module docstring + the issues-table SQL
comment), artifact_store.py, tracker/db.py ("two writers") and
AGENTIC_BUILDS.md. All corrected to "three processes, serialized by
WAL". artifact_store.py also referenced a scripts/artifact-store path
that does not exist.
design:
No change to the on-disk layout (artifact_root, objects/sha256/...) or to
the wire contract of the /v1/ endpoints — only the host:port they live
on. Keep the /v1/ paths verbatim to minimise client churn.

31a — mount the artifact-store endpoints on the FastAPI app, and
make content-addressing single-sourced.
Port /v1/artifacts/{get,put,put-fs}, /v1/bundles/upsert,
/v1/jobs/transition and /v1/user-context to FastAPI routes calling the
existing ArtifactStore class in-process. Define the blob put routes as
sync `def` so FastAPI dispatches them in its threadpool and a large
upload cannot block the async UI/event loop.

The tracker becomes the process that WRITES the blobstore, so the dedup
path moves with the fold: sha256_bytes, blob_path, the "skip the write
if the object already exists" check in put_blob and the ON
CONFLICT(sha256) DO NOTHING on blob_objects are the tracker's code now,
not a neighbouring service's. Delete resolve_artifact_path's inline copy
of the layout and have it call blob_path, so one function owns where a
blob lives on disk and the FileResponse path cannot drift from the put
path.

31b — repoint clients. Collapse artifact_store_get /
tracker_artifact_get into one function and delete the fallback.

NOT a collapse of ARTIFACT_STORE_URL into DPORTSV3_TRACKER_URL. The hook
keeps posting to loopback permanently — see the relay note below — so
ARTIFACT_STORE_URL stays 127.0.0.1 in every env's hooks conf and it is
the RUNNER that learns the tracker URL. One knob leaves every env's conf
and lands in one place per host.

31c — retire the standalone service AS A STORE, not as a listener.
The ArtifactStore class moves in-process behind the FastAPI routes and
the tracker owns the blobstore. But a loopback listener stays on each
builder as a forwarding relay that stores nothing; the hooks keep
calling it exactly as they do today. So :8788, ArtifactStoreServer and
the Handler class are not simply deleted — they are reduced to a
forwarder. The artifact-store-client stays unchanged, still pointing at
loopback.

The relay is what makes a builder remote-capable and is tracked
separately; this bead only has to stop the standalone service from
being the STORE.

31d — ops + permissions. The tracker process now WRITES artifact_root; it
only read it before. Confirm the service account has write permission,
drop polytropos_artifact_store from RC_SCRIPTS and the runbook, and start
one service instead of two.

INTERACTION WITH WHAT JUST LANDED

poly-7z1 made `dev-env hooks-install` write ARTIFACT_STORE_CLIENT,
POLYTROPOS_PYTHON and DPORTSV3_TRACKER_TARGET into the env's hooks conf.
31b removes one of the two URLs that conf carries; env_hook_settings and
the conf example both need updating, and OPERATOR_SETUP.md's hook section
with them.

put-fs deserves a decision here rather than later, and it is narrower
than "remote producers should use put-blob".

Everything else is already remote-safe. The runner WRITES via
artifact_store_put (HTTP, streamed bytes) and READS via a materialize
step that pulls a bundle into a tempdir when there is no on-disk dir —
"Materialize the bundle if it arrived via artifact-store", steps.py. The
bundle_dir tier in read_bundle_text is an optimisation for the colocated
case, not a dependency.

put-fs is the one exception: exactly one caller, hook_pkg_failure,
gzipping the full dsynth log and handing the store a path to open itself.
It is the only artifact API that cannot cross a filesystem boundary, and
it is called from the one place guaranteed to sit on the builder.

It is ALREADY WRONG in a dev-env, not just under poly-fij. The hook
computes ${DIR_LOGS}/evidence/full-logs/... which inside the env is
/work/dsynth/logs/..., a chroot path, and sends it to a store on the
host. That writes an artifact_refs row with backend='fs' and an fs_path
nothing outside the chroot can open. Latent only because
/work/dsynth/logs/evidence does not exist yet — no in-chroot hook has
completed a run. The first one that does trips it. See poly-7z1.

So: reject put-fs from a caller that does not demonstrably share the
store's filesystem, and have the hook fall back to put-blob for the
compressed log. Cheap now; a silently unreadable evidence row later.

Disable the caller. Artifacts are centralized: pushed once at
production time, hook -> runner -> tracker, and the tracker keeps them.
Nothing is ever fetched back from a builder — no refetch, no cache, no
expiry. Distributed artifact storage was considered and rejected.

backend='fs' therefore has no caller and no planned one. Leave the
column alone (removing an enum value buys nothing) but do not describe
it as a seat for anything.

SIZING, MEASURED

The three failures in the 2026-08 x6 run were patch-stage, so their full
logs gzip to 1.2-1.7 KB — not representative. A deep compile failure is
a few MB of text, which gzip -9 lands around 100-500 KB; a 1500-failure
run is then a couple hundred MB. Build logs also dedup badly
(timestamps, paths and build ids make each one unique), so central
storage's main advantage does not apply to them. Kept here as the sizing
record, not as an argument for distributing them: a couple hundred MB
per run on one host is not a constraint worth a refetch protocol.

SEQUENCING — NOT BLOCKED BY STEP 21

The backlog doc ordered this 21 -> 31 -> 17, on the grounds that 31a
would otherwise mean "physically relocating artifact_store.py's
still-scattered write code and re-consolidating later".

Checked, and it does not hold. ArtifactStore's writes are not scattered:
it is a cohesive class whose public methods already map almost
one-to-one onto the six endpoints — upsert_run_bundle, apply_transition,
put_blob, put_fs_ref, get_artifact, upsert_user_context. It already IS
the write surface for its half, and 31c above keeps the class rather than
relocating it. So 31a is "mount six routes onto an existing class" and
needs nothing from Step 21 (poly-39v, now rescoped and related-not-
blocking).

Before poly-fij's auth children (17c/17e). A builder should aim at one
service and one auth surface; wiring auth against two endpoints you are
about to collapse is wasted work. poly-fij's 17d (claim endpoint) does
not depend on this either and can land first.
acceptance_criteria: 1. One process, one port (:8080). :8788 retired, polytropos_artifact_store gone from the rc.d scripts. 2. The runner and the dsynth hooks reach blobs and state through one URL; the artifact_store_get -> tracker_artifact_get fallback is deleted. 3. The tracker is the only PROCESS writing state.db, leaving the runner as the sole direct-sqlite writer for poly-fij to convert. 4. The /v1/ wire contract and the on-disk artifact layout are unchanged.
notes:
VERIFIED ON x6 2026-08-27, branch fold-artifact-store.

Full suite on DragonFly: identical failure set before and after (38
pre-existing, environmental — missing git identity for the test user,
and the host's own polytropos.conf overriding the queue-root default the
rc.d test asserts). Zero regressions.

Functional, against a second tracker on :18080 with its own logs root,
with the real hook_pkg_failure and the real client:

- GET /health answers on the tracker, the shape the hooks gate on.
- The hook posted a complete bundle, rc=0. All five artifacts landed
  backend='blob', including logs/full.log.gz (kind=gzip). No 'fs' rows.
- /v1/artifacts/get and /api/bundles/{id}/artifacts/... returned
  byte-identical content, so the writer's blob_path and the reader's
  resolve_artifact_path agree.
- put-fs with a chroot-style path is refused 400 "fs_path is not
  readable by the store", instead of writing a row that 404s forever.
- Error bodies are {"error": ...}, not FastAPI's {"detail": ...}.

DEVIATION FROM THE PLAN. 31c said to reduce Handler to a forwarder for
poly-fij.7. Deleted instead: a forwarder must not interpret payloads and
Handler is nothing but per-endpoint validation, so fij.7 shares no code
with it and is better off written fresh.

title: 17e Operator auth, separate from runner tokens
description:
The manual-queue endpoints (POST /api/manual-requests/.../context, .../discard) are a human path, not a builder path. They need their own scheme — at minimum an operator password or SSO behind a reverse proxy.

Do not reuse runner tokens here. A compromised builder must not be able to discard manual work. Keeping the two surfaces separate is the whole point; sharing one token collapses the blast radius the epic exists to bound.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A valid runner token cannot reach an operator endpoint. 2. The operator surface is not publicly writable once the tracker leaves a private network.
notes: ORDERING: same as 17c — auth last while nothing is published.

title: 17c Authenticated writes from a builder
description:
Every write a builder makes carries Authorization: Bearer <token> and X-Runner-Id. The tracker validates the pair, rejects mismatches and revoked tokens with 401, and stamps the authenticated runner_id onto the row it wrote. bundles gets a runner_id column so every bundle is traceable to the host that produced it; older rows stay NULL.

Scope note: this presumes the builder writes over HTTP at all. Today the runner writes 9 tables through local sqlite (57 execute/commit sites) — activity_log, env_health_status, runner_status, runners, user_context_requests, bundles, issues, jobs, verify_requests. Converting those is Step 21's centralization work, and this bead depends on it rather than duplicating it.

put-fs cannot be authenticated into working: a remote builder has no path the tracker can open. Reject it with an explicit 400 for remote callers instead of writing an artifact_refs row nobody can read.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A forged or revoked token cannot write. 2. Every bundle names the builder that produced it. 3. put-fs from a remote builder fails loudly rather than storing an unreadable ref.
notes:
ORDERING: lands after 17d/17a/17b, not before. Nothing is published yet, so the doc's 'auth first because the runner path is the larger attack surface' does not bind — that argument applies to an exposed tracker. Auth becomes load-bearing the day the tracker leaves a private network; land it before that day, not before it is useful.
PRIORITY RAISED TO P1 2026-08-27. With no VPN (decided in the storage design discussion), the tracker's machine surface is internet-facing and a scoped runner token is the ENTIRE boundary protecting it. This is not ordinary epic work that can land after the first remote builder — it has to land with it. See poly-fij.7 for where the token lives (one per host, in the relay, never inside a chroot).
PRIORITY RETURNED TO P2 2026-08-28. The P1 raise the day before rested
entirely on the tracker being internet-facing with no VPN. Operator has
deferred internet exposure, so that premise does not currently hold and
the epic's original ordering argument stands again: auth becomes
load-bearing the day the tracker leaves the private network, not before.

TRIGGER TO RAISE AGAIN: any of — the tracker gets a non-loopback,
non-LAN listener; a builder outside the trusted network enrolls; the UI
is put behind a public name. Whoever does that first should raise this
to P1 in the same change, because at that moment the runner token is
the entire boundary and there is nothing else in front of it.

title: 17b Stable runner identity + enrollment
description:
runner_id today is hostname-pid-uuid4[:8], regenerated on every process start. That is fine as a forensic tag and useless as an auth subject: a bearer token bound to it dies at the next restart. This is a CHANGE to identity, not an addition.

Persist the id (e.g. /usr/local/etc/polytropos/runner.json) and generate it once, at enroll. Enrollment: the operator runs an enroll subcommand on the builder pointing at the tracker URL, gets a one-time code, approves it on the tracker; the tracker issues a bearer token bound to the runner_id and the builder stores it 0600.

The runners table already exists but is liveness-shaped (runner_id, hostname, pid, started_at, last_heartbeat_at, stopped_at). It needs display_name, enrolled_at, token_sha256, revoked_at — an extension, not a new table.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A runner's id survives restart. 2. A revoked token stops that builder and no other. 3. The existing heartbeat keeps working against the same row.

title: 17a One tracker URL knob; retire hardcoded loopback
description:
Audit every hardcoded localhost / 127.0.0.1 / :8080 / :8788 across the runner and the hook scripts and route them through one config knob. The hooks already read ARTIFACT_STORE_URL and DPORTSV3_TRACKER_URL (note: the backlog doc calls the first DPORTS_ARTIFACT_STORE_URL, which is not its name). The runner has two separate accessors, _artifact_store_url() and _tracker_url(), which Step 31 collapses into one.

Cheap, and it is the step that tells us how much of the system still assumes loopback.
acceptance_criteria: 1. No hardcoded loopback address decides where a builder talks. 2. Pointing one variable at a remote host routes every runner and hook call there.
notes:
DONE 2026-08-27 on branch fold-artifact-store.

The audit found less than the bead expected, because poly-g19 had
already collapsed the runner's two accessors. What was left was three
modules each spelling "http://127.0.0.1:8080" for themselves — runner,
verify_fix, artifact_store_client — so changing the default in one left
two disagreeing.

dportsv3/common/endpoints.py now owns DEFAULT_TRACKER_URL and
tracker_url(), which also strips a trailing slash once (callers join
paths onto it, and "//v1" 404s in a way that reads like a missing
endpoint rather than a config typo).

Tests: setting DPORTSV3_TRACKER_URL to a remote host and capturing every
URL the runner opens for a round of bundle traffic — artifact get, put,
bundle list, port history — asserts none stay on loopback and that /v1/
and /api/ ride the same base. A separate test walks the package for
private copies of the literal.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERION 2 IS SCOPED, NOT MET AS WRITTEN. "Pointing one
variable at a remote host routes every runner and hook call there" holds
for the runner. It deliberately does not hold for the hooks: they post
to ARTIFACT_STORE_URL on loopback and always will, because on a remote
builder that is the local forwarder holding the host's credential rather
than the tracker (poly-fij.7). That decision postdates this bead. It is
what lets `dev-env hooks-install` write one config that is correct
whether the tracker is on this box or three hops away.

The store client keeps a duplicate default on purpose —
test_the_store_client_stays_stdlib_only requires the file to run under a
bare system python3 with nothing else importable, which is a stronger
guarantee than sharing the constant. A test pins the two equal.

title: 17d Claim endpoint: dispatch from the DB, not the directory
description:
The core of the epic, and the one piece worth landing before any auth work.

POST /api/jobs/claim picks work in one transaction, stamps jobs.owner_id, transitions to CLAIMED with a lease expiry, and returns the payload. 204 when there is nothing to claim. The runner stops sweeping pending/ to decide what runs next and calls this instead.

NOT 'pick the oldest'. claim_next_job_batch coalesces siblings: every pending job sharing a dedup key (origin + flavor) is claimed together, one becomes the lead the runner processes, the rest are folded into job['sibling_bundle_ids'], and they all retire together. Expressed as a sequence of renames today, which is why each one has to tolerate racing. In SQL it is one statement over a group — easier, but it must not be dropped on the way across.

The queue directory does not go away; it stops being a queue. Nothing outside the builder has ever read a .job file (three globs, all in runner.py; steps.py only receives a path it is handed), so the files can keep being written for operator breadcrumbs. What changes is that nothing DECIDES from them.

Atomicity moves from the atomic rename into the DB. That is what makes the builder's location irrelevant — and it closes poly-7z1's chroot seam as a side effect, with a single local runner and no network involved.

Already in place: GET /api/jobs and GET /api/jobs/{job_id} (reads, no claim); jobs.owner_id (recorded, never branched on); the jobs row itself, INSERTed by lifecycle on the hook's HTTP hook_enqueued before any runner sees the file.
acceptance_criteria: 1. The runner selects work without reading pending/. 2. Sibling coalescing survives the move: same-key jobs are still claimed and retired as a group. 3. Two runners against one tracker never claim the same job. 4. A claimed job whose runner dies is reclaimable without a global sweep.
notes:
PREMISE CONFIRMED ON HARDWARE 2026-08-27. After a real in-env dsynth build, the store's jobs table held all three failures:

  state=queued, type=triage, origin, target=@2026Q3, bundle_id — for
  devel/glib20, graphics/jpeg-turbo and lang/rust

delivered entirely over HTTP from inside a chroot, via the hook's job-transition hook_enqueued. The runner could not act on any of them, purely because it looks in a directory instead of the DB. Nothing else was missing.

Also confirmed: the .job file itself is already location-independent. Its full contents are profile, target, origin, flavor, bundle_id, run_id, type, snippet_round, has_snippets — no paths at all. So the claim endpoint does not have to invent a payload; the jobs row plus that field set is the payload, and the runner materializes the bundle over HTTP already (steps.py materialize_bundle).
CORRECTION 2026-08-27. The note above claiming 'the jobs row plus that field set is the payload' generalised from the triage job file, which is the only type the jobs table fully covers. patch, verify and confirm carry ~14 fields the schema does not model (profile, run_id, iteration, max_iterations, previous_bundle, user_context_rev, snippet_round, has_snippets, dev_env, tier, triage_relpath, issue_key, requested_build_generation, requested_by).

That does NOT block poly-b2r, which is the reason it looked urgent: the hook only ever creates type=triage, and the runner creates the other types locally where files work. This bead is still the right shape for remote builders, where every type crosses — and there it needs a spec carrier (see the backlog's Step 32 out-of-scope note on spec_json).
Claimed and released 2026-08-27 without being implemented. poly-b2r took the stranded-triage case instead, using lifecycle.apply(CLAIM) — already BEGIN IMMEDIATE — as the mutex and materializing the job file into inflight/. What is left here is the part that needs a design decision rather than a fix: a spec carrier for patch/verify/confirm, which the jobs table does not model (~14 fields), plus lease expiry for acceptance criterion 4 (a claimed job whose runner dies is reclaimable without a global sweep). b2r's dependency edge on this bead was stale and has been removed.

title: Step 17 — N builders, one tracker (remote runners + auth)
description:
Every piece of the loop assumes colocation today: the runner, the chroot,
the artifact-store and the tracker live on one host, talk over loopback,
and trust each other implicitly. That is fine for one builder. The
cost-effective shape going forward is N builders, one tracker — failures
aggregate in one place and build capacity scales horizontally.

The invariant that has to invert is stated in the code. `_apply_transition`
in runner.py:

    The filesystem queue is the source of truth for what processes next;
    the typed jobs table is the UI's read model.

Everything else in this epic is a consequence of swapping those two.

WHAT HOLDS IT TOGETHER TODAY, AND WHAT EVAPORATES

Mutual exclusion is an flock on `queue_root/runner.lock`
(LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB, EXIT_RUNNER_LOCKED=3): one runner per queue directory.
Give each builder its own queue directory and that lock stops meaning
anything — it guards a local directory, not the shared work set.
`sweep_stranded_inflight` reasons that "the runner holds an exclusive
lock, so nothing in inflight/ belongs to a live runner", which is sound
only because of the flock and false the moment the work set is shared.
Mutual exclusion has to move into the claim.

RECONCILED AGAINST THE CODE — Step 17 in the backlog doc predates a lot

1. "the runner must stop opening state.db directly (lifecycle,
   verify_requests/user_context_requests polls)" understates it: 57
   execute/commit sites writing 9 tables — activity_log,
   env_health_status, runner_status, runners, user_context_requests,
   bundles, issues, jobs, verify_requests.
2. "the store has no GET for pending state rows" is stale. `GET
   /api/jobs` (state + target filters) and `GET /api/jobs/{job_id}`
   already exist. What is missing is an atomic CLAIM, not a read.
3. 17b proposes creating a `runners` table. One exists — but
   liveness-shaped (runner_id, hostname, pid, started_at,
   last_heartbeat_at, stopped_at), not enrollment-shaped. `jobs.owner_id`
   also exists, "recorded only; no code branches on it".
4. `runner_id` is ephemeral: hostname-pid-uuid4[:8], regenerated every
   process start. A bearer token bound to it dies on restart, so 17b is a
   CHANGE to identity, not an addition.
5. The hook variable is ARTIFACT_STORE_URL, not DPORTS_ARTIFACT_STORE_URL.

THREE THINGS THAT MAKE THIS CHEAPER THAN THE DOC'S ~600 LOC

1. The write half already landed by accident. `enqueue_job` sends
   `job-transition --event hook_enqueued` with the full detail block, and
   lifecycle INSERTs the jobs row on first transition. Every job already
   exists in the DB, delivered over HTTP, before any runner touches the
   file. The file is a parallel copy.
2. C2 set the precedent. `issues_needing_build` already derives
   confirm-build work from the DB instead of draining a queue. Job
   dispatch is the last file-driven entry point in the system.
3. Step 17 does not have to solve poly-s9m first. dsynth_active pgreps
   host-wide and gates the whole loop, and env resolution refuses when
   there is more than one env — both are correct behaviour when a host
   has exactly one env, so one-env-per-builder does not hit them.

   NOT a reason to skip poly-s9m. The real shape is M hosts x N envs: a
   big DragonFly box should run several envs, and that is the efficient
   use of it. The two compose — Step 17 is scheduling ACROSS builders,
   poly-s9m is scheduling WITHIN one — and a builder running N envs needs
   both. What this buys is only that they can land in either order.

WHAT THE QUEUE DIRECTORY IS ACTUALLY DOING

queue_root/{pending,inflight,done,failed} is two things at once: the
queue, and the audit trail. Only the first has to move.

Nothing outside the builder ever reads a .job file, in any topology.
There are three globs and all are in runner.py — the inflight sweep, the
confirm sweep, and claim_next_job_batch. steps.py only receives a path it
is handed. The one other consumer is write_error_note, which drops a
<name>.job.error breadcrumb beside the file for an operator to find.

So the split is: the QUEUE moves into the DB; what remains on the builder
is an audit trail, and it can stay exactly as it is.

WHAT "THE RUNNER STOPS OPENING state.db" ACTUALLY COSTS

Nine tables written and nine read: bundles, issues, jobs, runs,
activity_log, runner_status, runners, env_health_status, user_context,
user_context_requests, verify_requests. Every one of those accesses
becomes a tracker endpoint or gets dropped. Two already have endpoints
(bundle-upsert, job-transition); the rest do not.

A local DB on the builder would not own any of this — it is shared state
the UI reads. The only thing a local DB could do is BUFFER writes while
the tracker is unreachable, which is an availability decision and should
be made deliberately rather than fallen into. Default answer: no local
DB, a builder that cannot reach the tracker stops taking work.
design:
THE CLAIM ENDPOINT IS THE WHOLE THING.

    POST /api/jobs/claim {runner_id, targets?}

One transaction: pick the oldest QUEUED job (optionally filtered to the
targets this builder serves), stamp owner_id, transition to CLAIMED with
a lease expiry, return the payload. 204 when there is nothing to claim.

Atomicity comes from the DB, not from a rename. That single endpoint is
what makes the builder's location stop mattering.

It is not "pick oldest". claim_next_job_batch coalesces SIBLINGS: every
pending job sharing a dedup key (origin + flavor) is claimed together,
one becomes the lead the runner processes, the rest are folded into
job["sibling_bundle_ids"], and they all retire together. That logic is
currently expressed as a sequence of renames, which is why it has to
tolerate each one racing. In SQL it is one statement over a group, and
strictly easier — but it must not be dropped on the way across.

Then, in order of consequence:

- Lease renewal rides the heartbeat that already exists
  (runners.last_heartbeat_at, 5s).
- Sweeps become QUALIFIED. reap_orphans and sweep_stranded_inflight stop
  meaning "everything in flight" and start meaning "jobs whose owner's
  heartbeat is stale". That is exactly what poly-bg1 asked for, and the
  two blockers it named as expensive have since landed: jobs.owner_id
  exists, and the runners table is no longer a singleton.
- The queue directory stops being a queue and stays an audit trail. It is
  builder-local in every topology — the tracker has never read a .job
  file and will not start. The runner can keep writing the same files in
  the same places for the same operator breadcrumbs (including
  write_error_note's .job.error); what changes is that nothing DECIDES
  from them.

WHAT NOT TO DO

- Do not reuse runner tokens for the operator surface. The manual-queue
  endpoints are a human path; a compromised runner must not be able to
  discard manual work.
- put-fs is local-only by construction — a remote builder cannot hand the
  tracker a path it can open. Remote producers use put-blob. Make it an
  explicit 400 rather than a silently unreadable artifact_refs row.

SEQUENCING — DECIDED: auth last

The backlog doc ordered this 17a -> 17b -> 17c -> 17d -> 17f -> 17e, auth
first on the argument that the runner path is the larger attack surface.
That argument applies to an exposed tracker. Nothing here is published
yet, so it does not bind, and the order is:

    17d (claim) -> 17a (config) -> 17b (identity) -> 17c/17e (auth) -> 17f

The claim endpoint goes first because it is worth having on its own, with
no auth and a single local runner: it closes the chroot seam in poly-7z1,
where the hook writes a queue path inside the chroot that the runner
outside cannot see. A chroot is the cheapest instance of "not the same
filesystem", so fixing it exercises the remote path for free.

Auth becomes load-bearing the day the tracker leaves a private network.
Land it before that day, not before it is useful.

Step 21 (centralized writes) and Step 31 (one service) still come before
the auth children — a builder should aim at one service and one auth
surface. Neither has a bead yet.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A builder can be brought up, pointed at a tracker URL, and consume triage/patch jobs without sharing a filesystem with the tracker. 2. Two builders run concurrently without either's startup sweep touching the other's in-flight work. 3. Nothing on a builder has implicit trust over the tracker, and nothing on the tracker can forge work attributable to a builder that did not do it. 4. The filesystem queue is no longer consulted to decide what runs next.

title: Patch loop burns its whole budget on an unreproducible report
description:
First real patch job. The reported symptom (a symbol in the failure log) does not exist in the extracted source. The agent established that in attempt 1 within ~2 minutes: make_extract, then grep for the symbol in vim.h and buffer.c, matches=0 in both. It then ran attempts 2 and 3, re-extracting and re-grepping for the same symbol (matches=0 again, plus a broader prefix, also 0), and stopped only on 'budget exhausted after attempt 3 (130702 >= 120000 billable)'.

Result: changes.diff 0 bytes, rebuild_ok false, status budget-exhausted, tokens_total 1427086 (1375946 prompt / 51140 completion). Every analysis artifact was produced correctly — patch.md, patch_audit.json, rebuild_proof.json, tool_trace.jsonl — so the machinery is sound. What is missing is a verdict for 'this report is not reproducible against the current tree', which is a real case (stale bundle, fixed upstream, flaky build) and not only an artefact of the synthetic log used here.

Retrying identically after proving the symptom absent cannot succeed, and the retry is the expensive part. Worth noting attempt 3 alone billed 314855.

Related: the trigger here was a fabricated log, so treat the frequency as unknown; the cost of the failure mode is not.
acceptance_criteria: 1) An attempt that proves the reported symptom absent from the source ends the loop with an explicit unreproducible verdict rather than retrying. 2) The verdict reaches the operator as a handoff, distinct from budget-exhausted. 3) Token spend for that path is a small fraction of the tier budget.

title: Env dsynth profile name breaks the default tracker target
description:
dportsv3-hooks.conf leaves DPORTSV3_TRACKER_TARGET commented out, documented as 'Defaults to @${PROFILE} if unset (one profile per target)'. dev-env names the in-env dsynth profile after the ENV, not the target: profile_selected=2026Q3-editors_vim for a @2026Q3 env. So the derived target is @2026Q3-editors_vim.

issue_key hashes (target, origin, fingerprint), so every failure raised inside an env lands on an issue that can never match the same failure from the farm. Two parallel universes of issues, no error, nothing in the UI to suggest it. The hook looks like it is working.

Either dev-env should name the profile after the target, or hooks-install should write DPORTSV3_TRACKER_TARGET explicitly from the env's known target instead of relying on the @${PROFILE} default.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A failure raised inside an env files against the env's target, matching what the farm produces for the same port. 2) The value is not left to a default that the env's own profile naming defeats.
notes: VERIFIED ON HARDWARE 2026-08-27. hooks-install wrote DPORTSV3_TRACKER_TARGET=@2026Q3 into the env conf, and all three bundles from the real build landed with target=@2026Q3 while the dsynth profile was 2026Q3-editors_vim. The @${PROFILE} default would have produced @2026Q3-editors_vim and split them off from anything the farm builds.

title: In-chroot hooks cannot reach the tool that installs them
description:
hooks-install puts the 9 hooks in the env's writable etc/dsynth and prints next steps naming ARTIFACT_STORE_URL, DPORTSV3_TRACKER_URL and DPORTSV3_TRACKER_TARGET. It does not name the two variables that must point at something reachable INSIDE the chroot: DPORTSV3_BIN and ARTIFACT_STORE_CLIENT. Both default to /build/synth/polytropos/..., which on a real install exists neither in the chroot nor on the host.

Observed: env mounts are base root, writable/work -> /work, writable/root -> /root, writable/tmp, writable/var_tmp. Nothing maps /build/synth. So hook_pkg_failure dies at require_artifact_store (client absent), and would fail_soft at tracker_load_config anyway (DPORTSV3_BIN not executable) — every in-chroot dsynth failure is silently dropped.

Copying a venv in does not work: its shebangs are absolute (/usr/local/lib/polytropos/bin/python). A nullfs mount of the install prefix at the same path inside the env would resolve, which is probably the fix — plus naming both variables in the hooks-install output.
acceptance_criteria: 1) After hooks-install and the documented edits, a dsynth failure inside the env reaches the artifact-store. 2) hooks-install names every variable that must be set, including the two that must resolve inside the chroot. 3) The mechanism that makes the tool reachable is part of env creation or hooks-install, not operator improvisation.
notes:
Second half of the same symptom, found on the host side: bin/artifact-store-client is installed NOWHERE. It is not in [project.scripts] (only dportsv3 and artifact-store are), and deploy.py never copies it. So a packaged install has no store client, and ARTIFACT_STORE_CLIENT has nothing to point at even outside a chroot — hook_pkg_failure dies at require_artifact_store on any install that is not a git checkout. Fixing the mount without shipping the client leaves the hooks just as broken.
Third part, a code bug rather than config: dportsv3-hooks.conf states 'Tracker integration is OPT-IN: if DPORTSV3_TRACKER_URL is unset (or this file is absent entirely), the tracker_* helpers short-circuit and hooks only do artifact-store work.' That is not what happens. hook_pkg_failure calls tracker_load_config unguarded at line 28, before the bundle-upsert at line 39, and tracker_load_config exit 0s (tracker_fail_soft) when DPORTSV3_BIN is unset or not executable. So the documented degraded mode silently DROPS the failure evidence instead of preserving it. Note /usr/local/bin/python3 does exist in the chroot and bin/artifact-store-client is stdlib-only with #!/usr/bin/env python3, so the client half needs only a copy into the env's /work; it is DPORTSV3_BIN that needs a mount.
FOURTH PART, found 2026-08-27 while wiring the tools in. Reaching the tools is necessary but not sufficient: two of the hook's outputs are paths, and inside a chroot they are chroot paths that nothing on the host can resolve.

1. THE QUEUE. queue_root() derives from DIR_LOGS, which the env's dsynth.ini pins to /work/dsynth/logs. So an in-env hook enqueues to /work/dsynth/logs/evidence/queue/pending, while the runner watches the host path from polytropos.conf (/tmp/polyverify/logs/evidence/queue here). They never meet. Confirmed on x6: /work/dsynth/logs/evidence does not exist at all — no in-chroot hook has ever completed a run, and every job in the host queue came from host-side invocations.

2. PUT-FS. hook_pkg_failure gzips the full log to ${DIR_LOGS}/evidence/full-logs/... and sends that path to the store with put-fs. The store, on the host, writes an artifact_refs row with backend='fs' and an fs_path it cannot open. Latent for the same reason as (1); the first successful in-env hook run trips it. put-fs is the only artifact API that cannot cross a filesystem boundary — the runner's own writes (artifact_store_put) and reads (materialize_bundle into a tempdir) are both already HTTP.

Neither is fixed by a bind-mount without deciding what the mount MEANS. The queue half is poly-fij.1 (claim from the DB instead of a directory); the put-fs half is poly-g19 (fall back to put-blob, reject fs paths from callers that do not share the store's filesystem). Both make the chroot boundary stop mattering for the same reason they make a host boundary stop mattering.
The fourth part above is split out as poly-b2r so this bead stays scoped to tool reachability, which is fixed. Do not block this on it.
VERIFIED ON HARDWARE 2026-08-27 with a real dsynth build in the env.

Criterion 1: three real failures inside the chroot reached the artifact-store — devel/glib20@bootstrap (19 artifacts), lang/rust (15), graphics/jpeg-turbo (7). Criterion 2: hooks-install wrote and printed all four values. Criterion 3: the venv bind-mount at /work/polytropos comes from prepare_root_runtime and the conf from hooks-install; no operator step.

In-chroot proof of the mechanism: python resolves through the mount (sys.prefix=/work/polytropos, 3.11.12, matching the host), 'dportsv3 --version' runs via the POLYTROPOS_PYTHON indirection, and artifact-store-client reaches the host store over the shared loopback.

One caveat, split to poly-lx9: the venv needed four pure-Python modules force-installed by hand because --system-site-packages left them on the host. Until that is automated, criterion 3 holds for the mount and the conf but not for the venv contents.

Remaining in-chroot gaps are poly-b2r (queue + put-fs paths), not this bead.
PREMISE PARTLY WRONG — see the bead filed 2026-08-27 about the venv bind-mount. The tool WAS reachable in the chroot all along: layout.TOOL_DIR=/work/polytropos holds a full checkout with the repo's own shell wrapper at bin/dportsv3, verified running 3.0.0-dev inside the env. The real defect was narrower and is what the fix should have been: dportsv3-hooks.conf carried DPORTSV3_BIN=/build/synth/polytropos/bin/dportsv3, a path on no machine, instead of TOOL_BIN. Reading that stale value as evidence the tool was absent is what produced the bind-mount, which then shadowed the checkout.

title: rc.d scripts take a command, not a repo root
description:
L1 of the repo-coupling review (2026-08-25).

The three rc.d scripts exec ${polytropos_root}/bin/dportsv3 — a git
checkout's layout. Once this ships as a dport there is no checkout: the
package installs ${PREFIX}/bin/dportsv3 and ${PREFIX}/bin/dports-dev-env.

Change: make the *command* the knob rather than the root.
polytropos_cmd defaults to ${PREFIX}/bin/dportsv3; a checkout is then
one possible value (polytropos_cmd=/path/to/checkout/bin/dportsv3)
instead of the assumption. Same for the dev-env command the runner
needs (see the sibling bead on dports-dev-env).

The venv-stamp probe from poly-abr.7 has to follow: it only applies to
the wrapper, since a packaged console script has no venv to be stale.
Probe conditionally rather than unconditionally.
notes:
## Implemented 2026-08-25

The scripts name commands now, not a repository:

    polytropos_cmd          default /usr/local/bin/dportsv3
    polytropos_dev_env_cmd  default /usr/local/bin/dports-dev-env (runner)

polytropos_root is gone from every script and from the config sample. A
checkout is one possible value rather than the assumption.

Two knobs and not one, because the `dportsv3` console script does not
implement `dev-env`. The runner also exports
DPORTS_DEV_ENV_CMD=${polytropos_dev_env_cmd} so worker.py uses the
configured command rather than whatever PATH holds — the resolver added
in poly-abr.8 honours it first.

The poly-abr.7 probe generalised rather than becoming conditional, which
is better than planned. Probing with the service's own argv works in
both worlds: in a checkout it still catches a stale install stamp, and
in a packaged install it proves the command runs at all. The runner
probes BOTH entry points, since they are separate distributions with
separate venvs and separate stamps.

deploy install now reports which of the two commands are absent from
<prefix>/bin after installing, with the exact polytropos.conf lines to
point them at a checkout. Installing from a checkout does not put
console scripts in the prefix, and that is worth saying rather than
leaving to a failed service start.

Tests: 75 in test_deploy_rc_scripts.py, 21 in test_deploy_install.py.
Mutation tested: reintroducing a repo-root assumption, dropping the
DPORTS_DEV_ENV_CMD export, and removing the dev-env probe each fail a
test. Suite 2276 passed.

title: Runtime invokes dports-dev-env directly, not through the shell wrapper
description:
L2 of the repo-coupling review (2026-08-25). This is the one that
actually blocks a packaged install from working.

Facts:

  * The console script `dportsv3` does NOT implement `dev-env`. Verified
    from its own --help: nine subcommands, none of them dev-env. Only
    bin/dportsv3, the shell wrapper in the checkout, routes it — and it
    does so by exec'ing `dports-dev-env`.
  * `dports-dev-env` is already a console script of the dev-env
    distribution ([project.scripts] in dev-env/pyproject.toml), so a
    packaged install puts it at ${PREFIX}/bin/dports-dev-env.
  * worker._resolve_dportsv3_cmd() falls back to
    shutil.which("dportsv3") when $DPORTSV3_CMD is unset. In a packaged
    world that finds the console script, which then fails at
    `dev-env exec` with an argparse "invalid choice" — not the clear
    RuntimeError the function already contains for this exact case.

Change: the 25 call sites reach the chroot through one helper. Point it
at `dports-dev-env` (new $DPORTS_DEV_ENV_CMD, falling back to
which("dports-dev-env")), so the runtime never needs the wrapper. Keep
$DPORTSV3_CMD honoured for compatibility, and make the which() fallback
refuse a `dportsv3` that cannot route dev-env rather than picking it up.

Do NOT add a dev-env subcommand to cli.py instead: bin/dportsv3 states
that keeping it out is deliberate, so that the agent "never finds the
console script by mistake".
notes:
## Implemented 2026-08-25

worker.py's resolver now targets the dev-env entry point rather than the
checkout's shell wrapper. _resolve_dportsv3_cmd/_dportsv3_cmd/_run_dportsv3
are gone, replaced by _resolve_dev_env_cmd/_dev_env_cmd/_run_dev_env,
which return the argv PREFIX that routes a dev-env subcommand:

  1. $DPORTS_DEV_ENV_CMD          (explicit)
  2. $DPORTSV3_CMD + "dev-env"    (checkout wrapper, exported by bin/dportsv3)
  3. which("dports-dev-env")      (what a port installs)

`dportsv3` on PATH is deliberately NOT in that list, and the removal of
that fallback is the point of the change. Demonstrated on the real
binaries in this checkout:

    $ .venv/bin/dports-dev-env --help      -> routes, lists create/shell/...
    $ .venv/bin/dportsv3 dev-env --help    -> error: argument COMMAND:
                                              invalid choice: 'dev-env'

The old code fell back to which("dportsv3") and would pick the second
one in any packaged install, failing at the first chroot call with that
argparse error instead of the RuntimeError the function already carried.

Order note: the checkout wrapper is honoured AHEAD of PATH, so a checkout
uses its own dev-env venv rather than another copy installed on the host.

Every consumer prefixed the literal "dev-env" — worker's _exec and three
_run_dportsv3 calls, health.py's _run_in_env, and verify_fix's
apply-and-build — so the word moved into the prefix and out of all five
call sites. verify_fix's docstring described a "repo-root sibling"
resolution step that no longer exists; rewritten to match reality.
health.py's operator_action now names the variables that actually help.

Worth recording: .venv/bin/dports-dev-env already exists in a normal
checkout, because bin/dportsv3 pip-installs dev-env into the generator
venv. So the packaged resolution path is exercisable today, not only
after a port exists.

Tests: tests/test_dev_env_entry_point.py (12). Mutation tested —
restoring the which("dportsv3") fallback, letting PATH outrank the
checkout wrapper, and re-adding the literal "dev-env" to _exec each fail
a test. Suite 2263 passed.

title: Service start must fail on a stale venv stamp, not every job
description:
Found while measuring how often the runner enters a dev-env, 2026-08-25.
Proved on x6, not reasoned about.

bin/dportsv3 computes an install stamp on EVERY invocation (a Python
process that hashes pyproject.toml) and compares it to the one recorded
in the venv. DPORTSV3_NO_BOOTSTRAP=1 does not skip that check — it only
suppresses the install that would follow, turning a mismatch into:

    dportsv3: dev-env bootstrap required but DPORTSV3_NO_BOOTSTRAP=1
    rc=1

Measured on x6: 0.34s per `dev-env exec`, and NO_BOOTSTRAP=1 changes
nothing (0.33s) because the stamp work happens either way.

The rc.d scripts set DPORTSV3_NO_BOOTSTRAP=1 deliberately — a service
start is the wrong moment to pip install. But the consequence was not
thought through: after any upgrade touching dev-env/pyproject.toml or
the generator's, the service starts CLEANLY and then every job fails.
The runner reaches a dev-env from 21 distinct functions; all of them
would return rc=1, and the actual reason sits in per-job output rather
than anywhere an operator looks first.

Fix: probe the wrapper in start_precmd and refuse to start when it is
stale, so the failure lands at `service ... start` with the command that
repairs it. The runner must probe the `dev-env` branch specifically —
that path has its own separate stamp and venv.
notes:
Implemented with the same change: all three scripts probe the wrapper in
start_precmd under DPORTSV3_NO_BOOTSTRAP=1 and refuse to start when it
exits non-zero, naming the command that repairs it. The runner probes
'dev-env --help' specifically — that branch has its own venv and its own
stamp, so probing '--version' would pass while every dev-env call still
failed. Verified on x6: the probe returns 0 healthy, 1 with a stale
stamp (tested by swapping the stamp file and restoring it).

Tests: 14 more in tests/test_deploy_rc_scripts.py (51 total), executing
each script's start_precmd against a fake bin/dportsv3 that exits 0 or
1, plus the queue-subdir creation, the 600-vs-644 credential warning,
and 'no credentials still starts'.

## Follow-up bug in the fix itself, found before it shipped

The first version of this probe used `bin/dportsv3 --version`. Wrong:
the INSTALL PROFILE is part of the stamp string. compute_stamp prints
"<profile>:<digest>", and the wrapper sets INSTALL_PROFILE=tracker only
when argv is exactly `tracker serve`. So a --version probe compares
against the base stamp and fails both ways round — it refuses to start
on a tracker-profile venv, and it passes on a base-profile venv that
`tracker serve` then rejects. Confirmed from the recorded stamp on x6:
'base:28f8df1a...+0f555fe9...'.

Probes now use each service's own argv: 'tracker serve --help' and
'artifact-store --help'. Only a bare -h/--help/help as $1 short-circuits
the wrapper, so both still reach the stamp check, and argparse handles
--help afterwards without binding a port.

The test for this initially had a hole and a mutation survived: the
probe spans a backslash continuation, so a per-line scan saw
'bin/dportsv3' and the flag on different lines, while the err message
still contained the expected argv. The test now joins continuations into
logical lines before checking. Re-run: probing --version in either
service, or removing the probe, each fails a test.

RESIDUAL GAP, not covered: a venv whose [tracker] extra install failed
part-way would still pass the stamp check, because the stamp records the
profile that was requested rather than what landed. _cmd_serve's own
uvicorn find_spec catches it at that point with a clear message.

title: Tracker binds 0.0.0.0 with no auth — decide the exposure before enabling at boot
description:
Found while planning the epic, 2026-08-25. Verified in code, not inferred.

  * dportsv3/commands/tracker.py, _cmd_serve: the listener is
    `uvicorn.run(app, host="0.0.0.0", port=int(args.port))`. The address
    is a literal — `tracker serve` takes only --port and --db, so there
    is no way to bind it to loopback from the CLI.
  * artifact-store does the opposite and gets it right: DEFAULT_BIND is
    "127.0.0.1" with a --bind flag (dportsv3/artifact_store.py).
  * The tracker exposes 24 mutating routes (POST/PUT/PATCH across
    tracker/routes/), and there is no authentication of any kind:
    no middleware, no Depends(), no token check anywhere under
    dportsv3/tracker/. The only api_key in that tree is the LLM
    provider key used by the chat route.
  * Several of those routes are not read-only in the cheap sense:
    POST /api/issues/{key}/build starts a build,
    POST /api/bundles/{id}/chat spends LLM credit,
    PUT /api/config/active-env repoints which dev-env the runner uses.

Today this is mitigated by circumstance — an operator starts the tracker
in a shell, watches it, and stops it. An rc.d service enabled in rc.conf
removes that mitigation: it listens on every interface, from boot,
unattended. That is why this belongs to the deployment epic rather than
being filed as a general hardening ticket.

Decide, then implement in the same change as the rc script:

  1. Add a --bind flag to `tracker serve` mirroring artifact-store, and
     default it to 127.0.0.1.
  2. Choose the deployment posture: loopback plus an ssh tunnel for
     remote access, or a LAN bind with something in front of it.
  3. If it is ever to listen off-loopback, authentication stops being
     optional — at minimum on the mutating routes.

Item 1 is worth doing regardless of what is decided for 2 and 3: a
hardcoded bind address is a defect on its own.
notes:
DECIDED 2026-08-25: LAN bind, no auth (trusted network), expressed
explicitly rather than hardcoded.

Scope reduces to item 1 of the description: give 'tracker serve' a
--bind flag so the address is a documented, overridable option instead
of a literal buried in _cmd_serve. The flag keeps 0.0.0.0 as its
default so nothing changes for anyone running the tracker by hand
today, and the rc.d script sets it explicitly from rc.conf.

Items 2 and 3 (loopback posture, authentication) are NOT being done.
The 24 unauthenticated mutating routes stay reachable on the LAN by
choice. Recorded here so the next person reads a decision rather than
an oversight.

## Implemented 2026-08-25

commands/tracker.py gains DEFAULT_BIND = '0.0.0.0' and _cmd_serve now
binds getattr(args, 'bind', None) or DEFAULT_BIND. cli.py adds --bind to
'tracker serve', defaulting to that constant, with help text that says
the tracker has no authentication and what binding it wide means.

The getattr is not defensive padding: _cmd_serve is reachable with a
hand-built Namespace, and an empty rc.conf knob arrives as '' rather
than absent. Both cases fall back to the default; both are tested.

Behaviour is unchanged by design — same address, now a documented option
instead of a literal in the uvicorn call.

Tests: tests/test_tracker_bind.py (6), including one that pins the
asymmetry with artifact-store (127.0.0.1) so the two are not
'harmonised' by someone who reads it as an inconsistency. Mutation
tested: restoring the literal, dropping the getattr guard, and flipping
the default each fail a test. Suite 2168 passed.

Docs: OPERATOR_SETUP.md section 6 now shows --bind explicitly, states
the no-auth exposure, and gives the ssh -L tunnel for anyone who wants
loopback instead.

title: Verify: cold start, reboot, restart on x6
description:
The acceptance gate for the epic, on real hardware rather than in tests.

  1. From cold: enable the three services in rc.conf, `service ... start`
     each, and confirm the tracker dashboard loads on :8080 and the
     artifact-store answers on :8788.
  2. Reboot the host and confirm all three come back without hand-holding.
  3. `service polytropos_runner restart` mid-job and confirm the startup
     sweeps do their job — the inflight row is reaped, the stranded job
     file lands in failed/, stale worktrees are removed (poly-bg1,
     poly-tr8, all previously verified by hand but never through the
     service scripts).
  4. Start a second runner and confirm it exits 3 rather than starting.
  5. Run the runner service as a non-root user and confirm exit 4 with
     the message naming the fix (poly-i7y).

Passing 1-2 is also what unblocks the end-to-end case that is still
outstanding on poly-m7o: a real patch job being retired
worktree_unavailable needs a live LLM job, which needs the stack up.
notes:
## Blocked on a push, 2026-08-25

Everything else in the epic is done (11/12). This needs the commits on
x6, and the standing instruction is never to push, so it waits.

Procedure, in order, with what each step proves:

  0. On x6: git pull. Confirm HEAD has the deploy/ tree.

  1. bin/dportsv3 deploy install --dry-run
     Every step prints 'do' or 'skip' and nothing changes. Expect it to
     report that dportsv3 and dports-dev-env are absent from
     /usr/local/bin, since x6 installs from a checkout, and to print the
     two polytropos.conf lines that point at the wrapper.

  2. sudo bin/dportsv3 deploy install
     Creates the polytropos user/group, /var/db/polytropos, the rc.d
     scripts, the config and credential stubs, the newsyslog drop-in,
     the four queue subdirectories, and chowns /build/synth/logs.
     That last one matters: the evidence tree there is root:wheel from
     runs dated 2026-08-01, and BSD group inheritance only covers NEW
     files.

  3. Set polytropos_cmd/polytropos_dev_env_cmd in polytropos.conf per
     step 1's output. Put a real key in harness.env.

  4. service polytropos_artifact_store start; then tracker; then runner.
     Check :8788 and :8080 answer and the dashboard loads.

  5. Negative cases, which are the point of the last few beads:
       - polytropos_cmd pointing at nothing        -> refuses, names the knob
       - polytropos_dev_env_cmd at the console script `dportsv3`
                                                   -> refuses (it cannot route dev-env)
       - stale install stamp                       -> refuses, names the repair
       - a second runner by hand while the service runs -> exit 3
       - runner service as non-root                -> exit 4

  6. Log rotation: newsyslog -F, confirm the logs rotate and the
     services survive. This is the one measured-but-not-yet-integrated
     piece — SIGUSR1 to the supervisor was verified directly on x6
     (poly-abr.4), but not yet through newsyslog driving it.

  7. reboot. All three come back. Then restart the runner mid-job and
     confirm the startup sweeps run (poly-bg1, poly-tr8).

  8. HOME across the privilege drop: confirm the tracker process has
     HOME=/var/db/polytropos, not /root.

## Verified on x6, 2026-08-25 (scratch logs root /tmp/polyverify/logs)

Ran against a scratch tree by operator choice, so /build/synth/logs was
left root:wheel and untouched. Everything except the reboot was
exercised. SIX bugs found, all fixed and committed; none of them was
visible from the tests alone.

BUG 1 — rc.subr's PATH excludes the local prefix. The very first
`service start` died with "dportsv3: required interpreter not found:
python3": DragonFly keeps python3 in /usr/local/bin, and rc.subr does
not put it on PATH. The runtime looks up dports-dev-env the same way.
Fixed: polytropos_path knob, exported before the probe uses it.

BUG 2 — the installer's chown never ran on a fresh tree. plan() decided
to skip it because the logs root did not exist AT PLAN TIME, but the
plan's own mkdir steps then created it as root. artifact-store died with
PermissionError creating evidence/blobstore. Fixed: chown is
unconditional, it is idempotent.

BUG 3 — the two HTTP services evicted each other. bin/dportsv3 records
ONE install profile in its stamp, so bootstrapping `tracker serve` wrote
"tracker:" and artifact-store's base-profile probe then failed — under
NO_BOOTSTRAP that is a refusal to start against a venv that can run it
perfectly well, since [tracker] is a superset. Fixed in the wrapper:
a tracker stamp satisfies a base request, one way only.

BUG 4 — `service status` lied. rc.subr matches the pid in $pidfile
against $procname, which defaults to $command = /usr/sbin/daemon. With
the CHILD's pid there it reported a service that was demonstrably
serving HTTP as "not running", and stop could not find it either.
Verified directly: .pid held python3.11, .sup.pid held daemon. Fixed:
$pidfile is now the supervisor's (also what newsyslog wants), and the
worker's pid goes to <name>.child.pid.

BUG 5 — a multi-word command could not be passed. rc.subr word-splits
${name}_env, and the checkout form of the dev-env command is two words,
so `env` took the second as the program: "env: dev-env: No such file or
directory". Fixed: exported from start_precmd, where quoting survives.

BUG 6 (docs) — the bootstrap advice named one command where three are
needed. The install profile is part of each stamp, so `--version`
records base: and the tracker still refuses. Corrected in the runbook
and in deploy install's output.

WHAT PASSED, after those fixes:

  install       user/group created, rc.d 0755 root:wheel, harness.env
                0600 root:wheel, chat.env 0640 root:polytropos,
                /var/db/polytropos owned by the service account, the
                newsyslog drop-in, all four queue subdirs
  dry-run       every step printed, nothing changed, and it named the
                two console scripts absent from the prefix plus the
                exact polytropos.conf lines to fix that
  services      all three start; :8788 answers; :8080 serves the
                dashboard; status reports real pids
  privileges    tracker and artifact-store run as polytropos; runner as
                root
  HOME          tracker child has HOME=/var/db/polytropos, not /root
  dev-env cmd   DPORTS_DEV_ENV_CMD reaches the child intact, both words
  chroot        health probe returned 2026Q3-editors_vim -> ready, so
                the whole chain works: rc -> wrapper -> dev-env venv ->
                chroot
  restart       clean stop and start, lock released and re-acquired
  exit 3        second runner by hand named the live holder, with pid
                and heartbeat
  exit 4        non-root runner refused with the poly-i7y message
  rotation      newsyslog -F rotated all three to .0.gz, created fresh
                logs, and ALL THREE SERVICES SURVIVED — the
                SIGUSR1-to-supervisor design confirmed through newsyslog
                itself, not just by hand

STILL UNVERIFIED: the reboot. Left for the operator to schedule.

NOTE: the x6 checkout carries hand-applied copies of the fixed rc.d
scripts and wrapper. A pull plus `deploy install` replaces them with
identical content.

## Reboot verified, 2026-08-25

Rebooted x6. All three services came back unattended, with no
intervention beyond the rc.conf _enable lines:

    polytropos_tracker         pid 908
    polytropos_artifact_store  pid 930
    polytropos_runner          pid 962

The runner came up last, which is what its REQUIRE line asks for. It
loaded its credentials, stubbed the env into env_health_status, and
started clean.

Listening sockets after the boot confirm both exposure decisions hold in
production, and the asymmetry between them is real rather than theoretical:

    polytropos python3.11 910  *:8080            tracker, LAN (deliberate)
    polytropos python3.11 932  127.0.0.1:8788    artifact-store, loopback

Both owned by the service account, so the privilege split survives a
boot as well as a manual start.

Every criterion in this bead is now met. Left running against
/tmp/polyverify/logs at the operator's request; /build/synth/logs was
never touched.

title: How the scripts get onto the host
description:
Writing the rc.d scripts does not install them. Polytropos is not
packaged: the documented install is a git checkout plus a uv venv
(OPERATOR_SETUP.md section 2), and the services are invoked through
bin/dportsv3 from that checkout.

Decide and implement the delivery path. Options, roughly in increasing
order of effort:

  * A `make install` / install.sh that copies the rc.d scripts and a
    sample config, and records the checkout path the scripts exec from.
  * A `dportsv3 deploy install-rc` subcommand, consistent with how
    dev-env hooks are already installed (`dportsv3 dev-env
    hooks-install`), which is the closest existing precedent in this
    repo.
  * An actual port/package. Largest effort, and premature while the tool
    still runs from a checkout.

Whichever is chosen, the scripts need an unambiguous answer to "which
python and which checkout do I exec?" — the venv path is operator-chosen
today.
notes:
## Implemented 2026-08-25

`dportsv3 deploy install`, in dportsv3/commands/deploy.py, wired into
cli.py. Chosen over a make target because it mirrors the precedent
already in this repo (`dportsv3 dev-env hooks-install`) and because a
port is premature while the tool runs from a checkout.

Finding the files without breaking the path rule: paths.py gains
tool_root() and deploy_dir(), resolving $DPORTS_DEV_TOOL_ROOT — the
variable bin/dportsv3 already exports, and the same one
dports_dev_env.builder resolves for the same reason. No parents[N] walk,
and an operator running the console script directly gets a raise naming
--tool-root rather than a guessed path.

plan() decides everything and touches nothing; apply() carries out a
plan. That is what makes --dry-run exact rather than approximate, and it
is why the decisions are testable without root.

Two ownership rules, taken from the ports framework:

  * rc.d scripts are TOOL-OWNED and replaced on every install. An
    upgrade that leaves a stale script in place is worse than one that
    overwrites it.
  * polytropos.conf, harness.env and chat.env are OPERATOR-OWNED and
    written once. This is Keywords/sample.ucl's rule: copy <f>.sample to
    <f> only when <f> is absent. (Its deinstall half — remove only if
    the file still matches the sample — is worth copying if an uninstall
    is ever added.)

Also creates /var/db/polytropos as the service account's home, because
`daemon -u` leaves HOME inherited from root (see poly-abr.1). A test
pins that path against the rc scripts' default so the two cannot drift.

The chown step is skipped when the logs root does not exist yet, and
planned when it does — /build/synth/logs/evidence on x6 is root:wheel
from earlier runs, and BSD group inheritance only covers NEW files.

Refuses on a non-DragonFly platform, and on non-root unless --dry-run.

Tests: tests/test_deploy_install.py (18). Mutation tested — overwriting
operator files, skipping rc scripts that already exist, installing
harness.env 644, executing skipped actions, and dropping the root check
each fail a test. Suite 2251 passed.

NOT YET RUN ON HARDWARE: `deploy install --dry-run` on x6 needs these
commits pushed first. That belongs to poly-abr.5 along with the real
install.

title: Three rc.d scripts, one per service
description:
The core deliverable: /usr/local/etc/rc.d/polytropos_artifact_store,
polytropos_tracker, polytropos_runner. Standard rc.subr scripts with
rcvar knobs, daemon(8) for backgrounding and pidfiles, start/stop/
restart/status.

Points that are decided already and must be honoured:

  * polytropos_runner runs as root and must not set a user. Every
    dev-env subcommand calls require_root(); a non-root runner exits 4
    (poly-i7y). Encode that rather than leaving it to the operator.
  * polytropos_artifact_store and polytropos_tracker have no root
    requirement. Give them a dedicated unprivileged user and say which
    paths that user needs to write (logs root, state.db, artifact root).
  * No custom "already running?" check for the runner. It flocks
    <queue-root>/runner.lock and exits 3, naming the holder (poly-bg1).
    Let the exit code surface; a second layer of pidfile guessing would
    be less accurate than the lock.
  * restart is safe by construction: the startup sweeps assume a
    restarted runner is cleaning up after a dead one (poly-tr8).
  * REQUIRE lines stay minimal — the services are order-independent
    (each is idempotent on schema init, per OPERATOR_SETUP.md).

Open question for the design: whether stop should be graceful for the
runner. It holds jobs in flight, and SIGTERM mid-job leaves an inflight
row that the next start reaps as an orphan. That is correct but lossy;
decide whether to wait for the current job or accept the reap.
notes:
## Implemented 2026-08-25

deploy/rc.d/{polytropos_artifact_store,polytropos_tracker,polytropos_runner},
plus deploy/README.md. Written against what DragonFly 6.5 on x6 actually
provides, checked before writing rather than assumed:

  * /etc/rc.subr honours ${name}_user, _group, _env, _chdir, _flags,
    _program, _nice, _prepend, and sources /etc/rc.conf.d/<command>.
  * /usr/sbin/daemon exists and supports -u user, -p/-P pidfiles,
    -o output_file, -t title, -f, -r/-R, -S syslog.
  * start_precmd is eval'd in the same shell, so `umask 002` and
    sourcing a credentials file there both reach the child process.
  * `find FILE -perm +077` behaves as intended (600 quiet, 640/644 warn).

Decisions encoded, each with the reason in the script:

  * The runner takes no -u and must not. dev-env require_root(), exit 4.
  * The runner starts with umask 002 because root writes into a tree
    owned by the service user; without it the tracker cannot write
    state.db-wal and it presents as a read-only database.
  * No `daemon -r`. It restarts on any exit code, and 3 (locked) and 4
    (env store unreadable) are configuration errors that would spin.
  * DPORTSV3_NO_BOOTSTRAP=1 everywhere: bin/dportsv3 otherwise builds
    the venv on first run, and service start is the wrong moment to
    discover the network is down.
  * The dev-env knob is polytropos_runner_dev_env, NOT
    polytropos_runner_env — the latter is rc.subr's own name for the
    child environment and would have been silently replaced.
  * The runner's prestart creates the four queue subdirectories, since
    the runner exits 1 when they are missing.

CORRECTION to poly-abr.2's original note: the runner is NOT the only
service that talks to an LLM. The tracker's fix-chat panel calls one
from inside the request (tracker/routes/_common.py reads
DP_HARNESS_CHAT_MODEL / _API_KEY / _API_BASE / _PROVIDER). So there are
two credential files with different ownership, not one:
harness.env (root:wheel 0600, runner) and chat.env
(root:polytropos 0640, tracker). Chat is feature-gated on
DP_HARNESS_CHAT_MODEL, so an absent chat.env is a supported state —
503 on the endpoint and the panel hidden.

Tests: tests/test_deploy_rc_scripts.py (37). These EXECUTE each script
against a stub rc.subr and inspect the command line it would hand to
daemon(8), rather than grepping the source — so config precedence
(rc.conf > polytropos.conf > script default) and the derived-path
logic are exercised for real. Mutation tested: giving the runner -u,
taking -u off the tracker, making the --env flag unconditional,
switching the sample to unconditional assignment, and dropping
DPORTSV3_NO_BOOTSTRAP each fail a test. Suite 2205 passed.

NOT verified, needs hardware (poly-abr.5): whether `daemon -u` preserves
the exported credentials through its setusercontext() call. If it does
not, the chat env has to reach the child another way.

## Revised against FreeBSD ports practice, 2026-08-25

Read the framework and 400 real rc.d scripts in ~/s/freebsd-ports on x6
rather than reasoning from first principles. Three changes and one
confirmation.

CHANGED — default assignment is now `: ${x:="v"}`, not `: ${x="v"}`.
Measured across those scripts: colon-form 1065 occurrences vs 364. It is
also the safer one: it substitutes the default for an empty value, so a
knob left as polytropos_tracker_bind="" in rc.conf does not become an
empty bind address.

CHANGED — every daemon(8) invocation now passes -c (chdir to /). Every
ports example does; a service holding a cwd keeps that filesystem busy.

CHANGED — HOME is set explicitly for the two services that drop
privileges. `daemon -u` lowers the uid but leaves HOME as it found it:
verified on DragonFly that a child running as an unprivileged user still
saw HOME=/root. www/grist-core exports HOME for the same reason. The
services now get /var/db/polytropos, which the installer creates and
chowns; the runner stays root so its inherited HOME is already right.

CONFIRMED — the `install -d -o user` in start_precmd, the 0755 rc.d
mode, and the sample/live config split all match what the framework
does. Keywords/sample.ucl copies <file>.sample to <file> only when the
target is absent, and on deinstall removes it only if it still matches
the sample. Our operator-owned files follow the install half exactly.

ALSO VERIFIED empirically on DragonFly, since the ports tree is FreeBSD
and the two can differ: `daemon -c -f -o LOG -p PID -t TITLE` works and
writes both the pidfile and the log; `-u USER` really drops privileges;
and an exported variable SURVIVES that drop (key=secret-abc reached the
child). That last one closes the open question recorded on poly-abr.5 —
chat.env sourced in start_precmd does reach the tracker.

NOT ADOPTED — `daemon -r` supervision, which ports like net-mgmt/bosun
and net-mgmt/telegraf do use. Wrong here: -r restarts on any exit code
and this runner uses exit 3 and 4 as configuration signals. Recorded in
the script, with the warning that anyone adding -r later must switch -p
to -P, because rc.subr signals whatever is in $pidfile and with the
child pidfile the supervisor would simply restart it.

Tests: 65 in tests/test_deploy_rc_scripts.py. New ones cover the colon
form, -c, HOME across the privilege drop, the installer/rc HOME
agreement, and that supervision and pidfile flags cannot disagree.
Mutation tested. Suite 2233 passed.

title: Config surface: rc.conf knobs and a secrets file
description:
Today the configuration is shell variables typed into three terminals
(OPERATOR_SETUP.md section 5): LOGS_ROOT, STATE_DB, ARTIFACT_ROOT,
QUEUE_ROOT, DPORTSV3_TRACKER_URL, ARTIFACT_STORE_URL, the ports. rc.d
needs these to come from somewhere durable.

Shape to decide:

  * rc.conf knobs for the non-secret settings (paths, ports, URLs, which
    services are enabled), with the derived ones derived rather than
    repeated — STATE_DB, ARTIFACT_ROOT and QUEUE_ROOT are all under
    LOGS_ROOT in the documented layout.
  * LLM credentials must NOT go in rc.conf: it is world-readable and gets
    pasted into bug reports. DP_HARNESS_TRIAGE_API_KEY and
    DP_HARNESS_PATCH_API_KEY (plus the model names) belong in a separate
    mode-600 env file sourced only by the runner — it is the only one of
    the three that talks to an LLM.
  * Decide the file locations and document them once, so the runbook
    (poly-4kr) has something stable to point at.
notes:
Config surface follows the two decisions on the epic: a polytropos
service user owns $LOGS_ROOT, and the tracker's bind address becomes an
rc.conf knob (default 0.0.0.0, per poly-abr.6).

Delivered with poly-abr.1: deploy/polytropos.conf.sample (shared,
world-readable, every setting in  form so /etc/rc.conf
outranks it), deploy/harness.env.sample and deploy/chat.env.sample.

Two credential files rather than one — see the correction on poly-abr.1:
the tracker's fix-chat panel calls an LLM too, and it runs as the
unprivileged service user, so it cannot read a root-only 0600 file.

title: EPIC: Supported deployment — rc.d scripts for the three services
description:
Polytropos has no deployment story. Starting it means three foreground
shells and a paragraph of documentation.

Established by scanning the repo 2026-08-24:

  * No rc.d script, .service unit or equivalent exists anywhere in the
    tree. The only /usr/local/etc references belong to dsynth's own
    config base.
  * docs/OPERATOR_SETUP.md section 6 is the whole of it: "In three
    separate shells or under your service manager of choice", with the
    environment set inline per shell.
  * bin/agent-queue-runner and bin/artifact-store are sys.path shims for
    running out of a checkout, not service entry points.
  * The operator's real bring-up is an ad-hoc local script that is not in
    the repo (poly-4kr).

The three components, from OPERATOR_SETUP.md section 6:

  artifact-store   `dportsv3 artifact-store --logs-root $LOGS_ROOT`, :8788
  tracker          `dportsv3 tracker serve --port 8080` (uvicorn), :8080
  queue runner     `dportsv3 agent-queue-runner --queue-root $QUEUE_ROOT`

Target is DragonFly BSD, so the native mechanism is /usr/local/etc/rc.d
plus rc.conf variables and daemon(8) — not systemd.

Two constraints are already settled by code, not assumption:

  * The runner MUST run as root. Every dev-env subcommand calls
    require_root() (dev-env/dports_dev_env/cli.py), and as of poly-i7y a
    non-root runner refuses to start with exit 4. The rc script for the
    runner cannot drop privileges. The other two services have no such
    requirement and should not run as root.
  * Double-start and restart are close to free. The runner takes an
    exclusive flock and exits 3 when another holds it (poly-bg1), and a
    restarted runner sweeps what the dead one left behind (poly-tr8), so
    `service ... restart` is already crash-safe.

Startup order does not matter — OPERATOR_SETUP.md notes each service is
idempotent on schema init — so REQUIRE lines stay simple.

Why it matters beyond convenience: with no supported way to bring the
stack up, anything that needs a live agent job cannot be exercised. That
currently blocks end-to-end verification of poly-m7o.
notes:
## Constraint found during planning: existing data is root-owned

/build/synth/logs/evidence on x6 — state.db, blobstore/, full-logs/ —
is entirely root-owned, from earlier runs. That collides with the
plan sketched in poly-abr.1 of running artifact-store and the tracker
as an unprivileged user: they both write there. Either the deployment
chowns the tree to a service user as part of install (poly-abr.3), or
all three services run as root and the privilege split is dropped.
This is a decision for the operator, not something to infer.

## Decisions from the operator, 2026-08-25

PRIVILEGE MODEL: split, and migrate the data to a service user. All of
$LOGS_ROOT ends up owned by a dedicated polytropos user/group; the
tracker and artifact-store run as that user; the runner stays root
because dev-env require_root() leaves no choice.

Consequence to design for rather than discover: root still writes into
that tree (the runner creates queue files, worktrees, state.db rows).
Root-created files must remain writable by the service user, so the
install needs a shared group, setgid directories, and umask 002 in the
runner's rc script. Getting this wrong shows up as the tracker failing
to write state.db-wal, not as an obvious permission error.

EXPOSURE: LAN bind, no auth, on a trusted network — but expressed as an
explicit rc.conf knob instead of the hardcoded literal it is today.
Keeps current behaviour; makes it visible and overridable.

## Root and the privilege split, measured on x6 2026-08-25

WHY THE RUNNER IS ROOT, quantified. It reaches a dev-env from 21
distinct functions in worker.py plus health.py's own probe helper — all
funnelling through `dportsv3 dev-env exec`, whose cmd_exec calls
require_root(). Of the 17 LLM-callable tools, 7 shell into the chroot
(dsynth_build, materialize_dports, make_extract, make_patch, genpatch,
dupe, validate_dops); the other 10 reach the env through the host
filesystem and need no chroot at all. 0.34s per call, measured.

Not every path is chroot traffic: the per-poll dsynth gate uses
host-level `pgrep -x dsynth`, and the health probe (2 exec calls) is
cached 60s. The volume comes from patch attempts — 3 attempts x up to 5
snippet rounds by default, one exec per tool call.

WHY THE OTHER TWO NEED NOT BE. Neither the tracker nor artifact-store
ever shells into a dev-env. The tracker reads env names and health rows
from state.db only (tracker/agentic_queries/env.py). That is exactly
what the runner's stub_unprobed_envs() exists for: the tracker cannot
enumerate the env store itself — that needs root — so the root runner
publishes what it can see into the DB for the UI to read. The split is
sound.

FILE OWNERSHIP — one claim corrected. I wrote that the evidence
directories need to be setgid. On DragonFly they do not. Tested on
HAMMER2, root-created files:

    umask 002, plain dir  -> -rw-rw-r-- root <dirgroup>
    umask 002, setgid dir -> -rw-rw-r-- root <dirgroup>   identical
    umask 022, either     -> -rw-r--r-- root <dirgroup>   service user locked out

BSD semantics inherit the group from the parent directory with or
without setgid, so the setgid bit Linux would need here is redundant.
The umask is the entire mechanism, and it does propagate: verified that
`umask 002` survives the rc script, bin/dportsv3, the Python CLI and the
chroot boundary — `umask` inside the chroot reports 0002 and the file
lands rw-rw-r--.

Consequence for poly-abr.3: group inheritance applies to NEW files only.
/build/synth/logs/evidence is root:wheel today, so the install must
chgrp -R the existing tree once; the umask handles everything after.

title: Runner silently loses the dsynth gate when it cannot enumerate envs
description:
Observed on x6 2026-08-23 while testing as a non-root user.

list_available_envs raised PermissionError on /root/.cache/dports-dev/envs. env_resolver logs a WARNING and treats it as 'no envs exist', so resolve_env_for_job refuses, runner_env comes back empty, and _gate_blocked returns False without ever calling dsynth_active. The runner then processes jobs with NO dsynth-busy gate at all.

The runner does log a WARN ('no dev-env resolved at runner start; dsynth-busy gating disabled'), so this is not silent in the logs — but it is silent in behaviour: the runner starts and runs normally with a safety gate switched off, and the only signal is one line at startup.

env_resolver already distinguishes 'dev-env package not importable' (logged as an error, since the operator action differs) from 'no envs'. A permission error is a third case with a third action — run as root — and is currently collapsed into 'no envs exist'.

Related: the same startup path is what B3's worktree sweep keys off, so a runner in this state also sweeps nothing.

Worth deciding whether a runner with no resolvable env should refuse to start rather than run ungated.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A permission error enumerating envs is distinguishable from 'no envs exist'. 2. A runner that cannot resolve an env either refuses to start or makes the ungated state unmistakable.
notes:
## Implemented 2026-08-23

Both criteria, plus one correction to the bead's premise.

Criterion 1 — `env_resolver.list_available_envs_detailed()` returns
`(names, error)`. `error` is non-None only when the store could not be read:
PermissionError, an unloadable config, or the pre-existing "dports_dev_env
not importable" case, each with its own operator action in the message.
`list_available_envs()` stays as a names-only wrapper for existing callers.
`EnvResolution` gains `enumeration_error`; a refusal caused by it no longer
says "create one with dev-env create", which pointed at the wrong problem.

Criterion 2 — split by cause, because the two empties are not the same:

- Store unreadable -> the runner REFUSES to start, exit 4
  (EXIT_ENV_UNREADABLE, distinct from 1 and from 3/locked). Checked before
  taking the lock, so a refusal costs a live runner nothing. Justified by
  dev-env cli.py: cmd_exec (and every other env subcommand) calls
  require_root(), so a runner that cannot enumerate envs cannot exec into
  one either.
- No env resolved but enumeration worked -> the runner HOLDS rather than
  running ungated. `_gate_blocked` now returns True with status "paused"
  and stage "no_dev_env: <reason>", rate-limited log + activity_log.
  Reversible from the tracker UI: selecting an env re-resolves next tick.
  Blanket refuse-to-start was rejected: tracker mode legitimately starts
  with no env and waits for the operator to pick one.

CORRECTION to the bead's reading: `Path.is_dir()` does NOT swallow EACCES.
`pathlib._IGNORED_ERRNOS` is ENOENT/ENOTDIR/EBADF/ELOOP only. I wrote a
fallback probe for an "unreadable store reads as empty" path and mutation
testing showed it survived every mutation — it was dead code resting on the
opposite belief. Removed. `store.list_infos()` raises PermissionError from
the `is_dir()` guard when the parent is untraversable, and from `iterdir()`
when the store itself is unreadable; one branch covers both. Verified
against 3.11 with a real mode-000 parent.
